commits.subject: fix(macho): derive the runtime name of each Mach-O symbol (#7105)
commits.body:
fix(macho): derive the runtime name of each Mach-O symbol (#7105)

inspect_macho reported only the symbol-table spelling (`_main`), while
LLDB, dlsym and observe_native_calls use the runtime spelling (`main`).
Passing a static name as a breakpoint silently selected a different
function, so results from the two tools could not be joined by name.

Keep `name` as the exact symbol-table fact and add a derived
`runtime_name` to every export and import row, produced by one shared
Mach-O symbol-name owner. Managed P/Invoke verification now uses the
same owner instead of its own underscore stripping.

Fixes #5298

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(artifacts): admit raw UDRW disk images (#7106)
commits.body:
fix(artifacts): admit raw UDRW disk images (#7106)

* fix(artifacts): admit raw UDRW disk images

Raw (UDRW, UDTO) disk images have no UDIF koly trailer, so target
admission and root inventory both refused them as unsupported binaries.
Recognize disk images in one domain owner (koly trailer, GPT, Apple
partition map, MBR, or an unpartitioned HFS+/HFSX volume header) that
both boundaries consume.

hdiutil reports "has no checksum" for these images; the native reader
now treats that status line as an explicit absent checksum, records the
nonzero verify command, attaches read-only, and reports that integrity
was not verified. Checksum mismatches and unrecognized images are still
refused.

Positional range reads used by these probes now fill until end of file
so short host reads cannot hide a signature.

Fixes #5687

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(artifacts): read disk image signature windows at the recognizer

Target admission passed its first unfilled 4 KiB read to the raw-image
checks, so a short host read could hide a GPT, APM, MBR or HFS+
signature that inventory (which fills its prefix) still observed. The
recognizer now reads its own leading window through the caller's
filling positional read, and target admission fills its format-probe
prefix as well. The controlled short-read regression now covers target
admission alongside inventory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(mcp): advertise reduced array elements with Gemini-compatible item types (#7107)
commits.body:
fix(mcp): advertise reduced array elements with Gemini-compatible item types (#7107)

Reduced compact input schemas gave every array property an any-value item
schema, a six-member type list beside nested `items`. Gemini function
declarations accept `items` only beside the single `array` type, so every
request through a Gemini-backed client failed with
`properties[functions].items.items: field predicate failed: $type == Type.ARRAY`.

Reduced array properties now advertise the element types their canonical item
schemas accept. Unknown, tuple, and mixed array elements use the empty item
schema, and properties that may be arrays or another type list typed anyOf
branches. An inline `not: {}` keeps the empty schema. The compact catalog test
now rejects `items` beside a non-array type as well as untyped item unions.

Fixes #5201

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: perf(native): charge function matching for the copies it makes (#7108)
commits.body:
perf(native): charge function matching for the copies it makes (#7108)

* perf(native): charge matching for what it copies, not borrowed retained inventories

Native function matching deep-walked every retained list_procedures record
at about 2.8 KB per Ghidra-shaped row, although the session ledger lends
those immutable records without a copy, and charged each inventory's one
Evidence ID once per function. The report and Evidence copies of every
emitted member were not charged at all.

Charge each inventory row before parsing for the member it becomes,
including its report and Evidence copies, charge the shared inventory ID
once, and skip the walk only for borrowed immutable inventories and closure
records that matching never parses. Inline Evidence, bundle records and
selected observations keep their existing charges. Retained references now
fit about 22,000 rows per side instead of 10,000, and an oversized side is
refused before its rows are parsed.

Refs #6406

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(native): charge the envelope of borrowed matching inputs

Borrowed inventories skipped admission entirely, but matching copies their
limitations into the report and Evidence and digests their profile, so a
retained inventory with few rows and large limitations escaped the
allowance. Charge every envelope field and leave only the result payloads,
which row charging covers or matching never parses, uncharged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(lldb): keep the bridge's no-target proof through interruption (#7111)
commits.body:
fix(lldb): keep the bridge's no-target proof through interruption (#7111)

When cancellation or the deadline interrupted LLDB after it had published
its bridge result, the tracer never read that result, so an explicit
`target_process_created: false` (or `target_process_exit_observed: true`)
was lost. The run kept a `native-target:unknown` marker that no cleanup
retry could release, wedging the tracer for every later trace.

Read the published result once LLDB's process group is stopped, even for
an interrupted run, and apply the same target-gone proof in cleanup retry.
Cancellation or timeout stays the primary outcome; a created target, a
truncated result, or a missing PID alone stays unresolved.

Fixes #5385

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(javascript): bind defaulted and destructured Webpack factory roles (#7117)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): bind defaulted and destructured Webpack factory roles (#7117)

* fix(javascript): bind defaulted and destructured Webpack factory roles

A Webpack factory whose module parameter was defaulted (`e = {}`) or
destructured (`{exports: x}`) reported an exact empty export list with
complete coverage, because roles were taken only from plain identifiers.

Bind factory roles once, by position, in javascriptBundlerFactoryRoles.
Defaulted module/exports parameters keep their role (the convention always
supplies the argument), `{exports: alias}` binds the alias to
module.exports, and a repeated sloppy parameter name binds its last
argument. Other role patterns (rest, array, nested or computed keys, a
non-identifier loader) receive no role and count as an unknown finding,
so the file's analysis is partial instead of claiming no exports. The
export collector, the factory require name and the standalone bootstrap
externals all use these parsed roles.

Fixes #7113

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(javascript): keep factory receivers through unordered reads

A defaulted role parameter kept the unused default in the binding facts
passed to write ordering, so a receiver read inside a loop, nested block
or closure was unresolved and its export silently dropped while the
module stayed complete.

The role owner now removes defaults the calling convention never runs
before ordering. Separately, an export-shaped write through a role
binding whose read stays unordered now counts as an unknown finding
instead of being dropped, so an incomplete list is never reported as
complete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(javascript): treat never-run factory parameter defaults as dead code

Removing unused defaults from binding facts let writes inside a default
expression reach the export collector: `(e = {}, t = (() => {
e.exports.ghost = 1; })())` reported `ghost` although Webpack supplies
both arguments. Loader calls in such defaults also produced require
references and async chunk keys.

The role owner now records the default of every role parameter, any
binding pattern included, as never run. The export collector, the
async-chunk walk and the static source traversal skip those subtrees,
so they yield no exports, references or chunk keys. Defaults of later,
non-role parameters still run and are still reported.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(mcp): fit every advertised input schema within the 64 KiB client limit (#7119)
commits.body:
fix(mcp): fit every advertised input schema within the 64 KiB client limit (#7119)

* fix(mcp): fit every advertised input schema within the 64 KiB client limit

Claude Desktop drops a local connector tool whose compact-JSON input
schema exceeds 64 KiB. The full input profile advertised
compare_web_captures at 171,867 bytes and inspect_analysis_view at
71,632 bytes, because the self-contained projection inlines the
complete producer capture schemas once per side.

The full advertisement now fits the limit at its producing boundary.
A property whose schema repeats an earlier sibling's points at it, and
schemas below the deepest instance level that fits are summarized as
their types, size constraints and descriptions. Every rewrite widens the
advertisement through the existing relaxation rules for oneOf, not,
if/then/else, contains and unevaluated keywords, so canonical inputs
stay accepted and the canonical contract still validates every call.
Schemas within the limit are unchanged, and the compact profile is
still presented from the complete projection.

Numeric const and enum literals are also relaxed in the advertisement,
like boolean literals, since Gemini accepts only string enum members.

Fixes #4081

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(mcp): keep fitted input summaries widening and at the deepest fitting level

Array summaries took item types only from `items`, so a tuple such as
`{prefixItems: [{type: string}], items: {type: number}}` was advertised
as a number array that rejected `["a", 1]`. Item types now include tuple
positions from `prefixItems`, a draft-07 `items` array, and
`additionalItems`, and stay unconstrained when later elements are open.

A summary can also be longer than the schema it replaces (a nullable
array becomes an anyOf), so candidate size is not monotone in the
retained depth and stopping at the first overflow could skip a deeper
candidate that fits. A schema is now kept whole when its summary is not
smaller, and fitting searches from the deepest level down.

Property tests check that every summary accepts what its schema accepts
over every catalog input subschema and synthetic tuples, and that the
fitted schema is the deepest fitting candidate. The browser comparison
boundary test now expects a malformed `after` capture to be rejected
canonically, since `after` is advertised as the same schema as `before`;
the same malformation on `before` stays advertised-invalid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(javascript): evaluate each short-circuit left operand once (#7126)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): evaluate each short-circuit left operand once (#7126)

Logical branch selection evaluated the left operand to decide which
branches stay reachable, and value evaluation then evaluated the selected
left branch again. In a left-nested `a || b || c ...` chain every level
repeated that, so semantic analysis doubled per operand and a 24-operand
chain exhausted the per-source deadline.

The selection now carries the left operand's value with the branch, and
value evaluation reuses it. Provenance still walks the branch nodes.
Results are unchanged.

Fixes #7115

commits.subject: fix(mcp)!: return a compact binary_session status by default (#7127)
commits.body:
fix(mcp)!: return a compact binary_session status by default (#7127)

* fix(mcp)!: return a compact binary_session status by default

binary_session {} with no target open returned about 66 KB, most of it
provider rejection diagnostics and candidate capability sets that the
skill's recovery flow re-reads on every retry. 6.8.0 grew it by 21%
because the shared regex capability limitation began repeating setting
bounds and step-by-step recovery for every search operation of every
provider (#6099, #6267, #6301, #7049) and IDA gained that limitation for
its two search operations (#4862).

The regex limitation now states the effective deadline and heap, their
sources and where to change them; the deadline and heap errors keep the
full recovery. binary_session gains detail: summary (default) or
complete. The summary keeps open state, target identity, the binding,
route capabilities, run, activity and health status, each candidate's
availability and target-support status, code and reason, and every
tool's availability, reason, remediation and modes, and lists the
fields it leaves out in omitted_fields. Complete detail returns the
previous shape. The CLI capabilities and providers commands keep
complete provider facts through the same application projection.

BREAKING CHANGE: binary_session {} no longer returns
analysis_provider_candidates[].availability.diagnostics,
target_support.diagnostics or capabilities, or tool_availability group
surface, effects and annotations. Pass {"detail": "complete"} to get
them.

Fixes #7109

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(mcp): key binary_session output fields by detail

The output schema accepted detail: "complete" with summary candidates or
tool groups, and a summary without omitted_fields, so detail did not
tell callers which fields existed. Each session kind is now crossed
with a detail-specific shape: a summary requires omitted_fields and
summary-only candidates and tool groups; complete requires diagnostics,
candidate capabilities and static tool flags and forbids omitted_fields.
Both the canonical schema and the SDK-validated advertised schema reject
mismatched shapes.

The verifier helper accepts summary candidates only for a validated MCP
summary; CLI provider output still requires candidate capabilities.
Regex limitation tests check values, sources and setting names instead
of whole sentences.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(javascript): stop recording replaced slot values as store receivers (#7128)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): stop recording replaced slot values as store receivers (#7128)

Reference-store identity queries resolved the written target as a value,
so once a step consumed the written key the walk continued into the value
read from that slot and recorded it, and everything reachable from it, as
an object the store mutates. Every value stored into one local object at
unknown keys then received an entry for every such store, and each new
store re-queued every earlier one. Ambient-write indexing grew cubically
in the number of such stores.

Receiver queries now drop items whose projection no longer ends at the
written key. Stored-value selection has one owner, which the resolver and
the store fixpoint share. The fixpoint re-queues a dependent only when a
changed entry can reach it with a selection that its receiver query keeps.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(javascript): close member-path cycles through self stores (#7131)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): close member-path cycles through self stores (#7131)

A write below a slot that stores a value read from the same slot, such
as `s.c = s.c.p; s.c.i = 1` on a parameter, revisits the binding with
one more segment after the stored key on every turn. The cycle closure
only recognized segments added at the front of the path (`node =
node[key]`), so the work-list never terminated and exhausted the owned
worker heap (CodeMirror 5 `mode/stylus/stylus.js`).

Recognize a contiguous segment inserted after a stable base, check that
repeating it after that base can never be pruned, and escape through it
once, as the self-alias rule already does. Front insertions keep their
existing order and result.

Fixes #7130

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: revert(mcp): undo input schema fitting that broke main CI
commits.body:
revert(mcp): undo input schema fitting that broke main CI

This reverts commit 7336a566ace2f9d1412f78b0c56c2651b9b169cd (#7119).

After #7120 and the other merges of 2026-10-25 grew inspect_analysis_view's
complete input schema (71,762 bytes plus 3,003 bytes of examples), the 64 KiB
fitting from #7119 could no longer keep instance level 3 and fell back to
level 2. That summarized the inline Evidence source and the view selector
collections, so main CI failed in toolInputReferences, toolSchemaValidity,
analysisViewMcp, absoluteLocalPathSchema, javascriptFactsViewMcp and
godotPckMcp. #7119's own CI ran against bc143125e, before that growth.

Reverting restores the complete full-profile advertisement while the size
limit is redesigned against these contracts (#4081 stays open).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.body:
revert(mcp): undo input schema fitting that broke main CI (#7135)

This reverts commit 7336a566ace2f9d1412f78b0c56c2651b9b169cd (#7119).

After #7120 and the other merges of 2026-10-25 grew inspect_analysis_view's
complete input schema (71,762 bytes plus 3,003 bytes of examples), the 64 KiB
fitting from #7119 could no longer keep instance level 3 and fell back to
level 2. That summarized the inline Evidence source and the view selector
collections, so main CI failed in toolInputReferences, toolSchemaValidity,
analysisViewMcp, absoluteLocalPathSchema, javascriptFactsViewMcp and
godotPckMcp. #7119's own CI ran against bc143125e, before that growth.

Reverting restores the complete full-profile advertisement while the size
limit is redesigned against these contracts (#4081 stays open).

commits.subject: fix(cli): reject non-decimal Android overload index tokens (#7493)
commits.body:
fix(cli): reject non-decimal Android overload index tokens (#7493)

Android overload selection declared a plain number, so the CLI argument
parser coerced the raw token with Number before the schema ran. An empty
token therefore arrived as 0, and hexadecimal, exponent, signed, and
float spellings arrived as their numeric value, leaving both commands to
proceed to artifact admission on a selector the caller never wrote as a
decimal integer.

Reuse the existing decimal token parser that the other integer CLI
options already use. Omitted and explicit decimal zero keep their current
meanings, and the published schema for overloadIndex is unchanged.

Validation: npm run compile, the cli-boundary vitest project for
tests/boundary/cli/cliIntegerArguments.test.ts (56 passed), npm run
typecheck, npm run lint, npm run lint:typed, npm run format:check, npm
run metadata:check, npm run verify:architecture-guards, and npm run
knip:production. The new cases fail against the base source and pass with
the change.

Fixes #7430.

commits.subject: feat(environment): serve the writes that later reads explain (#7274)
commits.body:
feat(environment): serve the writes that later reads explain (#7274)

* feat(environment): serve the writes callers make without recorded form fields

- A create member a recording sent empty ("", null, false, [] or {}) is no
  longer required; a call that leaves it out is applied as sending that value
  (body.blank).
- List views render envelope members that list the listed entities' ids
  (Paperless's `all`), so creates in such collections are confirmed.
- Updates move their entity in collections kept sorted by a field they write,
  and a failed whole-collection read after an update can teach that order.
- A later create that stores an unruled field otherwise is withheld at the
  create, and an item read may fill values a create's answer had not loaded.
- An unsent field respelled between null, [] and {} is unchanged.
- The skill asks for one create with every field and one with only what a
  person must give.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(skill): show how to read signed-in pages before recording

Agents guessed capture keys (artifacts, dom, final) to see pages behind
sign-in, which inspect_web_page cannot reach.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): accept every empty spelling recorded creates sent

A create that fills only what a person must give sends `null` where the
full create sent a string, and `null` or `false` for the same flag. The
merged plan now accepts each recorded empty value, and a call that leaves
the member out is applied as the earliest call sent it.

Also adds the spec folder for this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(skill): keep the vary-fields step neutral on UI or API writes

Agents read "the form" as a cue to write through the UI, where some
applications' request bodies are not exposed; a body-unusable UI write
now re-records once with request steps.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record verification for blank members and sorted writes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): address review of blank members and sorted writes

- Bulk updates move their entities in turn against the others' earlier
  values and install the final order once, as replay does.
- A member's recorded empty values stay accepted once a later call teaches
  its default; a left-out member with a default keeps the default.
- Write answers spell empty lists and maps as their recorded answers did.
- A rename can teach a sort when the creates chose one by a field the
  update did not write, such as ids that ascend with titles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(environment): serve the writes that later reads explain

- An item read whose object is marked deleted (deleted, isDeleted or
  is_deleted true) agrees with an absent entity, as EspoCRM answers a
  deleted record; such an object never seeds or adopts an entity.
- maxSize, max_results and maxResults are page sizes, for whole-collection
  list lines and the list query's limit role.
- An item view also shows the fields only reads after its type's first write
  show, when no initial entity holds them (Vikunja's task subscription),
  without requiring them; write answers leave such a field out for entities
  without it, and it no longer withholds the write as incomplete-entities.
- The skill asks updates to change the fields a person would change, and
  expects a deleted object to read back as 404 or marked deleted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): answer sent empty members as sent, and keep a placed create's order

- A write answer spells an empty list or map the call did not send as its
  recorded answer did; one the call sent is answered as sent, so a create
  sending `[]` is not answered `null` because the first recorded create was.
- A read listing the whole collection that placed a create leaves the create
  only the sorted inserts whose order that read follows, so a later rename
  cannot teach a sort an earlier read ruled out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): answer bulk updates without fields only later reads show

A bulk update's answer renders each entity with the same allowance a single
update's answer has: a field only reads after the type's first write showed,
which no initial entity holds, is left out for an entity without it, so a
bulk update of a seeded task is no longer refused for lacking it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): correct how the EspoCRM contact update task passes

The agent trajectories show gpt-oss passes it by creating a replacement contact
and deleting the original, since the served update refuses emailAddress; the
update itself is refused in both builds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): answer a read of a served-deleted entity marked deleted

An application that soft-deletes still answers a deleted record by id, marked
deleted. Serving now keeps an entity a served delete removed from a type whose
recorded item reads show that, until a reset or load and within the size
data/add loads, and answers a read of it with its last fields and the flag
true, instead of refusing the read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): keep unloaded create answers, check bulk answers with sent members, narrow inserts only on collection-order reads

- A create whose item read loaded values its answer had not records them
  (`observation.read.unloaded`), and a served create's answer keeps them as
  the recorded answer showed them, a zero-time owner included, while the state
  holds the read's.
- Replay checks a bulk update's recorded answers with each target's sent
  members, as serving answers them, so echoed `null` and `[]` no longer make
  the plan body-unusable.
- A whole-collection read whose query sorts it shows the query's order, so it
  no longer narrows a create's sorted insert candidates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(environment): record the census with main's unknown-clock rule merged

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): learn a sort from a rename only when moving its entities reaches it

Serving moves only the entities a write changes in a collection kept sorted,
so replay now tries a sort after a rename only when the entities no write the
read exercised changed already follow it. Seeded folders listed out of title
order no longer teach a title sort that serving would answer with another

fix(browser): save from gzip, deflate and cached responses within a bound (#7361)

A saved response's decoded size is bounded by its received size, or the
declared length of one served from cache, times 1032 for each gzip or deflate
coding, the most DEFLATE expands. Grafana answers folder creates gzipped, so a
UI step saving a new folder's uid was refused. Other codings and unknown or
zero sizes stay refused before the body is read.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): test literals for Next page paths in linear time (#7748)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): test literals for Next page paths in linear time (#7748)

Every source string literal without an established Next root was tested
against /(?:^|\/)app\/(?:[\s\S]*\/)?page(?:\.[cm]?[jt]sx?|-[^/?#]+\.js|)(?:[?#].*)?$/u.
The unanchored search restarted at every app/ segment and rescanned to the
end of the literal, and each page? or page# candidate scanned to the next
line terminator before $ failed. A long literal therefore took quadratic
time on the analysis thread: about 6 s for a 256 KB literal of repeated
app/ segments, and 3.5 s for 224 KB of x/page? followed by a newline.

The first app/ segment admits every later page segment, and . cannot cross
a line terminator, so a query or fragment after the page filename starts on
the last line. Test the tail after the first app/ segment one page segment
at a time instead; results are unchanged.

commits.subject: fix(apktool): read Apktool 2.9+ metadata in its line-oriented dialect (#7747)
commits.body:
fix(apktool): read Apktool 2.9+ metadata in its line-oriented dialect (#7747)

Apktool 2.9.0 replaced SnakeYAML with the YamlWriter that 3.x still uses:
apktool.yml starts with an untagged `version: 2.x.y` line and strings are
written unquoted with Java-style escapes. Only a `version: 3.x.y` header
selected the producer dialect, so 2.9.0-2.12.x output went through YAML
core parsing: a versionName of `1.0 #beta` became `1.0`, escaped quotes kept
their backslashes, an empty name became null, and `1.0: beta` made the whole
decode fail as invalid metadata.

Select the line-oriented reader for 2.9.0 and later as well. Older tagged
SnakeYAML documents keep YAML scalar semantics.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): resolve Vite build-output preload dependencies (#7745)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): resolve Vite build-output preload dependencies (#7745)

* fix(javascript): resolve Vite build-output preload dependencies

With an absolute base, Vite writes __vite__mapDeps entries relative to the
build output directory (for example assets/chunk.js), and its preload helper
prefixes the configured base at runtime. REA emitted these entries as
dynamic-import module specifiers, so a scheme-less path without a leading
dot resolved as a bare package and every entry was reported as an
unresolved "external" module, even when the build output directory was
selected.

The static analyzer now marks such entries with a vite-output: specifier,
as Webpack chunk loads are marked with chunk:. Entries starting with ./,
../ or /, and scheme-qualified entries, keep their previous handling. The
graph resolves a marked entry as a URL path under each ancestor directory
of the importing file; exactly one ancestor holding the file establishes
the build output directory. Otherwise the entry is not-found (or
unavailable when several ancestors match) with a limitation that names
the build output directory.

On a synthetic 7-file Vite build, the 12 preload entries that were
"external" now resolve when the build output directory is selected, and
are not-found with that guidance when only assets/ is selected.

* fix(javascript): keep unanalyzed Vite output candidates

resolveViteOutputDependency considered only resolved ancestors. A file
that exists under an ancestor but was not analyzed (for example
dist/assets/lazy.css for the entry assets/lazy.css) resolves there as
unavailable, and that result was replaced by the root's not-found with a
limitation saying that no ancestor holds the file.

Keep resolved and unavailable ancestor candidates together. One candidate
is returned with its own path and limitations; several are reported as
unavailable with every candidate path and limitation. Only when no
ancestor can hold the file does the root's not-found result stand.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): stop double-expanding application projection estimates (#7744)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): stop double-expanding application projection estimates (#7744)

* fix(javascript): stop double-expanding application projection estimates

estimateJavaScriptStaticApplicationProjection multiplied the per-record
metadata allowance (2 KB plus the path) by the 8x expansion that it also
applies to checkpoint bytes. A projected record serializes to about 0.46 KB,
so the allowance alone already covers retention; expanded again, the
charge was about 25x the serialized application relationships.

The charge accumulates in the parent's shared result budget. On a
synthetic 2.8 MB Vite-style build (88 files, one 456 KB chunk), the first
10 files used 2.0 GB of a 2.08 GB budget while the parent heap held about
300 MiB. The other 78 files lost their application relationships and were
offered a 0-byte semantic budget. On a 201-file build the charges exceeded
the budget at file 93 and the analysis failed with resource_constraint,
leaving the remaining sources without static facts.

Keep the 8x expansion for checkpoint and repeated bytes and count the
per-record allowance once. The same builds now refuse 14 and 102
projections instead of 78 and a failed run; peak RSS stays at 1.2 GB and
2.0 GB under a 4.2 GB parent heap limit.

workerFailureComposition simulated 64 KiB of parent result budget, which
the corrected charge for its one-finding checkpoint fits. Lower that
headroom to 32 KiB so the case still exercises a refused projection.

* test(javascript): cover application projections near the shared parent budget

The estimate test compares one file's charge with its serialized graph,
but no test put several sources against one parent result budget. Replay
one recorded static checkpoint for five sources against an exact budget:
sources 1-3 fit, source 4 misses by half a source and keeps its static
facts with the reported required and budget bytes, and the last source
fits again once no checkpoint reserve is held back. A worker that charges
the projection twice, or not at all, passes the existing tests and fails
this one.

* test(javascript): cover a malformed source before a valid one under the shared budget

The testing guide asks representation-expansion and capacity changes for
a large malformed input followed by a valid input, and for escaped or
expanded representations.

Under an exact parent budget, a 3 MiB checkpoint cut off inside a string
comes first and is rejected as unreadable output with no static facts.
The valid source after it keeps its application relationships; it fits
only if the rejected bytes took no charge. A worker that charges the
static checkpoint on receipt, before parsing, passes the existing tests
and fails this one.

The estimate ratio test also runs with a nested source path and storage
keys holding quotes, backslashes, a tab and multibyte text, which expand
in serialized JSON; the charge stays within 3x to 8x of the serialized
application graph (5.3x).

commits.subject: fix(javascript): keep both-direction feature traces from crossing shared containers (#7743)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): keep both-direction feature traces from crossing shared containers (#7743)

* fix(javascript): keep both-direction feature traces from crossing shared containers

trace_application_feature with direction "both" walked the application
graph as if it were undirected. From a seed, one outgoing or incoming step
into a shared container (an asset or the artifact root) followed by steps
in the other direction reached every sibling of that container, so a trace
seeded on one storage key returned the whole connected graph.

"both" now returns the union of the outgoing and incoming closures. Each
walk keeps its own predecessor chains, so a terminal path never changes
direction midway. "outgoing" and "incoming" are unchanged.

* test(javascript): check both-direction trace paths end to end

The existing tests checked predecessor maps but no returned path. Add a
trace whose seed reaches one storage terminal outgoing and another
incoming, and assert each path's complete node_ids and edge_ids. A
pathTo that reads only the first walk's map returns a one-node path for
the incoming terminal and fails this test.

* fix(javascript): confine only ascended containers in both-direction traces

Making "both" the union of separate outgoing and incoming walks dropped
modules that a feature reaches by crossing directions. In the Notes
known-answer evaluation, the notes:export channel is pointed at by both
the preload asset (invokes) and the handler (handles); its preload,
renderer and csv modules are reached only through relationships that
change direction, so the trace kept main.js alone and the feature_modules
claim failed in tests/boundary/mcp/agentKnownAnswerMcp.test.ts.

Walk both directions in one traversal again, and confine only the
containment case the change was meant to stop: a node reached by stepping
up a contains edge from one of its children follows only further contains
steps up. A shared asset or artifact root then no longer leads into its
other children, while relationships across the feature are kept. The
Notes trace returns csv.js, main.js, preload.js and renderer.js again
(30 nodes; the previous main returned the whole 32-node graph).
outgoing and incoming traces are unchanged, and paths come from one
predecessor map again, as before this branch.

commits.subject: feat(artifacts): inventory and extract ESP32 firmware images (#7498)
commits.body:
feat(artifacts): inventory and extract ESP32 firmware images (#7498)

* feat(artifacts): inventory and extract ESP32 firmware images

ESP32-family app and bootloader images (magic 0xE9) had no reader, so
open_binary refused OTA downloads, app partitions and bootloaders.

Add the esp-image container format behind inspect_artifact and
extract_artifact. A pure decoder reads each byte once and keeps only
fixed-size fields. Derived facts cover the chip, from a table cited to
ESP-IDF v6.1; segment classification as ESP-IDF's should_map and
should_load; checksum and appended SHA-256 results; app and bootloader
descriptors; Secure Boot v2 signature blocks, observed and unverified;
and undescribed trailing byte ranges. Truncation and undescribed bytes
make coverage unknown. ESP8266 images are refused with a specific
reason, and ciphertext stays unrecognized.

Add the format to every target, Evidence, snapshot, live-summary and
artifact vocabulary, document it, and add an optional verify:esp-images
lane that compares esptool-built images with esptool image-info and
espsecure signature-info-v2.

Refs #3615

* test(artifacts): run the ESP image lane on esptool v5.6.0

The lane compared descriptor fields only when esptool image-info printed
one, so a descriptor that REA reports and esptool does not print passed
without comparison. Compare the descriptor kind in both directions.

Record that the lane passed for all 13 images with esptool and espsecure
v5.6.0, the version the layout facts cite, as well as with 4.12.0.

* refactor(artifacts): define ESP image layout sizes once

The decoder and the derived facts each defined the segment-header,
appended-digest and flash-sector sizes, the erased-byte scan and the
offset formatter. Define them once with the other fixed-layout structures
and import them in both places. The signature slot count is the one
constant that drives the slot scan.

Correct the observedEnd comment: it is the end of the last chunk read.

* fix(artifacts): report ESP-IDF's segment length limit by chip

ESP-IDF's verify_segment_header rejects a segment of 16 MiB or more
unless the chip maps flash through 32-bit cache addresses
(SOC_SPI_MEM_SUPPORT_CACHE_32BIT_ADDR_MAP: ESP32-S3, P4, C5, C61, H4 and
S31 in v6.1). Record that capability in the chip table and add a
limitation for such segments; unknown chips get none.

`loaded` repeats should_load. It does not mean the bootloader accepts the
segment: verify_load_addresses still rejects one outside the chip's RAM,
which REA does not model. Say so in the docs, the skill reference and the
inventory limitation.

* test(artifacts): check ESP lane tools first and verify extraction

The lane started work before checking its tools, so a missing RISC-V
target, ld.lld, esptool or espsecure surfaced as a raw spawn or command
error. Check each one before building and name the variable to set. Warn
when esptool is not v5.6.0, the release the layout facts cite.

Assert each segment's class for the ESP32-C3 app, its variants and the
bootloader, as the Xtensa image already did. Extract the app and the
signed image through the CLI and compare every file with the bytes at
esptool's segment offsets or in the appended signature sector; the
source's SHA-256 must be unchanged and equal the reported root_sha256.

* docs(artifacts): state what the ESP image lane does not establish

The Verification section listed the lane's checks but not its gaps: only
ESP32-C3 and ESP32 images come from a real producer, no real project
build, OTA download or flash dump is inspected, no signature is verified,
and the lane does not run in CI.

Record the timing of the final lane run on esptool v5.6.0.

* fix(artifacts): compare ESP segment declarations

Segment entries hash only their data, so compare_artifacts reported a
segment that moved to another load address with the same bytes as
unchanged; only the image itself changed. Compare each segment's
load_addr and data_len as its declaration, as Node SEA and PyInstaller
members are compared, and count a changed declaration as a metadata
change, also when content is unavailable.

Header offsets are layout and the classification is derived, so neither
is compared.

* test(artifacts): run ESP lane commands as owned process trees

The lane ran its tools through execFile. A timeout killed only the direct
child, so a linker or assembler that Clang or GCC had started could keep
running while the lane removed its workspace. Run every command through
createVerifierCommands, check the tools inside withVerifierCleanup, and
remove the workspace only after commands.close() has stopped every tree;
a failed close keeps the workspace.

Only a nonzero exit now counts as a refusal or an expected esptool
failure; timeouts and spawn failures propagate. Supervising each command
roughly doubles the lane's run time.

* test(artifacts): cancel ESP decoding after its first decoded chunk

The cancellation test requested cancel or close on setImmediate, which
can land while the file is still being opened and checked, so it never
showed that decoding had started. It also passed against a reader that
ignored both requests while decoding. Acknowledge the decoder's first
chunk, then cancel or close, join the operation, and assert that no
later chunk reaches the decoder and that the reader ends closed.

* docs(artifacts): record which ESP metadata comparison ignores

Segments are compared by their declaration. The image's and the
signature blocks' format_metadata are not: every field comes from their
own bytes, which content comparison already covers, and a block's
image_digest_matches follows the image's content.

* docs(artifacts): state that ESP mmu_page_size is a base-2 logarithm

The app descriptor's mmu_page_size keeps ESP-IDF's name and value, the
MMU page size in log base 2 as esp_app_desc_t declares it, so 16 means
64 KiB. Say so in docs/esp-image.md and the schema comment; a reader
could otherwise take 16 as 16 KiB.

* fix(esp-image): retain member consumption and share lifecycle regressions

* test(artifacts): scope MCP catalogs and budget full-schema validation

* test(artifacts): verify compact output profiles and document bounded catalogs

* test(artifacts): close readers when cleanup-test admission fails

* test(artifacts): compare ESP image limitations with their owners

The decoder and reader tests froze complete limitation sentences, so a
harmless rewording failed them. The wording now has two owners:
ESP_IMAGE_LIMITATIONS in espImageFacts.ts, which the decoder, the inventory
and the reader use, and ESP_DESCRIPTOR_LIMITATIONS beside the descriptor
decoder. Tests compare delivered limitations with the owner, called with the
facts each case establishes (segment index, declared and available bytes,
offsets, chip, page range), next to the structured assertions they already
make. Delivered text is unchanged.

* test(esp-image): assert structured facts and owned guidance

* fix(esp-image): keep spi_flash_mode and descriptor fields before a truncated tail

ESP-IDF v6.1's esp_app_desc_t declares spi_flash_mode at byte 181, after
mmu_page_size, as the committed reference layout shows; the descriptor now
keeps it as stored. The decoder also required all 256 descriptor bytes,
though it reads none past byte 181, so a file ending in the reserved tail
lost the version, project, digest and revision facts it does hold. The app
descriptor now needs only its fields; the segment's truncation is reported
as before.

* test(esp-image): pin the P-192 public key digest to espsecure's layout

espsecure packs ECDSA signature blocks as "<BBBx32sB64s64s1031x" and
zero-pads a 48-byte P-192 point to 64 bytes, so the signature starts at
byte 101 for every SHA-256 curve. signature_info_v2 hashes sig_block[36:101]
and _digest_sbv2_public_key the curve ID with the padded point. No test built
a P-192 block; this one checks public_key_sha256 against that definition.

* fix(esp-image): keep each app descriptor field the file holds in full

A file can end anywhere inside the 256-byte esp_app_desc_t. The decoder
needed every field byte, so a cut at byte 176 dropped the version, project
and app_elf_sha256 it does hold. Once the 4-byte magic identifies an app
descriptor, each field is now kept when the file holds all of its bytes and
is null otherwise; observed_length records where the descriptor ends, so a
cut field is told apart from text that is not UTF-8. The fields after the
magic become nullable in the metadata schema.

* fix(esp-image): report a signature block whose image digest does not match

A CRC-valid Secure Boot v2 block can carry another image's digest. The
block recorded image_digest_matches false, but no limitation said so, unlike
a checksum or appended-SHA mismatch, so CLI and MCP summaries showed only
the generic unverified note. The mismatch is now a limitation; coverage
stays complete and signature_status stays unverified. The three other
signature-sector limitations move into ESP_IMAGE_LIMITATIONS with their
text unchanged, so all ESP image wording has one owner.

* refactor(esp-image): remove redundant descriptor byte guards

commits.subject: fix(artifacts): split U-Boot script uImages on their size table (#7805)
commits.body:
fix(artifacts): split U-Boot script uImages on their size table (#7805)

U-Boot's mkimage writes the multi-file size table for script images
(`mkimage -T script`, the boot.scr format) exactly as it does for multi
images, `mkimage -l` lists the script as "Image 0", and the `source`
command skips the table before running the script ("scripts are just
multi-image files with one component", boot/image-board.c).

The uImage reader parsed the table only for IH_TYPE_MULTI, so a script
image reported sub_image_count 0 and exposed only payload.bin, whose
first bytes are the binary size table rather than the script text.

Treat IH_TYPE_SCRIPT like IH_TYPE_MULTI: parse the same bounded table,
expose image-<n>.bin components and report the size-table limitation.
payload.bin is unchanged. A script payload without a valid table now
fails closed, as a multi image already does.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): read the spawn env option as Node reads it (#7713)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): read the spawn env option as Node reads it (#7713)

* fix(javascript): read spawn env as Node reads it

Node's normalizeSpawnArguments starts with `const env = options.env ||
{ ...process.env }`, so a falsy env is replaced by a copy of the parent
environment. A child started with env: null, undefined, 0, "" or false
therefore inherits everything, exactly as if no env were passed.

REA tested the key's presence alone, so every one of those reported
environment_supplied: true and the graph emitted a resolved supplies-env
relation. The presence test also missed the opposite direction: an env
supplied through an inline object spread reported false although Node uses
it.

Read the declared value the way stdioMode already reads stdio: an explicit
property whose statically known value is falsy does not supply an
environment, and an inline spread that carries env does.

Verified on Node v24.22.1 with a child that prints a parent marker variable:
no options, env: null, undefined, void 0, 0, "" and false all print the
marker, while env: {} prints nothing and env: { A: "1" } prints only that.

* fix(javascript): read falsy numeric literals as Node does

greptile flagged that environmentSupplied still reported a supplied environment for
`env: -0` and `env: 0n`: staticJavaScriptTruthiness recognized neither form, so it
returned undefined and `!== false` turned that into true. Node's
normalizeSpawnArguments uses `options.env || { ...process.env }`, so both inherit.

Extend the shared truthiness reader to cover a BigInt literal and a negated numeric
literal, and add regression cases for `-0`, `0n` and `0.0`.

The reader is shared with the route scan and the state tracker; both treat
`undefined` as "unknown", so a more precise `false` only strengthens them.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): match resource release methods to the acquired handle (#7773)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): match resource release methods to the acquired handle (#7773)

* fix(javascript): match resource release methods to the acquired handle

Every acquisition family admitted every release method, so `h.close()`,
`h.destroy()` and `h.end()` each resolved as a complete release of whatever the
binding held. Node exposes a different subset per acquisition, and the rejected
pairs throw at the call site instead.

Measured on Node 24.22.1:

| acquisition | value | release members |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fs.openSync` | number | none |
| `fs.open` (callback) | undefined | none |
| `fs.createReadStream` | ReadStream | `close`, `destroy` (`end` is the byte-offset field) |
| `fs.createWriteStream` | WriteStream | `close`, `destroy`, `end` |
| `fs/promises.open` | FileHandle | `close` |
| `net.connect` | Socket | `destroy`, `end` |
| `tls.connect` | TLSSocket | `destroy`, `end` |

So `fs.openSync(...)` + `fd.close()`, `createReadStream(...)` + `.end()`,
`net.connect(...)` + `.close()` and the FileHandle cases emitted a `releases` /
`resolved` fact for a call that throws.

Carry the specifier with each acquisition candidate, list the release methods
each pair actually has, and emit no release when the pair is not one of them. A
release stays `complete` only when the binding held exactly one acquisition and
that acquisition admitted the method.

`tls.createConnection` is not a Node export at all: `'createConnection' in
require('node:tls')` is false and the ESM import does not link. Drop it from the
table so a `tls.createConnection` call yields no acquisition.

* chore: retrigger title and readiness checks after the title was corrected

* fix(javascript): cover a mixed-family binding before completing a release

greptile asked for the mixed-family case: a binding that can hold either a
FileHandle or a socket, then calls close(). The FileHandle is the only linked
acquisition and the release stays partial.

That case also showed the `candidates.length === 1` guard was dead: an
acquisition of another family is not in `linked`, so `holdsOnlyAcquisitions`
already returns false for it and the release already stayed partial without the
guard. Removing the guard and keeping the test means the behaviour is now pinned
by a test rather than by two overlapping conditions.

commits.subject: test(firmware): pin the staging ceiling at the request boundary (#7775)
commits.body:
test(firmware): pin the staging ceiling at the request boundary (#7775)

* test(firmware): exercise the staging ceiling through the emitted refusal

The ceiling recovery added in #6971 was covered through the wording helper only, so a wiring change that passed the schema ceiling where the selected value belongs, or that dropped the remediation, would have stayed green.

Adds boundary coverage that calls inventoryFirmwareOutput itself: a sparse file reaches the real byte ceiling without storing the bytes and asserts the projected refusal carries the ceiling recovery, and a one-byte tree below the ceiling asserts the raise advice. Verified red on both regressions — passing the schema ceiling for the selected value fails the below-ceiling case, and restoring the single-form remediation fails both.

* test(firmware): compare the emitted recovery with its owner

The wiring test matched three phrases of the emitted remediation, so an ad-hoc or truncated action that kept those phrases would still pass while the emitted recovery had diverged from firmwareStagingBudgetRemediation.

Assert exact equality with the owner's output for the selected value in both cases instead. Verified red: replacing the emitted action with a divergent sentence that keeps the ceiling phrases now fails both cases, where the phrase matching passed.

* chore: retrigger title and readiness checks after the title was corrected

* test(firmware): drive the staging ceiling through the request boundary

greptile and codex both flagged that the ceiling tests called
inventoryFirmwareOutput directly, so they would still pass if request parsing or
the provider wiring dropped or replaced max_output_bytes.

Add a request-level test that records the parsed request a provider receives:
the caller's max_output_bytes arrives unchanged at the schema ceiling and below
it, the documented default applies when omitted, and a budget above the schema
maximum is rejected before the provider runs. That is the wiring the previous
tests assumed rather than asserted.

commits.subject: feat(artifacts): inventory and extract U-Boot FIT images (#7771)
commits.body:
feat(artifacts): inventory and extract U-Boot FIT images (#7771)

* feat(artifacts): inventory and extract U-Boot FIT images

open_binary refused U-Boot Flattened Image Tree files as an unsupported
format, so inspect_artifact and extract_artifact could not list or
recover a FIT's kernel, devicetree, ramdisk and loadable images.

Recognize an FDT v16/v17 with a top-level /images node and parse it with
the existing parseDevicetree. Each /images child becomes an inventory
entry named images/<unit-name>.bin that extracts its stored bytes from
embedded data, data-offset (past the 4-aligned devicetree end) or
data-position (from the file start). Image format_metadata records the
declared type, arch, os, compression, load and entry; root metadata
records the description, timestamp and configurations.

crc32, md5, sha1, sha256, sha384 and sha512 hash nodes are verified in
one streamed pass per image; other algorithms are reported unverified.
Signatures are reported, not verified, and nothing is decompressed,
decrypted or executed. Data outside the file, overlapping or duplicate
image data, a missing or repeated data source and hash mismatches fail
closed. The devicetree is bounded by the fixed 16 MiB allowance;
external image data is streamed from disk.

Refs #7129

commits.subject: fix(javascript): emit no fork when a literal stdio array omits the IPC channel (#7992)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): emit no fork when a literal stdio array omits the IPC channel (#7992)

* fix(javascript): emit no fork when a literal stdio array omits the IPC channel

Node's fork() requires an explicit stdio array to carry the IPC channel:

    if (!ArrayPrototypeIncludes(options.stdio, 'ipc'))
      throw new ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_IPC_REQUIRED('options.stdio')

The throw is synchronous, before any child process exists, but the analysis
reported a resolved fork with stdioMode "array" — byte-identical to the valid
`[..., "ipc"]` form — which projects to a child-process node, a resolved spawns
relation and resolved connects-stdio.

Measured on Node 24.22.1:

    fork({stdio: ["inherit","inherit","inherit"]}) -> THROWS ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_IPC_REQUIRED
    fork({stdio: ["pipe","pipe","pipe"]})          -> THROWS ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_IPC_REQUIRED
    fork({stdio: ["ipc"]})                         -> SPAWNED connected=true
    fork({stdio: ["inherit","inherit","inherit","ipc"]}) -> SPAWNED connected=true
    fork({stdio: "pipe"})                          -> SPAWNED connected=true
    spawn({stdio: ["inherit","inherit","inherit"]})-> SPAWNED connected=false

A string stdio is normalised with "ipc" appended, so only the array form can omit
it. The same array is valid for spawn, which has no IPC requirement.

Drop a fork candidate only when its stdio array is fully literal and provably
lacks "ipc"; a spread or a non-literal element may still supply the channel and
stays a candidate.

fix(artifacts): name every U-Boot uImage type in the pinned image.h (#8007)

TYPE_NAMES stopped at flat_dt (8), while the U-Boot include/image.h
commit that the tables are pinned to defines image types 0-47. A header
declaring a later type, such as kernel_noload (14) or tfa-bl31 (45),
was reported with type_name "unknown".

Add types 9-47 with their mkimage -T short names from boot/image.c at
the same commit. IH_TYPE_LOADABLE (22) has no short name there and is
named "loadable", as other tables already name identifiers U-Boot does
not list. Identifiers past the enum stay "unknown".

commits.subject: fix(native): explain categories whose class reference names no class (#8006)
commits.body:
fix(native): explain categories whose class reference names no class (#8006)

An Objective-C category whose class field is null, or is bound to a
symbol other than `_OBJC_CLASS_$_`, was recorded as partial with
`category_class_unresolved`, but no issue was raised, so the
`objc_properties_categories` coverage facet reported `partial` with a
null reason. swiftc emits such categories for @objc members of an
extension on another module's Swift class and binds the class field to
the class metadata symbol (`_$s…CN`); Keynote and Notability carry them.

Report the reference as a `category_class_unresolved` issue naming the
bound symbol, or stating that the reference is null, matching the issue
already raised for an unreadable local class reference.

* feat(environment): serve the writes callers make without recorded form fields

  longer required; a call that leaves it out is applied as sending that value
  (body.blank).

  (Paperless's `all`), so creates in such collections are confirmed.

  and a failed whole-collection read after an update can teach that order.
- A later create that stores an unruled field otherwise is withheld at the
  create, and an item read may fill values a create's answer had not loaded.

  person must give.

commits.subject: feat(macho): report per-slice encryption status in inspect_macho (#5359)
commits.body:
feat(macho): report per-slice encryption status in inspect_macho (#5359)

* refactor(macho): extract non-throwing container and slice load-command readers

Split readMachoImage into readMachoContainer, which classifies a file as
thin, FAT or not Mach-O and keeps FAT range issues per slice, and
readSliceLoadCommands, which reads one slice header and frames its load
commands, returning every command framed before a failure.

readMachoImage keeps its strict policy on top of them: commands framed
before a framing defect still decode first, an unsupported FAT slice
still yields to a later malformed one, and the first FAT range issue is
still reported. A characterization test pins that precedence for inputs
with several defects; it passes against both the previous and the new
implementation.

Part of #4306.

* feat(macho): report per-slice encryption status in inspect_macho

inspect_macho now reports the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO(_64) state of every
slice in a new `encryption` collection, read in process from load
commands without reading code bytes.

- Each slice is encrypted, not-encrypted, absent, malformed or unknown.
  Absent requires a completed load-command walk; malformed and unknown
  carry a reason and keep commands read before the failure.
- The named range is end-exclusive in slice and input-file coordinates
  and maps to file-backed segment fragments, VM addresses and the
  overlapping nonempty sections.
- A ciphertext range adds a limitation naming its input-file bytes.
- The in-process read and the native tools are bracketed by one regular
  file descriptor and stat identity checks; a change reports
  artifact_changed. A missing or inaccessible target keeps the tool
  facts and reports encryption as non-exhaustive, never absent.
- Retained Evidence recorded before this field is parsed by the owning
  schema and reports encryption as unknown in the macho view and in
  managed/native verification.

Fixes #4306

* fix(macho): keep slice facts and failures under large tables and close errors

- Frame load commands through a visitor instead of retaining every
  command, restoring the pre-refactor memory profile (2M eight-byte
  commands: peak heap 370 MiB -> 0.9 MiB).
- Confirm a large FAT container from a valid slice's Mach-O header so a
  sibling's range fault stays per slice instead of hiding healthy slices.
- Name only sections whose bytes the range and their segment both cover.
- Throw inspection failures inside the owned descriptor callback so a
  close failure keeps them as its primary error.

* fix(macho): map encrypted ranges only within segment VM extents

mapRange gave every file-backed segment fragment VM addresses, even for a
segment with no VM size, whose file bytes dyld never maps, and past vmsize
when a segment declared more file bytes than memory.

Read vmsize with the segment. A segment with no VM size keeps its fragment
with null VM addresses. A file size beyond the VM size, or a VM range past
the address space, makes the mapping unknown with a reason while the slice
keeps its encryption status.

The docs also claimed the encryption read never reads code bytes. Like
every Mach-O container read, a 0xcafebabe input of at most 16 MiB is read
whole to rule out a JVM class file; say so.

* fix(macho): read encryption through the admitted descriptor facts

Main's withArtifactRegularFile now hands callers the admitted handle and
its initial stats. Use those facts instead of re-stating the handle, and
pass the legacy Evidence payload straight to createEvidence.

* fix(macho): retain a finished report when the target close fails

The file owner keeps the completed callback value when the descriptor close
fails or cancellation arrives during close. inspect_macho now validates that
value and retains the report as the error's partial observation, as
inspect_signature does, instead of returning only the cleanup or
cancellation error.

* test(native): supply readEncryption in merged dyld refusal cases

main's new dyld refusal cases build NativeMachoInspectionContext without
the encryption reader this branch requires.

* test(views): bind the Mach-O encryption page to its facet

main's facet-ownership case builds inspect_macho Evidence without the
encryption coverage this branch requires; the fixture now carries one
slice row and the loop checks the encryption page like the other facets.

* fix(macho): bound encryption commands and range mapping across slices

A slice retains at most two encryption load commands, since a second one
already makes it malformed; the reason keeps the full count. Range mapping
in every slice shares one budget of segment and section records, charged
from each segment command's capacity before it is decoded. A slice past
the budget keeps its encryption status and reports an unknown mapping.

* style(macho): format encryption reader and binding test

* fix(macho): stop retaining segments past the mapping budget

Segment commands are collected during framing only while their mapping
records still fit in the budget shared by all slices, and the budget is
charged only when the slice maps its range.

* docs(macho): clarify retained mapping allowance

* fix(ci): own the Mach-O encryption test in Apple scope

commits.body:
fix(process): corroborate exiting Linux ownership candidates (#7958)

* fix(process): corroborate Linux exits after procfs environ read races

A token read failing with ENOENT/ESRCH may race with process exit while
native identity observation still sees a live PID. Recheck native lifetime
and accept absence only when corroborated; keep unverifiable or reused
PIDs fail closed.

Refs #7790

* fix(process): recheck Linux exit after final token retry

A process can exit after the final retry of a failed procfs environment
read. Re-observe native identity before producing final cleanup failures,
and keep PID replacement and uncertain identity fail-closed.

Add five integration-facing sweep regression cases for absence, live,
unavailable, replaced and zombie-replaced candidates.

Refs #7790

* fix(process): bound native exit settlement for token-open races

After a terminal ENOENT/ESRCH run-token read, allow a tightly bounded
native-only settlement window to corroborate pending Linux process exit.
Retain an explicit failure for live/unavailable or changed PID identities,
without inferring exit from the token error itself.

Cover delayed absence, delayed replacement and bounded live retries.

Refs #7790

* fix(process): share native token exit settlement

* fix(process): signal only groups with validated members

* fix(process): retain lineage through exit settlement

* fix(process): type mixed identity observations in exit checks

Map inference collapsed a readable/absent union onto the absent
overload after main tightened ProcessIdentityObservation.

* fix(process): refresh groups whose members exit during revalidation

A same-group child forked after the revalidation snapshot is not an
empty group, so cleanup reads the table again before skipping the signal.

* feat(environment): serve the writes callers make without recorded form fields

- A create member a recording sent empty ("", null, false, [] or {}) is no
  longer required; a call that leaves it out is applied as sending that value
  (body.blank).
- List views render envelope members that list the listed entities' ids
  (Paperless's `all`), so creates in such collections are confirmed.
- Updates move their entity in collections kept sorted by a field they write,
  and a failed whole-collection read after an update can teach that order.
- A later create that stores an unruled field otherwise is withheld at the
  create, and an item read may fill values a create's answer had not loaded.
- An unsent field respelled between null, [] and {} is unchanged.
- The skill asks for one create with every field and one with only what a
  person must give.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(skill): show how to read signed-in pages before recording

Agents guessed capture keys (artifacts, dom, final) to see pages behind
sign-in, which inspect_web_page cannot reach.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): accept every empty spelling recorded creates sent

A create that fills only what a person must give sends `null` where the
full create sent a string, and `null` or `false` for the same flag. The
merged plan now accepts each recorded empty value, and a call that leaves
the member out is applied as the earliest call sent it.

Also adds the spec folder for this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Agents read "the form" as a cue to write through the UI, where some
applications' request bodies are not exposed; a body-unusable UI write
now re-records once with request steps.

  values and install the final order once, as replay does.
- A member's recorded empty values stay accepted once a later call teaches
  its default; a left-out member with a default keeps the default.
- Write answers spell empty lists and maps as their recorded answers did.
- A rename can teach a sort when the creates chose one by a field the
  update did not write, such as ids that ascend with titles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

  is_deleted true) agrees with an absent entity, as EspoCRM answers a
  deleted record; such an object never seeds or adopts an entity.
- maxSize, max_results and maxResults are page sizes, for whole-collection
  list lines and the list query's limit role.
- An item view also shows the fields only reads after its type's first write
  show, when no initial entity holds them (Vikunja's task subscription),
  without requiring them; write answers leave such a field out for entities
  without it, and it no longer withholds the write as incomplete-entities.

  expects a deleted object to read back as 404 or marked deleted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): answer sent empty members as sent, and keep a placed create's order

- A write answer spells an empty list or map the call did not send as its
  recorded answer did; one the call sent is answered as sent, so a create
  sending `[]` is not answered `null` because the first recorded create was.
- A read listing the whole collection that placed a create leaves the create
  only the sorted inserts whose order that read follows, so a later rename
  cannot teach a sort an earlier read ruled out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(environment): answer bulk updates without fields only later reads show

A bulk update's answer renders each entity with the same allowance a single
update's answer has: a field only reads after the type's first write showed,
which no initial entity holds, is left out for an entity without it, so a
bulk update of a seeded task is no longer refused for lacking it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The agent trajectories show gpt-oss passes it by creating a replacement contact

update itself is refused in both builds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

An application that soft-deletes still answers a deleted record by id, marked

recorded item reads show that, until a reset or load and within the size

true, instead of refusing the read.

wording. Live observations keep REA evidence ids rather than provider
supplied ones, and the real Hopper verifier uses advertised MCP schemas.

The packaged Hopper stand-in echoed unknown bridge methods, so
analyze_function rejected rea_caller_scan_target as an invalid scan
target and the native package baseline returned unreadable_output.

* fix(hopper): share caller identities in failed scan observations

Failure partials repeated each caller identity under every destination.
The page budget counted compact replies, then schema parsing copied the
expanded form. Identities are stored once and destinations cite addresses.

The environment schema hard-coded the 2000 ms scan default. The domain
limit owner now names that millisecond budget and the schema reuses it.

message is the selector contract, without an abi: prefix.

A missing document selector blocks snapshot replay. Backward call-graph
and trace reads still keep the native result and forward observations,
and the workflow Evidence links those records.

Caller and callee walks still stay in Evidence without a document.
procedure_pseudo_code does not, so decompile_all leaves each body in the

budget bounds and the fixed allowances with no runtime override, is
appended from configuration. Setup forwards the budget, and the bridge
uses one byte allowance for instructions, native callers, and pages.

* fix(hopper): retain compact caller references within the scan budget

Recovered call sites stay in the address form the scan already counted.
Expanded identity copies are measured before allocation and refused when
they exceed the retention budget. Instruction lists are not part of the
retained reply.

Documentless caller and callee reads stay in the ledger for the session.
Their evidence keeps call sites and drops instruction lists the scan
already consumed.

The session no longer reads native_result.instructions.

returning after an ok check. Expected failures assert structured tags,

commits.subject: fix(desktop): charge retained rows at their measured representation (#8105)
commits.body:
fix(desktop): charge retained rows at their measured representation (#8105)

* fix(desktop): charge retained rows at their measured representation

The desktop scan reserved 1024 + 24 bytes per path character for every
row, omission and the root against its 32 MiB representation budget. Real
rows cost 800-940 heap and 490-640 JSON bytes, so the charge overstated
them 6-13 times and large macOS bundles stopped at 3,700-7,200 entries,
far below max_entries.

Charge each path at the larger of its UTF-16 heap size and its escaped
JSON size, plus the existing fixed row and omission overheads, in one
helper. The bound still covers the retained heap and the serialized
report, including control-character paths that expand six times in JSON.

Fixes #8104

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): charge every retained copy of a path

The tighter row charge counted each path once, but rows repeat it in
convention-fact values and the next probes those facts offer, and host
failure issues name the absolute path. Control-character paths under a
convention such as Content/Paks or resources/app.asar therefore serialized
47-80 MiB of reports within the 32 MiB budget.

Reserve each copy through the same text helper where it is stored: path
convention facts with their row, the probes any fact offers (at most two,
pinned by a projection test) with that fact, retained read ranges before
their read, and probe failure issues before they are recorded.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): stop reporting self-defaulted receivers as module loads (#8109)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): stop reporting self-defaulted receivers as module loads (#8109)

The CommonJS loader search treated any repeated state on its own ancestor
chain as an unknown loader. A self-default such as
`session.messages = session.messages || []` forms that cycle, because a
member read inside the assigned value was attributed to the later call's
read site and selected the same write again. Each `push` on the value was
then reported as an unresolved `require` load, and graph coverage became
partial.

Record a member read inside a flowed value as a depth-1 captured selection
at its own position, as member mutations already do for flowed origins.
Treat a revisited state as adding no source; the cycle's other entries are
still expanded once each. Remove the superseded ancestor tracking.

commits.subject: fix(captures): admit browser-serialized HAR request URLs (#8112)
commits.body:
fix(captures): admit browser-serialized HAR request URLs (#8112)

* fix(captures): admit browser-serialized HAR request URLs

har-schema@2.0.0 checks request.url with ajv-formats' strict RFC 3986
`uri` format. Browsers record and send URLs as WHATWG serializes them,
which keeps characters such as `|` and `{` unescaped in the query, so one
Google Fonts or GraphQL GET entry made inspect-web-network-capture and
environment-build reject the whole HAR.

HAR 1.2 defines request.url only as the absolute request URL. Own that
correction in the HAR validator: every URL the RFC 3986 check accepts
stays accepted, and a URL that WHATWG URL serialization reproduces
unchanged is accepted too. Spellings WHATWG would rewrite (a backslash
authority, a tab, a space) and relative references still fail.

Fixes #8110

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(captures): state that RFC 3986 request URLs stay admitted

The HAR request URL rule is "passes RFC 3986, or WHATWG serialization
reproduces it unchanged". A spelling WHATWG would rewrite therefore fails
only when it also fails the RFC 3986 check; an uppercase host still
passes. Say so in the docs and the validator comment, and pin the
accepted uppercase-host case in the CLI test.

commits.subject: fix(apple): charge the XML plist decoder's DOM before decoding (#8115)
commits.body:
fix(apple): charge the XML plist decoder's DOM before decoding (#8115)

* fix(apple): charge the XML plist decoder's DOM before decoding

The XML preflight charged 4 bytes per character and 256 bytes per start
or end tag. The decoder builds an @xmldom/xmldom DOM that measured
1,000-1,160 bytes per element and up to 240 bytes per text, comment or
CDATA node, which were not charged at all. A 1.75 MB plist of 230,000
<true/> lines was admitted under the 64 MiB decode budget and peaked at
249 MiB of heap; shipped Apple plists peaked at 80-104 MiB.

Charge each element and each text, comment, CDATA or DOCTYPE node at a
measured upper bound, keeping the character and number-projection terms.
The binary estimator already bounds its decoder and is unchanged.

Fixes #8113

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(apple): charge every XML element, attribute and reference

The XML preflight recognized only element names starting with an ASCII
letter, so names such as é, _, a CJK or astral character escaped the
element charge: 100,000 <é/> elements (0.5 MB) built an 84 MiB DOM before
the plist decoder rejected the tag. Attributes and entity or character
references were also uncharged; 20 attributes per element measured about
210 bytes each, and each reference about 26 bytes beyond its characters.

Classify markup by the character after "<" instead of a name pattern, so
anything other than an end tag, comment, CDATA, PI or declaration counts as
an element (saxes rejects malformed markup before the DOM is built). Charge
each unquoted "=" in a start tag as an attribute node and every "&" as a
reference.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(apple): charge XML references only where the parser expands them

The previous commit charged every "&" in the document as a reference,
including literal ampersands inside CDATA sections and comments. A valid
plist with one CDATA string of 1,000,000 ampersands was refused although
it is a single node the decoder holds as one string.

Count "&" during the existing token walk, only in text runs and in the
attribute values of start tags, so comments, CDATA, PIs and declarations
add no reference charge and the scan stays a single pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(electron): keep literal IPC sends ambiguous beside unresolved handlers (#8120)
commits.body:
fix(electron): keep literal IPC sends ambiguous beside unresolved handlers (#8120)

* fix(electron): keep literal IPC sends ambiguous beside unresolved handlers

A main handler on an unresolved channel can receive any literal renderer
send of a compatible mode, but pairing ignored it unless it had a scoped
receiver. The send was then reported unpaired, or paired with another
handler. Treat an unresolved-channel handler as a competitor that never
pairs.

The wrapper pass seeds only calls with a literal first argument, so it now
records which invocations of a dynamic site it traced. The syntax finding
gains `invocation_channels: "literal"` only when every invocation is a
traced direct call of an unexported local function supplying a literal
channel. Such a site is already represented by its per-invocation findings
and does not compete.

Fixes #8118

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(electron): keep guarded wrapper registrations competing in IPC pairing

A guarded wrapper registration keeps its predicate on a call path and has
no IPC finding. It still counted toward `invocation_channels: "literal"`,
so pairing lost it: a send on that channel was reported unpaired, or
paired uniquely with a direct handler. The enumerated site now carries
these channels as `guarded_invocation_channels`, and each one competes for
its own channel without pairing.

Index each binding's direct call sites by appending in place. Spreading
the earlier calls on every reference was quadratic in a file's call count.
