fix(artifacts): handle early ASAR extraction cancellation (#5672)

* fix(artifacts): own source errors during output setup

* fix(artifacts): join silent source destruction before returning

* fix(artifacts): retain source cleanup failures with primary errors

* fix(artifacts): join source finalization and classify secondary failures

* fix(firmware): separate source cleanup from output rollback

* fix(artifacts): retain live source cleanup dependencies

* fix(artifacts): preserve source failure completion and semantics

* fix(artifacts): retain scope cleanup owners and typed failures

* fix(artifacts): keep cleanup classification and admission recovery

When the operation completed and only scope cleanup failed, keep the cleanup failure's own reason instead of reporting io, matching main (fixes artifactProvider.cleanupRetry). When a typed primary is rebuilt with pending scope cleanup, carry its userMessage and ASAR header admission so callers keep the configured ceiling and setting.

* fix(artifacts): translate plain file-close failures through the reader path

The outer file-cleanup branch rebuilt every ArtifactFileCleanupFailure as a
ProviderAdapterError, so dyld reads lost their io, unavailable, format and
cancelled reasons and their exact file-cleanup cause. Compose separately only
when the failed primary owns its own translation (a domain error, source
failure or scope cleanup failure); raw and reader primaries are already
projected by the file failure with its exact lease.

* fix(artifacts): bound source destruction by cancellation and keep wrapper admission

After cancellation, SafeOutputTree.write could wait indefinitely for a source
whose destruction did not settle, both in the destroy join and in the
iterator's wait for close. Both waits now end at cancellation plus a fixed 1 s
grace, modeled on the process-output closure grace. A destruction that
outlives it is reported as incomplete source cleanup under an exact lease that
releases only once closure is observed without a late error.

ArtifactResourceCleanupFailure and SafeOutputSourceFailure now keep the
primary's admission, matching withCleanup.

* fix(artifacts): keep one settled wait while observing a stuck source

observeClosure raced the same pending close promise against a new timer every
10 ms, so a source whose destruction never settled accumulated one reaction per
poll for as long as it stayed open. Each poll now waits on its own promise that
the close listener or the unref'd timer settles, leaving one pending wait and
one close listener. The lifecycle test also asserts that a late close releases
the retained owner without an explicit retry.

commits.subject: fix(gdb): keep inferior-tty verification for read-only queries (#5539)
commits.body:
fix(gdb): keep inferior-tty verification for read-only queries (#5539)

* fix(gdb): keep TTY verification across read-only inferior-tty inspection

The console command path cleared `inferiorTtyVerified` before dispatching
any command whose text merely mentioned `inferior-tty`, so the read-only
`show inferior-tty` query permanently revoked a persistent session's
verified output sink; no in-session path ever restored the flag, and a

commits.subject: feat(native): report binary hardening for ELF, PE and Mach-O (#8524)
commits.body:
feat(native): report binary hardening for ELF, PE and Mach-O (#8524)

* feat(native): report binary hardening for ELF, PE and Mach-O

Documents inspect_binary_hardening and its CLI equivalent, including
per-property states, supporting evidence, read budgets, and one report
per Mach-O slice. Explains that missing protection imports remain
unknown, signature presence does not establish validity, and hardened
runtime requires inspect_signature. Adds hardening links throughout the
documentation. The supplied diff also removes the advanced CodeQL
workflow and configuration, along with snapshot-binding mismatch
guidance.

* fix(native): validate declared payloads and dynamic tables before hardening rows

Run the shared range checks for ELF, read imports from the dynamic tables
rather than section metadata, and keep an unresolved symbol count apart from
an absent table. Check every Mach-O command before building rows and retain
only the offsets the rows need.

Make the verifier's readelf output wide, check the emitted format before
parsing Mach-O, and place the sources before the libraries in the link.

* fix(native): share Mach-O segment admission with hardening reads

A segment with a section count its cmdsize cannot hold passed the hardening
reader and could enable restrict_segment. Move the size, section count and
file range checks to a shared admission that readMachoImage and the hardening
reader both use, and pin the ELF load-size case with a regression test.

* fix(hardening): reject Mach-O section payloads past the slice and empty ELF interpreters

Segment admission never checked each section's payload range, so a
file-backed section past the slice still produced rows. Decode sections with
the section header owner and mark the slice malformed when a payload leaves
it; zero-fill and empty sections own no file bytes and are exempt.

admitInterp accepted a NUL first byte in a longer extent, which counted an
empty interpreter as PIE evidence. It now requires a nonempty path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KuWHGvzJkrhCqjtEHUwqyH

* fix(native): read CFG instrumentation from decoded GuardFlags

Use the IMAGE_GUARD_CF_INSTRUMENTED flag that guardFlagRecord already
decodes instead of masking the raw GuardFlags word a second time.

* fix(native): reject ELF table spans a second PT_LOAD remaps

The hardening reader mapped DT_STRTAB, DT_SYMTAB and hash tables through
the one PT_LOAD containing the table's first address. A second PT_LOAD
starting inside the table could map the rest of it from other file bytes
and the reader still reported parsed import evidence.

Cap each mapping at the next PT_LOAD that starts inside it, reject a
requested range that crosses that boundary, and stop hash reads at the
same limit, matching the conflicting-mapping refusal in readElfSymbols.

* fix(native): dedupe ELF note tables only on shared boundaries

The hardening reader dropped any note table whose bytes another table
already covered. A covering SHT_NOTE can hold a non-GNU note whose
descriptor is itself a complete GNU property note, while PT_NOTE names
that inner note directly. Walking only the outer stream missed the GNU
marker and reported CET disabled.

Drop an alias only when it starts and ends on boundaries of admitted
tables, which are note boundaries of the walked streams. Any other
covered alias leaves the feature rows unknown, as a partial overlap
already does.

* fix(native): admit every Mach-O symbol record after a canary match

The Mach-O stack protector scan returned as soon as it found an
undefined ___stack_chk_fail, so a later undefined symbol whose n_strx
lay outside the string table was never checked. The same damaged table
parsed or failed as malformed depending only on record order.

Keep the match and finish the bounded record walk. Records after the
match are only checked against the string table bounds, so their names
are not read or charged to the scan budget. The ELF reader already
admits its whole symbol table before matching names.

* fix(native): accept ELF load aliases with the same file translation

The hardening reader treated every PT_LOAD that starts inside a table,
or that also contains the table's address, as a conflicting mapping.
A load with the same address-to-file translation names the same file
bytes, so tables it overlaps still have one interpretation, and the
canonical ElfLoadMap already merges such spans.

Treat equivalent loads as one interpretation. A load with a different
translation, or the zero-filled tail of an equivalent load, still ends
the usable range, so a remapped table is still rejected.

* fix(native): keep same-span ELF note tables with different alignments unknown

A section and a program header that share endpoints were treated as one
note stream even when their effective note alignments differed. Walking the
same bytes at 4 and 8 can frame different notes, so dropping the second table
could hide a GNU property word and report CET or BTI as disabled.

Require matching effective alignment at both endpoints, and no alignment
change inside the covered span, before treating a table as an alias.
Otherwise mark the feature rows unknown. The fixture's .note.gnu.property
section now declares the class's note alignment, as toolchains emit it.

* refactor(native): read LC_SYMTAB through the shared fixed-word decoder

Move the Mach-O fixed uint32 command layouts out of MachoCommandNames
into domain/apple/machoLoadCommands so there is one owner of those
offsets. MachoCommandNames and the hardening reader now both decode
through it; the hardening reader keeps its own bounds and import policy.

* fix(native): skip Mach-O common definitions in canary imports

A common definition sets N_UNDF|N_EXT like an import but stores its
allocation size in n_value. An object holding only
`int __stack_chk_fail;` therefore reported stack_protector: enabled.

Require a zero n_value before an undefined external counts as an
import, for both nlist widths.

* refactor(native): read linkedit data commands through the shared fixed-word decoder

readMachoLinkeditDataCommand reproduced the dataoff/datasize offsets that
FIXED_WORD_FIELDS already owns. Take the command and decode through
decodeMachoFixedWordFields, as readMachoSymtabCommand does, keeping the
truncation and endianness behavior.

* fix(native): skip empty SHT_NOTE sections in ELF hardening

A zero-sized SHT_NOTE owns no bytes, so the section directory marks it
not file-backed and the hardening reader rejected the whole image as
malformed, while readElfImage accepted the same bytes. Skip empty note
sections before the file-backing check; they have nothing to walk.

* fix(scripts): run hardening verifier commands through the shared owner

The binary hardening verifier started its probes and compiler drivers with
raw spawnSync, which bypassed the src/process/ supervision that AGENTS.md
requires. Every launch now goes through createVerifierCommands, and the
temporary root is removed only after the owner closes cleanly.

* fix(scripts): clean up hardening verifier commands on Ctrl-C

SIGINT or SIGTERM ended Node before withVerifierCleanup ran, so detached
compiler trees and the temporary root could outlive the verifier. The
verifier now turns those signals into an abort that every owned command
receives, so cleanup closes the owner and removes the root before exit.

* fix(scripts): fail the hardening verifier when a signal lands outside a command

Only the owned commands read the interruption signal, so a SIGINT or
SIGTERM during the final cleanup or between commands was recorded and
then dropped, and the verifier exited 0. After cleanup settles, the
verifier now throws the interruption reason. A failure the operation or
its cleanup already raised still leaves first and is not replaced.

* fix(native): fail Mach-O slices with a malformed encryption command

The hardening reader turned every malformed status from the shared
encryption reader into an unknown `encrypted` row, so a short
LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO_64 or an encrypted range past the slice still left the
slice parsed with a full report.

Only two conflicting encryption commands stay an unknown row now. Any other
encryption defect fails the slice like other structural command failures.

* fix(native): ignore STB_LOCAL undefined ELF symbols as imports

A local undefined __stack_chk_fail or __memcpy_chk is never resolved
against another object, so it does not establish an external import.
Skip STB_LOCAL bindings when reading protector signs, and give the
fixture's positive symbols STB_GLOBAL binding.

commits.body:
fix(cli): reject project-scoped Amp registration (#7979)

* fix(cli): reject project-scoped Amp registration

Incur's mcp add parses --no-global but its Amp writer always writes the
global settings file, so a project-scoped Amp request exited 0 reporting
success while changing global config. Fail closed in the entrypoint before
Incur dispatches: project-scoped Amp registration now exits 1 with a
diagnostic and leaves global settings untouched. Global Amp registration
is unchanged.

Fixes #7535

* fix(cli): exempt discovery requests from the Amp project-scope guard

Discovery requests are not registrations: mcp add --no-global with a
discovery flag (--help, -h, --llms, --llms-full, --version, --schema) now
passes through to normal handling instead of exiting 1 with the scope
error, matching the discovery set mcp add itself exempts. Real
project-scoped Amp registrations are still rejected before Incur runs.
Also restores the executable bit on scripts/rea.mjs, and adds launcher
dispatch tests proving the guard rejects a real registration before the
CLI runtime loads and passes discovery requests through.

* fix(cli): share the mcp add discovery classification between guard and routing

The Amp project-scope guard kept its own copy of the mcp add discovery
flags, which could drift from the discovery routing in cli.ts.
classifyMcpAddDiscovery in cliBuiltinArguments.ts is now the single
owner: the guard and the cli.ts mcp add special-casing both consume it,
with bypass/version/schema precedence matching the routing. No behavior
change; covered by classification unit tests and the existing mcp add
discovery serve test.

* fix(cli): emit structured output for Amp project-scope refusal

The Amp project-scope guard wrote a plain message to stderr and left
stdout empty when the caller asked for a structured document (json,
jsonl, yaml), contradicting the failure framing documented for the
output argument. Structured formats now render the refusal through the
same pre-execution error renderer the neighboring output-argument
branch uses, with code AMP_PROJECT_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED on stdout; every
other format keeps the byte-identical plain stderr message. The guard
still exits 1 before dist/cli-runtime/cli.js is imported.

Co-authored-by: Saim Shafique <128062316+sx4im@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(cli): cover Amp project-scope guard through the launcher

The guard tests only called isProjectScopedAmpRegistration, so they
still passed with its call in scripts/rea.mjs removed. Add a launcher
test with an isolated home and working directory that checks the exit
code, the diagnostic, the unchanged global settings, and the absence
of project files for both explicit Amp and default-agent requests.

Co-authored-by: Saim Shafique <128062316+sx4im@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(cli): assert Amp project-scope refusal by error code

The --no-global refusal tests locked the full English sentence. Structured output now asserts AMP_PROJECT_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED and a message field.

* fix(cli): share normalized mcp add agent selection with the scope guard

The project-scope guard scanned raw arguments and only recognized the spaced --agent form, while dispatch expanded --agent= equals forms first: --agent=claude-code was wrongly refused as default Amp, and --agent claude-code --agent=amp slipped Amp past --no-global. The equals expansion and agent scan now live once in cliBuiltinArguments.ts and both callers consume them, so guard and dispatch read the same selection.

Add regression coverage for large results, Unicode, null and empty

Real Ghidra, iTunes, and Claude Code verification remains unavailable.

Fixes #5032

* test(mcp): scope pseudocode contract lookup to official tools

* feat(desktop): capture and export apps installed from a downloaded .deb (#8954)

* feat(desktop): capture a Linux desktop application in use

Add `capture-desktop-application`, a CLI-only, Linux and X11 capture that
launches an installed desktop application, watches it while it is used and
writes capture Evidence plus SHA-256 addressed content:

- inventory: desktop entry, launch command, executable, package and its
  apt sources (or snap, flatpak, AppImage), Electron markers and candidate
  state directories;
- session: the launched process tree, client windows from xprop with the
  first application window time and a window match, and files held open;
- state: a stat walk of the home directory before launch, at checkpoints
  read from stdin, at stop and after exit, with created, modified, deleted
  and retyped paths and the content of changed files and state directories.

It refuses non-Linux hosts, missing DISPLAY or xprop, a non-empty output
folder and an application whose window is already open, and signals only
processes it started.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): own launched processes, confirm walk coverage and keep cancelled captures

- Launch through the owned provider path with a run token; release with
  SIGTERM, then the token-verified group cleanup, after every session.
  Processes without the token are never signalled; each records whether it
  carries it, and the session records whether cleanup was verified.
- Report creations and deletions only where a walk listed the nearest
  existing directory; count the rest as unconfirmed.
- Retain a file only when it is still the walked version, through owned
  no-follow reads; charge the budget only for new content; create files
  exclusively in a private output folder owned by the caller.
- Walk content roots outside the home directory, compare paths in their
  physical spelling, and run executables from the caller's directory.
- Refuse when the window list cannot be read, re-evaluate window ownership
  each sample, handle one queued request per sample with a bounded stdin
  queue, and write the capture with end reason `cancelled` on interruption.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep owned cleanup failures and fresh digests

- Allow a capture cancelled before any requested checkpoint to hold only the
  baseline.
- Retry an incomplete stop once; if cleanup is still unverified, write the
  capture and fail with the run token and process group as cleanup
  resources.
- Classify path changes after a walk (ENOTDIR and other selected-file
  errors) as changed_since_walk instead of failing the capture.
- Treat a non-directory ancestor as proof that nothing existed beneath it.
- Report a before digest only for the file version it was read from.
- Derive stderr_truncated from stderr's own byte counts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* wip(desktop): state view over a capture folder

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep failed file-handle closes owned for retry

Content reads pass retainFailedClose, so a handle whose close fails stays
owned by the content store; the capture retries those closes after it is
written and fails with the output folder as the cleanup resource if one
still cannot be closed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(desktop): read a captured application's state

Add inspect-desktop-application-state, a CLI command that reads a capture
folder into the application's state: every retained or changed file with

* fix(setup): replace the fixed Hopper download deadline with a stall timeout

Hopper package downloads aborted after a fixed 120 s, which was also the
largest deadline the download owner accepted. The current 32 MB Linux
package needs about 132 s at the reporter's sustained 245 KB/s, so setup
could never finish on that connection, and the timeout surfaced only as
Node's generic abort message.

Abort a download when no response bytes arrive for 30 s, or when it
outlives a 15-minute overall bound, with a tagged
HopperDownloadTimeoutError that names the URL, the limit reached and the
bytes received. Linux and macOS setup already relay a thrown download
error's message; the Linux publisher now keeps it for release metadata
and public key fetches instead of a generic verification failure.
Metadata and key fetches keep their 10 s bound.

Refs #7077

When REA_ADB_PATH or the PATH-resolved adb is a directory or a file the
host refuses to execute, the version probe fails at spawn with EACCES or
EPERM. That fell through to the generic "did not report a usable version"
refusal, which named neither the path nor the cause.

Fixes #5689

* fix(process): admit synchronous spawn errors as captured failures

Node throws spawn errors other than EACCES, EAGAIN, EMFILE, ENFILE and
ENOENT synchronously from execFile. execFileBytes called execFile inside
its Promise executor, so ENOTDIR or EPERM became a rejection without
capture fields and execFileOutputFailure returned undefined. Consumers
that classify by failure code, such as the adb version probe, could not
see the code, which left the adb EPERM branch unreachable.

Catch synchronous spawn errno errors at the capture boundary and attach
the same empty capture an asynchronous spawn failure carries. Argument
validation errors stay unadmitted.

The adb version probe now reports an ENOTDIR selected path, such as a
REA_ADB_PATH whose parent is a regular file, as a missing binary with
the filesystem error code instead of the generic version refusal.

* fix(process): expose spawn failures from the capture owner

execFileBytes knows when a command never started, but
ExecFileOutputFailure did not say so, so consumers reread raw syscall
and code fields and disagreed. Mark both the synchronous throw and an
asynchronous `spawn <path>` error with `spawnFailed: true`, and set
`path` on the synchronous error to match the asynchronous shape.
Argument validation errors stay unadmitted.

Consumers now use the owner field:

- inspectAdbClient never reports a spawn errno as `exit_code`. ENOENT,
  ENOTDIR, ELOOP and ENAMETOOLONG are `binary_missing`; EACCES and EPERM
  stay `binary_not_executable`; any other spawn errno, such as EINVAL,
  is `binary_not_executable` with a path-naming "could not be started"
  message. Each records `filesystem_error` and `path_source`. EACCES
  remediation also names parent directory search permission, and EPERM
  remediation no longer names host policy as the only cause.
- DarwinProcessRunTokenReader tags every not-started compiler as
  `spawn_failed`, not only ENOENT. EACCES, EPERM and ENOTDIR were
  previously `failed`.
- NativeDmgArtifactReader uses one not-started rule for both
  `processNotStarted` (previously `spawn ` only, so synchronous errors
  were missed) and the ENOENT unavailable/io split (previously any
  `spawn` prefix). Its fake hosts now reject with real execFileOutput
  spawn failures.

* fix(process): classify spawn failures consistently across consumers

Admit synchronous and asynchronous spawn errnos through one helper that
requires an errno and a `spawn` or `spawn <path>` syscall. The
synchronous shape now also gains `spawnargs`, so both shapes match.

Use the owner's `spawnFailed` fact in the remaining consumers:

- inspectAdbClient reports exhausted host capacity (EAGAIN, EMFILE,
  ENFILE, ENOMEM) as a host failure to retry and no longer tells the
  caller to change REA_ADB_PATH. Path-resolution errnos come from a
  predicate the filesystem owner exports.
- runAdbCapture says adb could not be started instead of claiming an
  exit code for a process that never ran.
- The Darwin compiler probe words every spawn_failed outcome as a start
  failure, not a compilation failure.
- Asset catalog inspection treats any assetutil that never started as
  unavailable, not only ENOENT.

* fix(process): report host spawn capacity as a retryable constraint

Spawn errnos that report exhausted host capacity (EAGAIN, EMFILE, ENFILE,
ENOMEM) were classified by adb readiness alone. assetutil reported them as
an unavailable tool, which marked inspect_asset_catalog unavailable in the
session, and adb commands reported them as protocol failures.

Classify them once in the process capture owner and report a retryable
capacity constraint with recovery advice from assetutil and adb commands.

* docs(adb): describe host capacity failures from device operations

* fix(adb): report exhausted host spawn capacity as runtime unavailability

A host that cannot start adb for lack of process, memory or descriptor
capacity is not a configuration problem. Give it its own failure code and
map it to the runtime_unavailable provider rejection instead of
not_configured.

* fix(adb): report probe-time host capacity as a retryable constraint

A device operation whose adb version probe could not start for lack of host
capacity was refused as capability_unavailable without retryable. It now
reports the same retryable capacity constraint as a later adb command.

* fix(adb): keep the selected adb path in probe-time capacity errors

The retryable capacity constraint raised at the version probe dropped the
selected_binary and path_source diagnostics the refusal used to carry.

* refactor(adb): keep the spawn-failure fact to adb consumers

Restore the DMG reader, Darwin compiler probe and assetutil to main. The
capture owner still marks a never-started command, including the spawn
errors Node throws synchronously, and only the adb readiness probe and
adb commands read that fact.

* test(adb): assert spawn-failure facts instead of refusal wording

The new adb tests compared complete refusal sentences and banned an old
phrase. They now check the errno, selected path, path source and the
owner's spawn-failure marker, so wording edits do not break them.

* fix(adb): own one host-capacity remediation and cover the spawn route

The host-capacity constraint and the configuration failure each carried their own remediation sentence. AdbConfiguration now owns the text and both use it, so the constraint's remediation.action equals diagnostics.remediation.

The synchronous spawn-throw test now runs on Node's execFile route and on the owned spawn route adb uses (stopSignal). The provider test covers inspect_adb_client under EMFILE next to list_adb_devices, and the docs say which operations report the retryable capacity constraint and which report runtime_unavailable.

* fix(process): report EMFILE and ENFILE spawn failures without stdio

After an EMFILE or ENFILE spawn failure Node creates no stdio, so the
owned stop-signal route threw a TypeError while reading the streams and
the later spawn error went unhandled. Attach the error listener first and
capture absent streams as empty, so adb reports retryable host capacity.

* fix(adb): keep a completed push when host capacity stops its digest check

A capacity failure starting sha256sum came back as a retryable error even
though adb push had already written the file. Repeating the request with
overwrite=false is then refused because the destination exists.

Return the receipt with an unavailable device digest and name the capacity
failure in its limitations, so the caller is told the transfer is unverified
rather than advised to retry.

* fix(changed-behavior): withhold equality for unknowns and contradictions (#7624)

find_changed_behavior derived behavior_status from each process

first_divergence was unknown (residual unknowns prevent proving no
divergence) and a consistent contradiction comparison both fell

* fix(process): reject contradictory filesystem capture facts (#7631)

* fix(process): reject captures whose top-level filesystem facts contradict their checkpoints

A process capture records its filesystem state twice: files_before,
files_after and filesystem_effects at the top level, and the initial
and final filesystem_checkpoints. Validation never reconciled the two,
and comparison reads only the checkpoints. A caller-authored capture
recording a created file at the top level while its final checkpoint
was empty was therefore accepted and compared as unchanged.

Semantic validation now requires the initial checkpoint to match
files_before with no effects, and the final checkpoint to match
files_after and filesystem_effects. The native producer builds both
representations from the same snapshots, so produced captures are
unaffected; consistent created-file captures still compare as changed.

parsing Mach-O, and place the sources before the libraries in the link.

* fix(native): share Mach-O segment admission with hardening reads

A segment with a section count its cmdsize cannot hold passed the hardening
reader and could enable restrict_segment. Move the size, section count and
file range checks to a shared admission that readMachoImage and the hardening
reader both use, and pin the ELF load-size case with a regression test.

* fix(hardening): reject Mach-O section payloads past the slice and empty ELF interpreters

Segment admission never checked each section's payload range, so a
file-backed section past the slice still produced rows. Decode sections with
the section header owner and mark the slice malformed when a payload leaves
it; zero-fill and empty sections own no file bytes and are exempt.

admitInterp accepted a NUL first byte in a longer extent, which counted an
empty interpreter as PIE evidence. It now requires a nonempty path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KuWHGvzJkrhCqjtEHUwqyH

* fix(native): read CFG instrumentation from decoded GuardFlags

Use the IMAGE_GUARD_CF_INSTRUMENTED flag that guardFlagRecord already
decodes instead of masking the raw GuardFlags word a second time.

* fix(native): reject ELF table spans a second PT_LOAD remaps

The hardening reader mapped DT_STRTAB, DT_SYMTAB and hash tables through
the one PT_LOAD containing the table's first address. A second PT_LOAD
starting inside the table could map the rest of it from other file bytes
and the reader still reported parsed import evidence.

Cap each mapping at the next PT_LOAD that starts inside it, reject a
requested range that crosses that boundary, and stop hash reads at the
same limit, matching the conflicting-mapping refusal in readElfSymbols.

* fix(native): dedupe ELF note tables only on shared boundaries

The hardening reader dropped any note table whose bytes another table
already covered. A covering SHT_NOTE can hold a non-GNU note whose
descriptor is itself a complete GNU property note, while PT_NOTE names
that inner note directly. Walking only the outer stream missed the GNU
marker and reported CET disabled.

Drop an alias only when it starts and ends on boundaries of admitted
tables, which are note boundaries of the walked streams. Any other
covered alias leaves the feature rows unknown, as a partial overlap
already does.

* fix(native): admit every Mach-O symbol record after a canary match

The Mach-O stack protector scan returned as soon as it found an
undefined ___stack_chk_fail, so a later undefined symbol whose n_strx
lay outside the string table was never checked. The same damaged table
parsed or failed as malformed depending only on record order.

Keep the match and finish the bounded record walk. Records after the
match are only checked against the string table bounds, so their names
are not read or charged to the scan budget. The ELF reader already
admits its whole symbol table before matching names.

* fix(native): accept ELF load aliases with the same file translation

The hardening reader treated every PT_LOAD that starts inside a table,
or that also contains the table's address, as a conflicting mapping.
A load with the same address-to-file translation names the same file
bytes, so tables it overlaps still have one interpretation, and the
canonical ElfLoadMap already merges such spans.

Treat equivalent loads as one interpretation. A load with a different
translation, or the zero-filled tail of an equivalent load, still ends
the usable range, so a remapped table is still rejected.

* fix(native): keep same-span ELF note tables with different alignments unknown

A section and a program header that share endpoints were treated as one
note stream even when their effective note alignments differed. Walking the
same bytes at 4 and 8 can frame different notes, so dropping the second table
could hide a GNU property word and report CET or BTI as disabled.

Require matching effective alignment at both endpoints, and no alignment
change inside the covered span, before treating a table as an alias.
Otherwise mark the feature rows unknown. The fixture's .note.gnu.property
section now declares the class's note alignment, as toolchains emit it.

* refactor(native): read LC_SYMTAB through the shared fixed-word decoder

Move the Mach-O fixed uint32 command layouts out of MachoCommandNames
into domain/apple/machoLoadCommands so there is one owner of those
offsets. MachoCommandNames and the hardening reader now both decode
through it; the hardening reader keeps its own bounds and import policy.

* fix(native): skip Mach-O common definitions in canary imports

A common definition sets N_UNDF|N_EXT like an import but stores its
allocation size in n_value. An object holding only
`int __stack_chk_fail;` therefore reported stack_protector: enabled.

Require a zero n_value before an undefined external counts as an
import, for both nlist widths.

* refactor(native): read linkedit data commands through the shared fixed-word decoder

readMachoLinkeditDataCommand reproduced the dataoff/datasize offsets that
FIXED_WORD_FIELDS already owns. Take the command and decode through
decodeMachoFixedWordFields, as readMachoSymtabCommand does, keeping the
truncation and endianness behavior.

* fix(native): skip empty SHT_NOTE sections in ELF hardening

A zero-sized SHT_NOTE owns no bytes, so the section directory marks it
not file-backed and the hardening reader rejected the whole image as
malformed, while readElfImage accepted the same bytes. Skip empty note
sections before the file-backing check; they have nothing to walk.

* fix(scripts): run hardening verifier commands through the shared owner

The binary hardening verifier started its probes and compiler drivers with
raw spawnSync, which bypassed the src/process/ supervision that AGENTS.md
requires. Every launch now goes through createVerifierCommands, and the
temporary root is removed only after the owner closes cleanly.

* fix(scripts): clean up hardening verifier commands on Ctrl-C

SIGINT or SIGTERM ended Node before withVerifierCleanup ran, so detached
compiler trees and the temporary root could outlive the verifier. The
verifier now turns those signals into an abort that every owned command
receives, so cleanup closes the owner and removes the root before exit.

* fix(scripts): fail the hardening verifier when a signal lands outside a command

Only the owned commands read the interruption signal, so a SIGINT or
SIGTERM during the final cleanup or between commands was recorded and
then dropped, and the verifier exited 0. After cleanup settles, the
verifier now throws the interruption reason. A failure the operation or
its cleanup already raised still leaves first and is not replaced.

* fix(native): fail Mach-O slices with a malformed encryption command

The hardening reader turned every malformed status from the shared
encryption reader into an unknown `encrypted` row, so a short
LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO_64 or an encrypted range past the slice still left the
slice parsed with a full report.

Only two conflicting encryption commands stay an unknown row now. Any other
encryption defect fails the slice like other structural command failures.

* fix(native): ignore STB_LOCAL undefined ELF symbols as imports

A local undefined __stack_chk_fail or __memcpy_chk is never resolved
against another object, so it does not establish an external import.
Skip STB_LOCAL bindings when reading protector signs, and give the
fixture's positive symbols STB_GLOBAL binding.

commits.subject: fix(filesystem): settle a Windows ChangeTime before recording a baseline (#8979)
commits.body:
fix(filesystem): settle a Windows ChangeTime before recording a baseline (#8979)

* fix(filesystem): settle a Windows ChangeTime before recording a baseline

Windows advances a file's ChangeTime shortly after it is written while
security components attach catalog and file-hash extended attributes. A
baseline captured during that advance disagrees with the next observation,
so an untouched file was reported as changed: "Root artifact changed before
inventory" and "Selected input changed while being read".

Dropping ctime on Windows is not an option because it is the only field
that catches a same-size rewrite whose modification time was restored.
Instead, keep ctime at full strength and stop capturing it mid-flight: on
win32 a ChangeTime still inside the drift window is observed again until two
consecutive observations agree, and the settled value becomes the baseline.

Applied where a baseline is captured and later compared: openRegularFile's
admitted metadata and the inventory root snapshot. The exhaustive process
capture walk is left alone, since settling there would delay every freshly
written file in the tree.

Refs #8975

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(filesystem): wait out the drift window instead of a repeated value

Settling on two matching observations was not enough. Two reads taken before
Windows performs its delayed ChangeTime update agree with each other and
disagree with every later one, so an unchanged file still failed a later
check: the reported drift lands 0.3-1.0 s after the write, well past a pair
of reads 25 ms apart.

Decide on the observation's age in the drift window instead, and keep
observing until the ChangeTime itself has aged out. Both the first read and
the empty-observation path now go through the same window check.

The window-exit test could not fail before: its clock was frozen, so the
window never closed and the exit branch never ran. Advance the clock while
sleeping and cover a match that precedes a delayed update.

Refs #8975

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(filesystem): configure Windows ChangeTime settle limits

REA_WINDOWS_CHANGE_TIME_DRIFT_MS, REA_WINDOWS_CHANGE_TIME_SETTLE_POLL_MS, and REA_WINDOWS_CHANGE_TIME_SETTLE_MAX_POLLS keep today's 2000 ms, 25 ms, and 40-poll defaults. Invalid values name the setting, current value, source, and range, and say to restart REA.

* fix(filesystem): settle on the selected environment and stop when cancelled

`settleChangeTimeBaseline` resolved its limits from `process.env`, but the
inventory already carries the environment its owner selected. A Windows
runtime with explicit settle settings therefore ran on ambient values or
the defaults, and an invalid ambient value could fail a runtime whose own
configuration was valid. `scanCanonical` now passes `options.environment`
through.

The wait loop also never observed the owning operation's signal, so a
cancelled inventory could keep polling for the whole drift window — up to
a minute at the configured maximum — and closing the artifact scope waited
on it. The loop now checks the signal before each poll and after the
sleep, and both call sites pass theirs.

Refs morluto/rea#8979

* fix(filesystem): keep the caller's typed error on cancellation

Checking the signal was not enough: `throwIfAborted` threw the raw
`signal.reason`, which `openRegularFile` passed through unchanged. Its
callers recognise cancellation through `RegularFileOperationCancelled`, so
a cancelled admission surfaced as an `ArtifactReaderFailure` with reason
`io` instead of a cancellation.

Let the seam supply the error a caller matches on, and have
`openRegularFile` pass its own cancellation type.

Refs morluto/rea#8979

* fix(filesystem): keep inventory cancellation typed during ChangeTime settle

scanCanonical passed the abort signal into settleChangeTimeBaseline without a cancellationError, so an aborted inventory threw the raw AbortError and analyze reported execution_failure. Inventory now throws ArtifactReaderFailure reason cancelled, which callers already translate as cancellation.

* fix(filesystem): skip ChangeTime settling for private PYZ images

External admission still waits out a fresh Windows ChangeTime. A private image REA just wrote is recorded as written, so a compressed PYZ spool does not add about a second per image.

commits.subject: feat(desktop): pick seed and end by checkpoint, and keep the capture host out of bundles (#9037)
commits.body:
feat(desktop): pick seed and end by checkpoint, and keep the capture host out of bundles (#9037)

* feat(desktop): capture a Linux desktop application in use

Add `capture-desktop-application`, a CLI-only, Linux and X11 capture that
launches an installed desktop application, watches it while it is used and
writes capture Evidence plus SHA-256 addressed content:

- inventory: desktop entry, launch command, executable, package and its
  apt sources (or snap, flatpak, AppImage), Electron markers and candidate
  state directories;
- session: the launched process tree, client windows from xprop with the
  first application window time and a window match, and files held open;
- state: a stat walk of the home directory before launch, at checkpoints
  read from stdin, at stop and after exit, with created, modified, deleted
  and retyped paths and the content of changed files and state directories.

It refuses non-Linux hosts, missing DISPLAY or xprop, a non-empty output
folder and an application whose window is already open, and signals only
processes it started.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): own launched processes, confirm walk coverage and keep cancelled captures

- Launch through the owned provider path with a run token; release with
  SIGTERM, then the token-verified group cleanup, after every session.
  Processes without the token are never signalled; each records whether it
  carries it, and the session records whether cleanup was verified.
- Report creations and deletions only where a walk listed the nearest
  existing directory; count the rest as unconfirmed.
- Retain a file only when it is still the walked version, through owned
  no-follow reads; charge the budget only for new content; create files
  exclusively in a private output folder owned by the caller.
- Walk content roots outside the home directory, compare paths in their
  physical spelling, and run executables from the caller's directory.
- Refuse when the window list cannot be read, re-evaluate window ownership
  each sample, handle one queued request per sample with a bounded stdin
  queue, and write the capture with end reason `cancelled` on interruption.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep owned cleanup failures and fresh digests

- Allow a capture cancelled before any requested checkpoint to hold only the
  baseline.
- Retry an incomplete stop once; if cleanup is still unverified, write the
  capture and fail with the run token and process group as cleanup
  resources.
- Classify path changes after a walk (ENOTDIR and other selected-file
  errors) as changed_since_walk instead of failing the capture.
- Treat a non-directory ancestor as proof that nothing existed beneath it.
- Report a before digest only for the file version it was read from.
- Derive stderr_truncated from stderr's own byte counts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* wip(desktop): state view over a capture folder

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep failed file-handle closes owned for retry

Content reads pass retainFailedClose, so a handle whose close fails stays
owned by the content store; the capture retries those closes after it is
written and fails with the output folder as the cleanup resource if one
still cannot be closed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(desktop): read a captured application's state

Add inspect-desktop-application-state, a CLI command that reads a capture
folder into the application's state: every retained or changed file with
its role and reasons, a typed JSON view of each version (SQLite through the
shared worker, dconf through a private dconf dump, JSON, XML, key files,
text) and the kinds of change between versions (lines, values, keys, rows).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): report process and handle cleanup failures together

When both the launched processes and a retained file's handle remain
unresolved after the capture is written, one cleanup error now lists both
reasons and both resource sets.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(desktop): export a captured application as an agentenv computer app

Add export-desktop-application, which writes an agentenv bundle with one
computer_app environment from a capture folder and its state view: the
apt package, a boot launch matched on the captured window class with a
window ready check, owned paths from the state roles, a seed of the
baseline files, data hooks that call agentenv's add/get/reset helpers
with a typed JSON view on get, a skill, a README and a deploy smoke task.
The desktop CLI commands now load their services lazily.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep state views faithful to the capture

- Read key files, XML attributes, dconf groups and SQLite tables into
  dictionaries without inherited properties, so captured keys such as
  __proto__ stay data.
- Version databases with their write-ahead log as of each checkpoint, and
  stage only digest-verified bytes for the SQLite and dconf readers.
- Detect the format per version, report format changes, keep JSON null and
  empty containers as values, keep XML text and preserved whitespace, and
  mark truncated views (including XML depth) and comparisons of them.
- Number versions and changes by checkpoint index, decide baseline
  presence from the captured type, and keep tagged SQLite integers, text
  bytes and blobs distinct.
- Carry the capture's limitations and omitted content forward, match state
  directories by their home path, index changes once per capture, keep
  failed handle closes owned, and finish the CLI through the shared owner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep coverage, logs and handles honest in the state view

- Read coverage flags only from formats whose readers write them, so JSON
  fields named truncated stay data.
- Fail a SQLite version whose write-ahead log existed but was not retained
  or does not match its digest, instead of reading the database alone.
- Close retained content on every exit, including cancellation, and report
  a close that still fails together with the primary failure.
- Finish the CLI with the canonical operation name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): export only what the computer can install and seed

- Refuse packages not from the Ubuntu 24.04 archive, since the computer
  installs by name from that archive.
- Start the launch command in the captured working directory.
- Respell the home path only in files the state view read as text.
- Report files that were not retained instead of dropping them silently.
- Load captured dconf keys for apps that own no files.
- Keep home-level files as owned paths; rename reserved Python class names.
- Mark truncated SQLite and text views in the class's get view, and read
  file types the way the state view does.
- Release the output tree through a resource scope, and read seeds through
  an owner closed on every exit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep staged folders owned, symlinked state roots and XML values

- Stage database bytes in a private runtime root released through a
  resource scope, so a failed removal keeps its owner and is reported with
  the read's outcome.
- Report cleanup facts and owners from desktop failures instead of
  wrapping them as a plain adapter error.
- Record the state directories as walked, in their physical spelling, and
  match roles against both spellings, so files in a symlinked state
  directory are not mistaken for selected documents.
- Keep whitespace-only XML leaf values; drop only formatting between
  elements.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): read XML in the exported app the way the state view does

Keep whitespace-only leaf values and xml:space="preserve" text in the
generated get view; drop only formatting between elements.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): release retained handles with their owners, read older captures

- Release retained-content handles whose close failed through a resource
  scope on every exit; a release that fails again reports the exact handle
  owners. A read that finished keeps its bytes when only its close failed.
- Accept captures written before state directories were recorded, and say
  in the state view's limitations that symlinked state directories may be
  misclassed for them.
- Compute each XML element's whitespace context once instead of scanning
  siblings for every text run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): boot without the working folder, bound XML, accept mirrors

- Try the captured working directory only when an argument is relative,
  and start the app even when that folder is missing.
- Cut the generated XML view at REA's node and depth limits, and keep one
  unreadable file from failing data/get.
- Accept Ubuntu 24.04 mirrors, not only the canonical hosts; PPAs and
  other repositories are still refused.
- Read seeds through the retained-content owner's new signature.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): state view review round

- Stage a retained -journal beside its database so the SQLite worker
  accepts an inactive journal and refuses a hot one; a -wal or -journal
  that existed but was not retained (including one omitted at the
  baseline) makes the version unreadable.
- Keep tables that read when another fails, and let cancellation and
  unfinished cleanup propagate instead of becoming view errors.
- Read text as a key file only when every line parses as one.
- Rank a file named in a window title or selected by the caller as a
  document even when the application holds it open; match titles on
  file-name boundaries; leave the display name out of dconf matching.
- Bound JSON and key file views (4 MiB, 500 levels, exact numbers) and
  report too-large, missing and altered retained content separately.
- Add no version or change while a database stays absent.
- Read staged databases in place instead of copying them again.
- Give Evidence the same limitations as the result.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): export review round

- Load captured dconf keys without D-Bus: install dconf-cli, compile the
  existing and captured key files into the user database, and warn on
  failure instead of stopping the server.
- Start relative-argument launches in the captured working directory,
  the home included, since the framework launches from the app folder;
  respell the home itself and option values under it.
- Read views in a thread, skip files over 64 MiB, align the generated
  readers with the state view's, and close SQLite connections.
- Never own the home or a shared base folder; map a symlinked state
  directory's files back to their home spelling.
- Report omitted files and unretained opened folders.
- Name the module so it cannot shadow another, and keep the class off
  the module's own names; derive names the bundle check accepts.
- Write seeds as they are read, and remove an unpublished bundle on
  failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): capture review round

- Ask the launch process group and token carriers to exit before
  killing them, on errors too; report incomplete cleanup with its facts.
- Count descendants of the launch as started by the capture even when
  their environment cannot be read; treat a reused pid as a new process.
- Follow symlinked desktop entries; name a flatpak's state after its
  application id; match flatpak windows by name only.
- Stop on end of input; refuse empty, duplicate and reserved checkpoint
  names; require whitespace after the checkpoint keyword.
- Stay on each walk root's device, and never walk or retain `/` or a
  directory containing the home; say so in the limitations.
- Refuse a window manager that does not publish _NET_CLIENT_LIST.
- Remove retained content when a capture fails before it is written.
- Skip reading a file larger than the remaining content budget.
- Record apt's archive origin for each package source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): read an unset client list as no windows when supported

xfwm4 leaves _NET_CLIENT_LIST unset while it manages no windows, so the
capture refused an ordinary desktop with nothing open. Read
_NET_SUPPORTED with the list: an unset list means no windows when the

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): pair members by identity first, build selectors lazily, and refuse oversized and deep text before building a view

- Pairing: an element with an identifier (name, id, xid, *:id) pairs only by
  it, so an unchanged id still names an edited element instead of a removal
  and an addition, and two objects of one type are never paired as a rename.
  Selectors keep the tag apart from each attribute condition and spell only
  the chosen one, so a long tag with many attributes no longer multiplies.
- Size: REA's detection and the exported reader decide JSON with a scanner
  that builds no value, and refuse a view over the parsed-view limit before
  building it, in files and zip entries alike.
- Deep text: the exported reader confirms the whole text is JSON before
  reporting a nesting depth error, as REA reads it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): count a selector's matches over every sibling while identified elements choose only their identifiers

Identity-first pairing also dropped an identified sibling's other
attributes from the counts that prove a selector names one member, so a
shared attribute such as `color` or `fill` could be chosen though it matched
two siblings: the diff reported present elements removed and drafts lost
their checks. Counting now covers every attribute of every sibling; only the
choice is limited to an identified element's tag and identifiers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): tell a UTF-16 seed's format without building it, and scrub XML without one piece per token

Choosing the scrubber for a decoded UTF-16 seed ran the full state
detection, which built the whole XML document (or JSON value), so a large
seed within the capture limit could exhaust memory at export. A syntax pass
now decides the format (the JSON token scan, and the XML parser's events
keeping only the open elements), and the XML scrubber copies out only the
spans it changes.

commits.subject: feat(desktop): keep an agentenv computer up and drive it through REA's MCP tools (#9041)
commits.body:
feat(desktop): keep an agentenv computer up and drive it through REA's MCP tools (#9041)

* feat(desktop): keep an agentenv computer up and drive it through REA's MCP tools

- A Python helper keeps one agentenv computer up per build with
  run_bundle(keep=True) and reports its address, MCP URL, control token
  and sandbox id; it tears the computer down when stdin closes.
- AgentEnvComputer owns the helper, waits for readiness, holds one MCP
  session to the computer's computer_* tools, records through the
  computer-recording routes, and removes the sandbox's containers by
  label when agentenv cannot confirm teardown. The token never leaves it.
- start_build_computer starts a computer from a request (archive package,
  apt repository or .deb, opened on demand with REA in /opt/rea) or from
  a bundle folder; act_on_build_computer forwards screenshot, click,
  drag, scroll, type, key and wait and returns the driver's images
  unchanged; close_build_computer tears it down.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): remove a build computer's container by name when agentenv cannot confirm teardown

agentenv's local provider runs an ordinary computer as agent-<sandbox id>
without the agentenv.sandbox label, so the label-only fallback found
nothing and reported a running computer as removed. The fallback now
lists containers by exact name and by label. The real test holds its
recording open long enough for a first frame, checks the container by
name, and runs rea inside the computer; the guide and tool descriptions
say the app opens from the Applications menu and that a screenshot after
opening a menu should come from a wait.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): own failed build-computer starts, keep ids past oversized screenshots, bound recordings

- A start is owned from the helper's spawn. One that fails and whose
  teardown is unconfirmed stays held under a computer_id close can retry;
  closeAll refuses new starts, cancels and joins starts in progress, then
  closes every held computer.
- When the first screenshot is too large, the error carries REA's result
  with the computer_id, and start_build_computer takes screenshot region,
  format and quality.
- Recordings are refused before reading when the manifest's total exceeds
  the allowance, then fetched one segment at a time, each read bounded and
  checked against its size and sha256.
- The helper keeps the tail of its output (a new tail retention mode in
  ProviderProcessSupervisor), so a build's own error is not crowded out.
- A helper that reported no computer exits on its own before SIGTERM, so
  no phantom owner is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): bound a build computer's action log

Every action kept its full arguments for the computer's whole life, so a long
session grew REA's memory without limit. The log now keeps the latest 256
actions within 256 KiB, cuts each string to 1 KiB and each list to 64 items
(naming what it cut), and keeps the total and the last applied index of each
kind of action, so rules over the whole session hold after entries drop.

* feat(harmony): disclose the unread pkgContextInfo.json declaration

A package that ships pkgContextInfo.json shows the entry in
unclassified_components, yet nothing said its isSO declarations were
skipped: bridge_candidates came only from the libs/<abi>/lib<name>.so
path rule. State that gap in limitations when the entry is inventoried,
so a path-convention hypothesis is not read as a package declaration.

The declaration-parsing half of #4489 needs a decision about who owns
reading inventoried file content; this projection receives identity and
digests only, and the shared inventory carrier guard rejects other
Evidence. No content is parsed here.

* test(harmony): assert the disclosure by its names, not its sentence

docs/testing.md requires asserting structured facts instead of freezing an
explanatory sentence, and says a replaced prose assertion must still pass on a
harmless wording change while failing when the fact is lost. The first version of
this test compared the whole limitation string verbatim, so any rewording of the
disclosure would have failed CI.

The assertions now require exactly one limitation naming pkgContextInfo.json,
carrying bridge_candidates, isSO, and the not-read/not-narrowed fact, and keep the
structural claim that the same package without the declaration file yields
identical bridge candidates and no such limitation.

commits.subject: fix(web-capture): bound the mitmproxy headline facet index (#2876)
commits.body:
fix(web-capture): bound the mitmproxy headline facet index (#2876)

* fix(web-capture): keep mitmproxy request targets and status codes in previews

Capture previews selected HAR/SAZ headline names (url, status) only, so a
native mitmproxy record lost its request target (scheme, host, port,
authority, path) and its status_code while keeping the reason phrase, and
the matching numeric sidecars were filtered out. Select those mitmproxy
headline fields too; headers and payloads stay omitted.

* fix(comparison): recheck historical calls-only changes (#2223)

* fix(comparison): preserve incomplete function call evidence

Keep missing, unknown, partial and unresolved call relationships unknown in function comparisons and reconstruction claims. Aggregate IDA caller and callee coverage without overwriting uncertainty.

Validate with 144 focused tests, typecheck/lint, docs checks and test discovery. Real providers were not verified; the full headless IDA session suite requires unavailable Windows native controls.

* fix(comparison): recheck historical calls-only changes

Co-authored-by: morluto <76467478+morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ci): isolate Linux Hopper process fixture inventory

* fix(android): make DEX descriptor pattern portable

* style: format comparison and IDA sources

* fix(web-capture): preview mitmproxy targets only as safe scalars

Select the mitmproxy target and status fields only for mitmproxy
records, only when they are scalars, and the path only in origin form.
An absolute, network-path or otherwise ambiguous path spelling can carry
userinfo that the native bridge's redaction does not recognise, and a
nested value could copy an arbitrary record subtree into the preview;
both stay in complete record pages. Other formats keep their existing
headline fields.

* fix(web-capture): keep the asterisk-form OPTIONS target in mitmproxy previews

* fix(web-capture): exclude ambiguous and oversized mitmproxy targets from previews

Origin-form checks alone accepted slash-backslash and slash-control
spellings such as /\user:password@host/a, which WHATWG resolves as an
authority with credentials and the recorded transport-URL interpretation
already treats as ambiguous credentials. Preview a mitmproxy path only
when parseRecordedTransportUrl finds no credentials, and omit mitmproxy
headline strings longer than 8 KiB so one record cannot exceed the reply
budget; both stay in complete record pages.

* fix(web-capture): keep userinfo-bearing mitmproxy target fields out of previews

Native redaction covers only request path and authority, so a malformed
state such as host "user:password@example.test" passed through the
preview. Omit every non-path mitmproxy headline string that contains a
userinfo marker (@); valid schemes, hosts and ports never do, and the
value stays in complete record pages.

* fix(web-capture): admit mitmproxy headline values only in their well-formed shapes

A per-string length cap still let a malformed capture fill every target
slot with escape-heavy text, so one default preview page could expand to
about 18 MiB of JSON. Preview each mitmproxy field only in its own shape:
a short scheme token, host/authority without controls, whitespace or
userinfo markers, integer port and status code, and a path of at most
2 KiB without control characters. That bounds every record's headline to
about 4 KiB serialized, even for an escape-heavy path.

* fix(web-capture): bind mitmproxy headlines to their message side and integer type

Select mitmproxy target fields only from the request and status_code
only from the response, so an unknown scalar extension such as
response.path or request.status_code is not promoted to a headline.
Admit port and status_code only when the record's numeric sidecar
reports the producer's integer type; a native float such as 443.0 is
otherwise indistinguishable from 443 after JSON parsing.

* fix(web-capture): require one canonical integer sidecar for mitmproxy numeric headlines

An inline parent could pair request.port 443 with an integer sidecar
whose literal is unbounded or does not represent the value, or with
duplicate sidecars, and the selected-pointer filter would copy them into
the preview. Admit port and status_code only with exactly one integer
sidecar whose literal is the value's canonical decimal, which also
bounds the copied literal to a few characters.

* fix(web-capture): add mitmproxy headlines only for HTTP flows

The mitmproxy container format does not make every retained flow HTTP; the bridge keeps non-HTTP and unknown flow states with their extensions. Add the mitmproxy target and status candidates only when the record's own type is "http".

* fix(web-capture): require consistent numeric sidecars for every mitmproxy headline

Selecting a field also selects its numeric sidecars, so a string target such as request.path with an unrelated multi-megabyte sidecar copied that literal into the preview. Admit integer slots only with exactly one canonical integer sidecar and string slots only with no sidecar.

* fix(web-capture): fail closed on any userinfo marker in previewed mitmproxy paths

URL parsing can fail before recognising userinfo: /\user:password@example.test:65536/a has an invalid port, so the parser reported no credentials and the path was previewed with them. Every userinfo needs "@", so preview a path only when it contains none and does not start with // or /\; such paths stay on complete pages. The parser check is no longer needed.

* fix(web-capture): never promote a redacted pointer to a mitmproxy headline

Inline or imported Evidence can carry a value at a pointer that its own redactions mark as sensitive. Skip any mitmproxy headline whose pointer has a redaction entry, so a preview never re-emits a value the record says was redacted.

* fix(web-capture): check integer headline types before comparing sidecar literals

The sidecar comparison called String(value) before the numeric shape check, so an inline object such as {"toString": null} at request.port threw a TypeError out of the view instead of being omitted. Require a number before canonicalizing it.

* fix(web-capture): honor ancestor value redactions before selecting mitmproxy headlines

A value redaction at /request or the record root excludes its whole subtree, but only exact-pointer matches were honored, so contradictory inline Evidence could still preview /request/host or /request/path. Treat a value redaction as covering every descendant pointer; a property-name redaction still only identifies the parent of an omitted key and hides no sibling values.

* fix(web-capture): treat redacted byte descriptors as exclusions for mitmproxy headlines

Producers mark excluded bytes with a redacted binary descriptor as well as a redaction entry, and the record schema accepts either facet alone. Skip a mitmproxy headline when a redacted descriptor covers its pointer, so contradictory Evidence that keeps the value cannot preview it.

* fix(web-capture): refuse a redacted flow type as the mitmproxy HTTP discriminator

Contradictory Evidence can keep type "http" while marking /type redacted. Apply the same redaction check to /type before treating the flow as HTTP, so no mitmproxy headline is added when the flow kind is unavailable.

* fix(web-capture): refuse mitmproxy headlines under contradictory numeric sidecars

A numeric sidecar records that the producer held a number at that pointer. Treat the flow as HTTP only when /type has no sidecar of its own, and promote a mitmproxy headline only when no ancestor (the record root, /request or /response) carries one.

* fix(web-capture): require a textual flow type before adding mitmproxy headlines

mitmproxy's flow state carries type as a string. When the native value was bytes, the bridge shows the UTF-8 display text "http" next to a retained binary descriptor, so the producer did not supply the discriminator mitmproxy defines. Treat the flow as HTTP only when /type has no numeric sidecar and no binary descriptor at or above it.

* fix(web-capture): refuse mitmproxy headlines under byte-valued ancestors

The mitmproxy bridge emits either a byte descriptor for a value or children for a dictionary, never both. Treat a byte descriptor on an ancestor like a numeric sidecar, and refuse a byte descriptor on an integer headline, while keeping the exact descriptor of byte-backed string fields such as the request path.

* fix(web-capture): check child facets and byte provenance of mitmproxy headlines

A facet beneath a scalar coordinate says the producer held a container there, so refuse the flow type or a headline field with a numeric sidecar, byte descriptor or redaction below it. A string headline may carry at most one byte descriptor, and only retained mitmproxy producer bytes whose content is the value's UTF-8; HAR content bytes or mismatched content keep it out.

* fix(web-capture): verify the byte count and digest of byte-backed headlines

The record schema checks a descriptor's length and digest shapes, not their relation to its content. Require a byte-backed string headline's descriptor to match the value's UTF-8 in content, byte count and SHA-256 before promoting it.

* fix(web-capture): reject byte-backed headlines without a UTF-8 form

Buffer.from replaces an unpaired surrogate with U+FFFD bytes, so a descriptor for those bytes matched a string no producer could have decoded. Require the value to round-trip through UTF-8 before comparing it with its descriptor, as CaptureRedaction already does.

* fix(web-capture): index mitmproxy facets once and refuse non-UTF-8 targets

Reject host, authority and path text containing an unpaired surrogate whether or not a byte descriptor backs it, since no producer could have reported such text. Build a per-record index of facet pointers (sidecars and descriptors by pointer, scalar pointers, container ancestors, withheld values and omitted names) once, only for mitmproxy HTTP records, so each headline check is a few set lookups instead of several passes over every facet array.

* fix(web-capture): bound the mitmproxy facet index to headline coordinates

Facet pointers have no length or depth bound, and recording every ancestor kept one set entry per prefix (a million for a 1 MB pointer). Record only the fixed headline coordinates (/type and the request/response target and status fields) that have a facet beneath them, examining prefixes no longer than those coordinates.

* fix(web-capture): index only facets at headline coordinates and their ancestors

Grouping every numeric sidecar and byte descriptor allocated an entry per facet even though only /type, the request/response headline fields and their ancestors are queried. Keep facets only at those pointers (at most two per pointer, which already decides every check), and let other facets merely mark the headline coordinates they lie beneath, using prefix comparisons that derive no strings.

* test(web-capture): pin headline omissions and controls beside many unrelated facets

The bounded facet index must not change what a mitmproxy preview withholds or keeps. Beside 20,000 unrelated sidecars, a redacted host and a path with a facet beneath it stay withheld while the scheme, port and status remain, with only their own sidecars retained. The test passes against both the current main projection and this change.

* test(web-capture): count long set additions in the million-character pointer tests

The two million-character pointer tests had no time or size bound, so on
Node 22 and 24 they passed against the old ancestor index too, and only
Node 26 caught a regression by running out of memory. Count the strings
longer than 1,000 characters the preview adds to sets instead: only the
pointer and strings cut from it are that long, the old index added
999,000 and 499,507 of them, and the new index adds none.

commits.subject: fix(evidence): bound malformed file field diagnostics (#8557)
commits.body:
fix(evidence): bound malformed file field diagnostics (#8557)

* fix(evidence): bound malformed file field diagnostics

`readEvidenceFileSource` projected every validator issue, and the generic error
delivery applied the MCP response budget afterwards. A file with many invalid
fields therefore produced a transport `resource_constraint` that replaced the
typed file error, so the caller lost the selected path entirely. Issue #8453
reports exactly that: 20,000 invalid values still returned a direct
`invalid_request` with the path and every field issue, while 125,000 returned
`resource_constraint` with neither.

`projectInputIssuesWithinBudget` already existed for this but had no production
caller. The reader now projects within a 64 KiB allowance and, when the whole list
does not fit, keeps the largest leading group that does and appends one explicit
omission issue naming how many of how many were dropped. The typed file error and
its `path` therefore survive the response boundary, and the diagnostics stay
actionable and explicitly incomplete instead of hiding the real failure.

Two regressions cover the bound and the fits-in-budget case. With the unbounded
projection restored, the bound test and its supporting fixtures fail.

* chore: retrigger title and readiness checks after the title was corrected

* fix(evidence): bound file diagnostics in one pass and cover the MCP boundary

Review findings on the first version.

**The prefix was not maximal.** `boundedContentIssues` halved the list and returned
the first attempt that fit, so a file just over the allowance lost roughly half its
diagnostics. Prefix selection now lives in the shared projector
(`projectInputIssuesBounded`), which walks the issues once and stops exactly at the
allowance, keeping the largest fitting prefix.

**A compound issue could still lose its location.** One `unrecognized_keys` issue
naming hundreds of keys expands into hundreds of field diagnostics and can exceed
the allowance on its own. The projector now retains a diagnostic at that issue's
path instead of returning only the omission notice.

**The regression never crossed the MCP boundary.** The issue is about the delivered
MCP error, so `evidenceFileSourceMcp.test.ts` sends the 125,000-value fixture
through the production `inspect_analysis_view` tool and asserts the delivered error
stays `invalid_request`, keeps `details.path`, keeps bounded `content_issues`, and
fits the response budget. Both regressions fail without the bound.

* test(evidence): move the MCP delivery regression to the adapters project

Review finding. `scripts/lib/test-projects.mjs` assigns `src/application/**` to the
`services` project, so the delivery regression sat in the wrong project even though
it exercises the production MCP tool registration. Moving it to `src/server/` puts
it in `adapters`, which runs the other MCP boundary tests and plans the same way.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): emit no fs acquisition for a rejected literal mode (#8624)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): emit no fs acquisition for a rejected literal mode (#8624)

* fix(javascript): emit no fs acquisition for a rejected literal mode

`fs.open`, `fs.openSync` and `fs/promises.open` validate the `mode` in argument 2 before
touching the filesystem, so a mode Node rejects throws synchronously and no descriptor
exists. The guard read only the flag, so a rejected mode kept its acquisition and any
linked release.

Measured on Node 24.22.1:

    fs.openSync(p, "r", -1)          -> THREW ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", 1.5)         -> THREW ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", NaN)         -> THREW ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", 1e21)        -> THREW ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", true)        -> THREW ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", 0n)          -> THREW ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", {})          -> THREW ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", "8")         -> THREW ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", "")          -> THREW ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE
    fs.openSync(p, "r", "0o644")     -> THREW ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE
    --- accepted ---
    fs.openSync(p, "r", 0o644)       -> ok
    fs.openSync(p, "r", 2147483647)  -> ok
    fs.openSync(p, "r", -0)          -> ok
    fs.openSync(p, "r", "0644")      -> ok
    fs.openSync(p, "r", null)        -> ok
    fs.openSync(p, "r", void 0)      -> ok

The guard decides only exactly-readable literals. A numeric mode is validated as an
unsigned 32-bit integer; a string mode must be a canonical octal digit string, padded
leading zeros allowed, and its value must stay inside uint32; `null`, `undefined` and
`void <expr>` default the mode and are kept, as is a computed value.

Three boundaries are deliberate:

- Values in `[2^31, 2^32-1]` **abort the Node process** rather than throwing
  (`Assertion failed: args[2]->IsInt32()`), so they stay undecided instead of being
  claimed as a synchronous throw.
- A spread before the mode slot shifts the runtime position.
- A unary chain is resolved through its innermost readable operand, and a nested
  boolean or string result is left undecided rather than applied as a number.

Regressions cover both directions. Full suite here: 5466 passed | 7 skipped.

* fix(javascript): remove the superseded string mode check

Review finding. `rejectsOpenModeLiteral` builds `octal` from a string literal or a
no-expression template and returns inside that branch for every value it matched. A
`StringLiteral` therefore never reaches the later `isStringLiteral` check, which cannot
run and is a second copy of the canonical-octal rule to maintain.

* test(javascript): cover the spread and boundary paths of the mode guard

Review feedback from @greptile-apps: the new mode tests skipped both paths the
guard deliberately leaves undecided. Two spread cases are added:

- `openSync(...args, "r", "0600")`, where a spread in the flag slot shifts the
  runtime position of the mode;
- `openSync(p, "r", ...modes)`, where a spread occupies the mode slot itself.

Both must keep the acquisition, because neither establishes the mode value. The
boundary cases were already present: `2147483647` and `2147483648` are keep
cases (`2147483648` aborts the process rather than throwing) and `4294967296` is
the reject case, alongside the octal `37777777777` keep and `40000000000` reject
pair.

127 cases pass in this file.
