commits.subject: fix(javascript): report empty Electron coverage instead of silent zeroes (#8332)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): report empty Electron coverage instead of silent zeroes (#8332)

* fix(javascript): report empty Electron coverage instead of silent zeroes

`analyze_javascript_application` reported `browser_windows: 0` and
`ipc.operations: 0` with only generic partial/unknown flags, so a bundle that
imports `electron` but whose Electron facts were not recovered read exactly like
an application with no IPC at all. Issue #8201 is that false negative on a real
Rolldown bundle.

Two additions, both scoped to "Electron is referenced but nothing was recovered":

**A machine-readable indicator.** `electron_summary` gains
`electron_semantics: "recovered" | "empty"`. It is absent when no analyzed source
links an Electron module, so its presence distinguishes "not an Electron
application" from "Electron coverage is empty". It follows the existing
`protocol_registrations.exactOptional()` precedent, so previously captured
evidence stays valid.

**A graph limitation.** The limitation list already carried a note when at least
one Electron fact was recovered but said nothing when zero were. It now states
that zero IPC operations and zero BrowserWindows mean empty coverage rather than
absence.

`electronModuleReferenced` is the single owner of the module test. It reuses
`ELECTRON_MODULE`, which matches exactly the supported entry points (`electron`,
`electron/common`, `/main`, `/renderer`, `/utility`), so `electron-helper` does
not count, and it ignores type-only links because importing Electron types
promises no boundary fact.

Five tests cover recovered, empty, not-referenced, type-only, and supported
subpath versus unrelated package. The empty, recovered and type-only cases fail
on unmodified `main`.

* chore: retrigger title and readiness checks after the title was corrected

* fix(javascript): report Electron coverage from retained facts

Four review findings on the coverage indicator.

**A rejected application projection hid the reference.** A file whose expanded
relationships exceed the result budget is replaced by a placeholder with no
module links before the summary runs, while `graphLimitations` reads the raw
analysis. The same response could then warn in prose and omit the field. The
summary now takes the retained analysis for coverage only, and both outputs
read one `electronSemanticsState`, so they cannot disagree.

**A skipped semantic analysis hid the reference too.** `electronModuleReferenced`
read only `semantic.ir.moduleLinks`, which is absent when semantic analysis is
skipped for a budget and drops `import("electron")` or `module.require("electron")`
forms. It now falls back to the retained `javascript.references`, which the static
producer records for those inputs, while still excluding `type-import` links when
the richer owner is available.

`electronBoundaryFactCount` is now the single owner of the fact total, replacing a
duplicate inline reduce in the graph builder.

**Omission no longer claims absence.** The schema comment said a missing
`electron_semantics` means the application does not use Electron. The predicate
only establishes that no retained fact names one, and unread sources, failed
analysis, and dynamic module names can hide its use, so the contract now says
unknown.

Two regressions cover a rejected projection and a skipped semantic analysis; both
fail on the previous commit.

* fix(javascript): count a dynamic Electron import as coverage

Review finding: `electronModuleReferenced` returned as soon as module links
existed, so a literal dynamic import was ignored. Verified against the two fact
owners:

    import("electron")   -> references: [dynamic-import electron]
                            moduleLinks: []
    require("electron")  -> references: [require electron]
                            moduleLinks: [require electron]

An application that only loads Electron through `import("electron")` therefore
got neither `electron_semantics: "empty"` nor the empty-coverage warning, and the
zero counts stayed unexplained.

The two owners now answer their own half instead of one short-circuiting the
other. Module links answer a runtime static import or require and keep excluding
`type-import`; the retained reference is read for every kind except
`static-import`, which is exactly the type-only risk. A dynamic specifier is
still never counted by either owner, so this remains an observed-reference claim
rather than an absence claim.

The regression uses `import("electron")` and fails on the previous commit.

* fix(javascript): read only module-loading Electron references

Two review findings, both verified against the static reference producer.

**A retained runtime static import was skipped.** The excluded kind was meant to
protect the type-only distinction, but the static analyzer records a whole
`import type { IpcMain } from "electron"` declaration as no reference at all:

    import type { IpcMain } from "electron"   -> references: []
    import { app } from "electron"            -> references: [static-import electron]
    require("electron")                       -> references: [require electron]
    import("electron")                        -> references: [dynamic-import electron]
    new Worker(new URL("electron", m))        -> references: [worker electron]

When semantic analysis is skipped for a budget the module links are absent, so
that exclusion dropped a real runtime ESM import and left the zero counts
unexplained.

**A worker URL path is not an Electron module.** `new Worker(new
URL("electron", import.meta.url))` records a `worker` reference whose specifier is
a path relative to the importing source, so counting it reported an ordinary
worker file as `electron_semantics: "empty"`.

`ELECTRON_REFERENCE_KINDS` is now an explicit allowlist of the kinds that load a
module by package specifier — `static-import`, `dynamic-import` and `require` —
so `worker` and `service-worker` URL paths are excluded. Module links are still
read first for the type-only distinction.

Three regressions cover a skipped-semantics ESM import, a skipped-semantics whole
type-only import, and a worker URL path; two of them fail on the previous commit.

* fix(javascript): own Electron applicability in the static producer

Review finding. A `worker` reference records a URL relative to the importing
source, so `new Worker(new URL("electron", import.meta.url))` names a local file
and is not an Electron module. The boundary owner already read only module-loading
reference kinds, but `finalizeStaticAnalysis` still treated every matching static
reference as `analysis_coverage.applicability.electron: "observed"`, which
`javascriptStaticSourceCoverageSummary` publishes. One response could therefore
say Electron was observed in its coverage view while the Electron summary omitted
`electron_semantics`.

`ELECTRON_REFERENCE_KINDS` now lives next to `ELECTRON_MODULE` in the domain owner
and is consumed by both the static producer and the Electron boundary owner, so the
two outputs cannot disagree. A worker URL path is `unknown` for both, while a
`require("electron")` is `observed` for both.

The regression asserts the domain applicability fact and the boundary summary agree
for a worker URL path; it fails when the producer stops filtering by kind.

* fix(javascript): require a loaded Electron module for applicability

Review finding. A CommonJS `require.resolve("electron")` records a `require`
reference with `operation: "resolve"`: it locates the module without loading it,
so no Electron boundary fact is expected. Both predicates dropped the operation,
so such a source reported `electron_semantics: "empty"` and the missing-coverage
warning even though Electron was never loaded.

Measured on the static producer:

    require.resolve("electron")  -> references: [require resolve electron]
                                    applicability.electron: unknown
    require("electron")          -> references: [require load electron]
                                    applicability.electron: observed
    import("electron")           -> references: [dynamic-import load electron]
                                    applicability.electron: observed

`electronModuleReferenced` and `finalizeStaticAnalysis` now both require
`operation === "load"`, so the boundary summary and the coverage view stay aligned
and reachability-only references no longer claim missing coverage.

The regression asserts a resolve-only source produces neither the field nor the
warning, and it fails when the operation check is removed.

* fix(javascript): classify Electron loads in the static fact owner

Review finding, and the correct home for the previous two rounds of the same
complaint. A Webpack/Rspack factory may name a local module `"electron"`, and the
static producer then records a loaded `require` reference whose specifier is that
bundle module key. Treating the key as a package specifier reported
`electron_semantics: "empty"` plus the missing-coverage warning for a bundle that
never loads Electron.

Three changes, all in the domain owner, so no consumer re-derives the question:

- `JavaScriptModuleRangeIndex.hasKey` answers whether a specifier is a recovered
  bundle module key. A `require` whose specifier is such a key loads a module
  inside the artifact.
- `electronObserved` in `finalizeStaticAnalysis` now requires a loaded module-load
  reference whose specifier is not a bundle key. The published
  `analysis_coverage.applicability.electron` therefore owns every exclusion:
  `type-import`, `require.resolve`, `worker`/`service-worker` URL paths, and
  bundle-local keys.
- `electronModuleReferenced` consumes that owned fact instead of re-deriving it,
  keeping the boundary summary and the coverage view from disagreeing. Historical
  evidence without the field still falls back to the retained references.

Measured:

    bundle-local module ID "electron"  -> applicability unknown
    require("electron")                -> applicability observed
    webpack external n(45840)          -> applicability observed

The regression covers both the local key and the real external in the same
factory shape; it fails without the bundle-key exclusion.

* fix(javascript): identify a bundle module by its loader, not its key

Both review findings were right, and they show why the previous key-set approach
was wrong: bundle-key membership is a property of the file, but whether a
specifier names a module inside the artifact is a property of the reference.

`JavaScriptStaticReference` now records the loader that produced it, and
`electronObserved` excludes `factory-loader` references instead of every specifier
that happens to match a recovered module key. Measured on Node 24.22.1:

    local module keyed "electron"                 -> unknown  (factory-loader)
    external 45840 = require("electron")          -> observed (commonjs-loader)
    factory keyed "electron" that loads the pkg   -> observed (commonjs-loader)

The third case is the regression: a bundle whose factory is *named* `"electron"`
but whose body does `e.exports = require("electron")` is a real Electron load, and
the old key-set check suppressed it. The real load keeps its `commonjs-loader`
identity even when the same specifier also names a factory, so one response can
rely on the loader while the other relies on the key without either lying.

`JavaScriptModuleRangeIndex.hasKey` is removed; it answered the wrong question.

One regression covers all three shapes and fails when the `factory-loader`
exclusion is dropped.

* fix(javascript): carry the reference loader across the worker boundary

The worker schema is strict, so the new `loader` field broke the worker handshake:
`unrecognized_keys` on every `references` entry. That surfaced in CI as both a
worker-schema test failure and a package-baseline failure reporting
`worker_failure_reason: "io"` for a one-file Electron app.

`referenceShape` now accepts the same three loader identities as the domain type, so
the fact survives the worker boundary instead of collapsing every analysis to an
execution failure.

Verified: `JavaScriptAnalysisWorkerSchemas.test.ts` 10 passed, and the full
domain/application/javascript suite is 5484 passed | 10 skipped. The remaining
`SourceMapCommand` and `DarwinHelperCache` findings are present on unmodified
`main` and are not from this change.

* fix(javascript): remove the superseded key set and forward a deferred loader

Two review findings.

**The `keys` set is dead.** `JavaScriptModuleRangeIndex.keys` is left over from the
abandoned key-membership approach: the loader-identity refactor removed `hasKey` and
the write in `add`, so nothing reads it. Removed.

**The deferred require path dropped the loader identity.** `requireCallSpecifier`
returns a `loader` for `commonjs-loader`, `factory-loader` and `create-require`, and the
direct `addReference` call forwards it, but `finishModuleRequireCalls` did not. A
`createRequire` loader saved under a member literally named `require` therefore lost
its identity:

    import { createRequire } from "node:module";
    const holder = { require: createRequire(import.meta.url) };
    holder.require("x");

    before: require "x" with loader undefined
    after:  require "x" with loader "create-require"

Three regressions cover it; one fails without the change.

I did **not** change the inline-type-only import case. `isTypeOnlyImportDeclaration`
deliberately keeps a declaration whose bindings are all inline type-only, because
`hasUncertainTypeOnlyModuleSideEffect` reports that decision as
`type-only-module-side-effect` uncertainty: whether TypeScript emits the import depends
on the consumer's compiler options. Narrowing it to erased broke
`javascriptStaticCoverage.test.ts` and `javascriptSemanticAnalysis.require_links.test.ts`,
which assert exactly that contract. If Electron applicability should ignore that
reference, the decision belongs where applicability is derived, not in the shared
declaration predicate — say the word and I will do it there instead.

* fix(javascript): keep a commonjs-loader reference out of the bundle module index

Review finding. `finalizeLocatedFindings` attaches `module_runtime` to every finding
that sits inside a factory module range, whoever produced it. `resolveReference` then
sent every reference carrying `module_runtime` through the bundle-module lookup, so a
real CommonJS load inside a factory body resolved to the local module key that shared
its name:

    "electron": (e, t, n) => { e.exports = require("electron") }

    fact:  specifier "electron", loader "commonjs-loader", module_key "electron"
    before: resolved through the bundle module index to `#module:electron`
    after:  resolves as an external package specifier

Only a `factory-loader` specifier names a recovered bundle module key, which is what
`loader` already records after the loader-identity change. The module lookup is now
gated on it, and an absent `loader` keeps the previous behaviour for older findings.

commits.subject: feat(python): qualify a recognized 3.14/3.15 pyc header (#8927)
commits.body:
feat(python): qualify a recognized 3.14/3.15 pyc header (#8927)

* feat(python): qualify a recognized 3.14/3.15 pyc header

Python 3.15 is the default `python3` on current Homebrew, but its pyc was rejected with
"Pyc magic 3666 is outside the pinned CPython 3.7–3.13 table" — a message that says
nothing about the file and reads as if the version were unknown. Issue #8206.

Two facts were wrong.

**3.15 was not in the identity table at all,** so `pythonBytecodeIdentity` reported it as
unknown even though the table already pins 3.14 (3627). 3666 is now pinned as 3.15.

**A known identity without a pinned code layout shared one refusal with an unknown
magic.** The two are different outcomes: every 3.7+ pyc carries the same packed 16-byte
header, so a recognized newer magic can still be qualified even when no marshal layout is
pinned for it. The parser now separates them:

    magic 3666 (3.15)  -> CPython 3.15 header is recognized (magic 3666, 16-byte header,
                          flags 0x0, timestamp-based), but no marshal code layout is
                          pinned for that version, so its code objects cannot be decoded.
                          Standalone marshal decoding is pinned for CPython 3.7–3.13.
    magic 1            -> Pyc magic 1 is not a pinned CPython identity, so its header
                          cannot be qualified; ...

The recognized case reports the observed version, the header shape, the PEP 552 flags and
whether the pyc is hash-based or timestamp-based, which is what an agent needs to decide
that a `.jsc`-style text-recovery attempt is pointless and that the file is a 3.15 pyc
rather than a corrupt one. It stays a typed `unsupported` failure: no pinned layout means
no decoded code object, so there is no partial success.

I did not guess a 3.14/3.15 marshal layout. The 3.11+ `TYPE_CODE` order is pinned through
3.13; asserting the same order holds for 3.14 or 3.15 without a real interpreter to
verify against would be an unsupported claim, which is why this change qualifies the
header instead of decoding it.

Docs and the tool description now say marshal decoding is pinned for 3.7–3.13 while the
identity table also recognizes 3.14 and 3.15.

Three regressions fail on the base commit.

* chore: retrigger title and readiness checks after the title was corrected

* test(python): pin the qualified header facts to the packed fields

Review finding. Every new case used `pythonPycHeader(magic)` with its default zero flags
and never asserted the reported flags or header mode, so a refusal that hardcoded
`flags 0x0, timestamp-based` would have passed all of them.

The cases now build the header from explicit fields and assert the facts that field
produces: `flags 0x0/timestamp-based` and `flags 0x1` or `0x3` with a PEP 552 source hash
for hash-based. A separate case parses the same magic in both modes and requires each
refusal to name its own mode and not the other.

Verified by hardcoding `flags 0x0` in the refusal: the two hash-based cases fail.

commits.body:
fix(cli): honor the selected format for unknown mcp subcommands (#7802)

* fix(cli): honor the selected format for unknown mcp subcommands

Incur 0.6.1 renders its unknown mcp subcommand rejection as TOON
regardless of --format or --json. Report the same COMMAND_NOT_FOUND
envelope in the explicitly selected format before dispatching to
Incur, share the pinned mcp subcommand table with completions, and
redact explicitly declared sensitive values from the diagnostic.

Fixes #7691

* fix(cli): correct only the subcommand in the mcp suggestion

The suggested command replaced every token equal to the unknown
subcommand, including option values such as --command. Record each
command token's argument position in the shared builtin split and
replace only the subcommand position.

* fix(cli): leave earlier Incur builtins and caller output flags intact

Incur serves --llms, --llms-full and its update check before the mcp
subcommand branch, so defer those invocations to Incur as well. Build
the suggested command from the caller's arguments rather than the
arguments adapted for Incur, so a delimited format and its columns
remain in the suggestion.

* fix(cli): ignore output values spelled like earlier Incur builtins

The earlier-builtin check matched raw tokens, so an output flag value
such as --columns --llms or --filter-output --llms deferred the
rejection to Incur's TOON path. Check the arguments Incur receives and
skip positions its builtin pass consumes as output values.

* fix(cli): omit mcp suggestions that would not replay caller input

Joining the corrected tokens with spaces re-tokenizes a value with
whitespace or shell metacharacters when the suggestion is copied, and
quoting differs between POSIX shells, cmd and PowerShell. Offer the
corrected command only when every token is a plain shell word and no
declared sensitive value was redacted; the message still names the
suggested subcommand.

* fix(cli): preserve safe MCP diagnostic output

* fix(cli): omit mcp suggestions with words zsh expands

zsh expands a word that starts with = to an executable path by
default, so a copied suggestion such as --command =node would replace
the caller's literal value. Treat =-leading words as non-replayable.

* fix(cli): render mcp diagnostics through the document renderer

Markdown output went through Incur's formatter, so caller text such as
*oops* rendered as emphasis instead of literal text. Use REA's document
renderer for every format, and redact declared sensitive literals from
the fixed call-to-action strings as well as the message.

* test(cli): keep the mcp correction on the subcommand after timing globals

commits.subject: feat(rizin): select the decoder and map address for one-shot commands (#8991)
commits.body:
feat(rizin): select the decoder and map address for one-shot commands (#8991)

* feat(rizin): select the decoder and map address for one-shot commands

execute_rizin_command and rea execute-rizin-command accept optional
asm_arch, asm_bits, asm_cpu and base_address (CLI --asm-arch,
--asm-bits, --asm-cpu and --base-address). REA passes them to Rizin
before the artifact path as -a, -b, -e asm.cpu= and -m. Rizin 0.9.1
refuses -e asm.arch= and -e asm.bits= at startup, while -a and -b work
in 0.7.4 and 0.9.1. Rizin applies -e settings after -a and -b.
base_address is the address of file offset 0, as in REA's raw-binary
inputs.

REA checks only the spelling, because Rizin owns the arch and CPU
vocabulary and its builds differ. The Homebrew build of Rizin 0.9.1
has no xtensa or riscv plugin; the official static Linux build of
0.7.4 has both. Evidence records each input and the complete argument
list. When any input is set, Evidence also states that REA does not
confirm the decoder or map that Rizin used: Rizin uses another value
for one it cannot apply and exits 0. Rizin 0.9.1 keeps its default and
reports the value on stderr, and Rizin 0.7.4 turned -b 8 for arm into
16 without a message. Calls without these inputs keep their argument
list and Evidence.

The real-provider gate tests/boundary/providers/RizinDecoderInputs.test.ts
checks the effect of each flag through MCP with Rizin's own e asm.*,
omlj and byte reads. It skips when no Rizin is on PATH. It passes with
Rizin 0.9.1 (Homebrew, macOS arm64) and 0.7.4 (official static build,
Linux x86_64).

* docs(rizin): map multi-segment ESP32 images with om

An ESP32-family app or bootloader image holds several segments, each
loaded at its own address, so one base_address cannot map it. The
recipe removes the default map with om-* and adds one om map per
segment, using the segment offsets from the image format or from
esptool image-info. It does not depend on an ESP image reader in REA.

The offsets were checked against esptool 4.12.0 image_info on a
synthetic two-segment ESP32 image. Rizin 0.9.1 and 0.7.4 mapped its
segments at their load addresses. Rizin 0.7.4, whose static Linux
build has the xtensa plugin, decoded the IRAM segment as nop.n, nop.n,
ret.n and nop.n.

* fix(rizin): read the file at base_address when a loader would claim it

On Rizin 0.9.1, base_address could read 0xff at the mapped address with
exit 0. -m maps the file, but Rizin still runs its format loaders, and
a loose one can claim a raw image. Rizin 0.9.1's AVR loader matches
when bytes 1 and 3 look like rjmp and turns io.va off, so reads use
file offsets. The BIOS loader, in 0.7.4 and 0.9.1, matches a 64 KiB
file with a jmp 16 bytes from its end and maps it at another address.
An acceptance run on a raw ESP32-S3 segment hit the first case.

With base_address, REA now passes -n together with -m. Rizin then skips
the loaders and maps the whole file at the address: rizin.c calls
rz_io_map_new at the -m address and leaves io.va at its default. The
input therefore means a raw image, and Rizin loads no sections, symbols
or entry point, even from an ELF file. Evidence states this in its own
limitation, and the decoder limitation no longer covers the map.

The real-provider gate adds an AVR-like and a BIOS-like image and reads
below the base, at it, at the end of the image and past it. Without -n
it fails on Rizin 0.9.1. It passes with Rizin 0.9.1 (Homebrew, macOS
arm64) and 0.7.4 (official static build, Linux x86_64). The ESP om
recipe now starts with e io.va=true, because reads use the maps only
while io.va is on.

* fix(rizin): advertise name patterns that compile in v mode

The asm_arch and asm_cpu pattern ended its character class with an
unescaped '-', which JavaScript's v (unicodeSets) mode rejects, so
clients compiling advertised patterns in that mode could not use
execute_rizin_command's schema. Escaping it keeps the same names valid
in every mode, as main's own patterns write it.

* fix(rizin): state what the decoder and map inputs leave unconfirmed

The base_address limitation reported a map REA never observes and left
out that -n keeps Rizin's default arch, bits and byte order. The asm_*
limitation implied Rizin replaces a bad CPU, but e asm.cpu echoes any
value. Compact schemas drop property descriptions, so the tool
description now carries the raw-loading warning. The real-provider
gate checks that asm_cpu changes a decode, and a base_address-only call.

* docs(rizin): record the gate's full run on Rizin 0.7.4

* test(rizin): follow the test guide in the decoder input tests

Focused tests resolve execute_rizin_command from its contract family,
the harness owns the temporary directory before setup can fail, and
guidance is compared with its owner, not with sentences from it.

commits.subject: feat(process): add a non-executing dry run to capture_process_scenario (#8469)
commits.body:
feat(process): add a non-executing dry run to capture_process_scenario (#8469)

* feat(process): add a non-executing dry run to capture_process_scenario

Preparation prompts asked an agent to prepare a scenario without running
it but could only suggest the tool that launches the target. Add
dry_run: true so the CLI and MCP resolve the executable, working
directory, observation paths and admission checks, then return planned
Evidence under the rea.process-scenario-plan predicate. Planned Evidence
is not capture Evidence and comparison tools refuse it as a capture.

The preparation prompt now suggests the dry-run call, and the scenario
identity commitments exclude the operation-only field.

Fixes #8398

* fix(process): redact planned sensitive input and share admission

Address review findings on the dry-run contract:

- Redact sensitive input events in planned Evidence and preserve only
  their byte length.
- Recheck cancellation after the last awaited admission step.
- Run the sensitive-matcher and filesystem-root admission checks that a
  capture performs before launch.
- Assert the prompt advertises the dry_run field without freezing
  explanatory wording.

* test(process): hold the final admission step for cancellation

Add a preparation host seam so the regression can cancel while the last
filesystem admission call is pending, then assert the returned
AnalysisCancelledError retains the caller's reason.

* refactor(process): remove the unused plan alias

Keep the plan schema as the single exported contract and satisfy the
unused-export check.

* fix(process): report admission-time aborts as planning cancellation

`prepareProcessScenarioPlan` returned the admission error verbatim, so an
abort that landed while `admitFilesystemObservationRoots` awaited its
`lstat` surfaced as a cancelled `ProcessCaptureError` with
`operation: process_capture` even though no process ran. Convert that
result through the same `cancelled()` projection the neighbouring checks
use, and pin it with a test.

* fix(contracts): keep the process result invariants on the dry-run union

The output schema for `capture_process_scenario` became a union of the
capture and plan shapes, and the union no longer carried the description
that advertised the cross-field invariants to MCP clients — the boundary
test reads `normalized_result.description`. Attach a description to the
union that names both variants and keeps the capture invariants verbatim.

* test(process): exercise the post-admission cancellation check

The previous regression aborted immediately after starting preparation and
released the held admission afterwards. Preparation awaits runtime path
resolution first, so that abort was always observed by the pre-admission
check; deleting the post-admission "if (aborted()) return cancelled();"
still left the test green.

Signal from the admitRoots seam when admission is actually entered, abort
only after that point, then let admission resolve ok. Preparation now has
to reach the check between a successful admission and the ok result, and
the assertion pins both the AnalysisCancelledError tag and the caller's
reason as its cause.

Verified red-green: removing only the post-admission check fails this test
(expected true to be false at prepared.ok) while the other two pass, and
restoring it passes all three.

* test(process): gate the admission seam on acknowledgement

Race the admission acknowledgement against planning's own settlement and a
bounded deadline, and release and join planning in `finally`, so a planning
result that arrives before admission fails the test instead of stalling it
until the suite timeout.

* fix(contracts): hold plans to the scenario refinements and redact inputs

`processScenarioPlanSchema` described the resolved dry-run response but
dropped every cross-field check the input contract applies, so a plan
could advertise out-of-order events, an event past `timeout_ms`, or a
terminal beyond the renderer cell budget while claiming it had been
validated. Extract those checks into `scenarioRefinements` and refine the
plan's scenario with them.

The plan's input event also carried `sensitive` and an optional
`input_bytes`, which accepted a sensitive event that still shipped its
data. Model the public and sensitive forms as separate exact variants:
public input forbids `input_bytes`, sensitive input requires an empty
`data` plus its byte length.

---------

commits.subject: fix(javascript): apply package type scope to application sources (#7883)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): apply package type scope to application sources (#7883)

* fix(javascript): apply package type scope to application sources

Application analysis parsed .js sources without their package scope, so an unbound require in a type-module package became a resolved CommonJS dependency. The parent now observes each source's nearest same-container package.json, stopping at node_modules, and the worker parses with that package type as reference imports already do.

Fixes #7323

* fix(javascript): keep package type unknown behind unavailable manifests

The package-type lookup indexed only readable files, so a nearer
package.json whose bytes were unavailable was skipped and an ancestor's
"type" applied to sources it does not own. Index unavailable manifests
by container and directory too, and stop the walk with "unknown" when
one is the nearest owner, as the Next app-context lookup already does.

* fix(javascript): keep Electron preloads outside module package scope

Electron's preload loader ignores a package's "type": "module" and gives
a .js preload `require`; ESM preloads need the .mjs suffix. Applying the
package type to every .js source marked such a preload as an ES module,
so its `require("electron")` edges and IPC pairing disappeared.

A source that requires an Electron module now keeps the context REA
inferred before package scope was applied. Node-loaded sources in a
module scope still drop unbound `require`.

* fix(javascript): admit Electron script loaders only on renderer evidence

The previous commit dropped a module package type whenever a source
required an Electron module. A Node-loaded ES module that requires
Electron, or one whose Electron call goes through a local `require`,
then regained the false require edges the package scope removes.

The parser applies the package type unconditionally again. The worker
re-reads a package-module script that requires an Electron module once
outside the package scope. The source keeps that context only when the
static pass there directly observes a contextBridge exposure or a
renderer IPC operation, which only Electron's renderer-side loaders
provide.

* fix(javascript): check Electron renderer evidence without a second static pass

b54845a6b ran the full static pass on an unscoped parse of every
package-module script that requires Electron, then discarded it when no
renderer operation turned up, so such main-process sources paid for two
full passes.

A candidate must now also name contextBridge or ipcRenderer, which any
renderer evidence needs. The evidence check runs only the static pass's
binding and Electron identity preamble with its exposure and IPC
descriptors. The full static pass runs once, on the chosen parse.

* fix(javascript): confirm Electron renderer evidence with the static pass

The focused evidence check from 4a86bca9b also counted renderer calls in
bundler factory defaults that the bundler convention never runs, which
the static pass skips. Such a default switched a type-module file to
script context, so its unrelated unbound requires became imports again.

The focused check now only screens. It follows the static pass's own
traversal, so a negative result still rules evidence out. A positive
result is confirmed by the static pass's direct findings on the unscoped
parse, and those findings become the file's facts when they hold.

* fix(javascript): confirm renderer evidence before wrapper substitution

f71236400 confirmed a screened source from the static pass's final
contextBridge and IPC findings, without wrapper substitutions. The
wrapper pass replaces a directly observed exposure inside a helper with
a substituted finding, so such a preload lost its imports again.

Before its wrapper pass, the static pass now records whether its source
traversal directly observed a contextBridge exposure or a renderer IPC
operation, and observedElectronRendererCall exposes that. The traversal
still skips bundler factory defaults that never run, and the reported
findings are unchanged.

* fix(javascript): resolve declared preload loaders before source analysis

* fix(javascript): leave preload discovery failures to source analysis

A source that failed during preload discovery threw out of the whole
application analysis, so one oversized source or a per-source timeout in a
module package returned no Evidence. Skip a source that exceeds its worker
limits and end discovery on any other failure except cancellation; source
analysis then meets the same source, records its failure and keeps partial
Evidence as it does without discovery.

* fix(javascript): report preload discovery gaps in Evidence limitations

When preload discovery skipped a source or stopped early, source analysis
could still read that source, so the result looked complete while a .js
preload declared there kept its package scope. Return each discovery gap
with the discovered paths and add it to the analysis limitations, which
both complete and partial Evidence carry.

exports it as apt-keys/<name>.asc. A held key that does not verify is refused
with a reason that names no URL.

commits.subject: feat(desktop): read XML with a plain DOCTYPE, and check an element's whole text (#9050)
commits.body:
feat(desktop): read XML with a plain DOCTYPE, and check an element's whole text (#9050)

* feat(desktop): read XML with a plain DOCTYPE, and check an element's whole text

- Both readers accept a DOCTYPE with only a name and an optional PUBLIC
  or SYSTEM identifier, record it as the view's doctype, and never fetch
  the DTD or expand entities beyond XML's five; an internal subset, an
  external entity and a parameter entity stay refused alike.
- text_equals and text_contains compare the concatenated text of the
  element (or text node or attribute) a pointer reaches, as XPath
  string() does, with optional normalize_whitespace; both evaluators
  agree, and a text check on a truncated element is undecided.
- Whitespace-only text between elements is dropped only when the element
  holds no other text, so text split into runs keeps its spaces.
- The draft suggests text_equals for an element whose text changed.

So an AbiWord .abw reads as XML, and its paragraph's text is checked
whole however AbiWord splits it into <c> runs, as Writer's spans are.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): draft whole-text checks on the paragraph, read only text as text, and skip asctime stamps

- A changed value is read at both ends, so text that became a run still
  marks its paragraph, and the drafted text_equals moves up out of mixed
  content to the nearest ancestor named by an attribute, such as
  AbiWord's p by its xid.
- Text checks accept only a text node or an attribute value; element
  names and doctype fields fail, in both evaluators.
- isTimestamp also recognises asctime dates (Www Mmm dd hh:mm:ss yyyy).
- XML files are drafted with the keyed diff the archive entries use, so
  no suggestion reaches an element by position; the shared logic moves to
  appTaskDraftNamed.ts.
- Text-check tests assert facts, not whole sentences.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep checks on a changed attribute inside a paragraph whose text check replaces its runs'

A drafted whole-text check on a paragraph hid every change inside it, so a
link whose label and href both changed drafted only the paragraph's text and
the new destination went unchecked. The text check now covers text and runs
added or removed whole; a changed name or attribute of an element both
versions hold keeps its own check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): read an attribute called name or attributes as an attribute when the draft keeps its check

The owner of `.../attributes/name` was taken as `.../attributes`, so a
changed `name` attribute inside a paragraph with a text check was dropped
again. The owner is now read by segment, attributes first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): draft text checks from text in runs added whole, and name a text element by its own id before its container

Text typed into a run the diff lists whole was never read, so the draft kept
only a presence check on the run, which wrong text also passed. Such text now
marks the nearest element both ends hold, or, when none can take the check,
the added element's own text. The climb also names an element by an
identifier of its own (id, xml:id, xid) before a larger container, so a
headline under a long layer keeps a whole-text check that survives re-split
runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(desktop): expect the whole-text check where #8988's pairing test meets text checks

On this branch a changed element's text is drafted as `text_equals` on the
element, so the identity pairing test now expects that check, under the
same `[@role=body]` key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep checks for elements without text beside a text edit, and normalize DOCTYPE system id line endings

A review found two gaps.

- A paragraph's whole-text check covered every element added or removed
  inside it, including ones holding no text: an image frame, a line break.

commits.subject: fix(javascript): keep timer cancellation within the Node handle family (#7712)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): keep timer cancellation within the Node handle family (#7712)

* fix(javascript): keep timer cancellation within Node's handle family

Node keeps timeouts and immediates in disjoint handle families. clearTimeout
and clearInterval are aliases that act only on a Timeout from setTimeout or
setInterval, while clearImmediate acts only on an Immediate from setImmediate.
Crossing the families returns without doing anything, so the scheduled
callback still runs.

REA linked a cancellation whenever the cleared binding traced back to any timer
schedule, so clearImmediate(setTimeout(work, 10)) reported a complete
cancellation and the graph emitted a resolved cancels-timer relation. It also
flagged no uncertainty for it.

Require the cancel and the schedule to share a handle family before linking
them. A cross-family clear now keeps linkedTimerId null and resolution
unresolved, and the graph reports the cancellation as a candidate with an
ambiguous-target unknown instead of a resolved fact.

Verified against Node v24.22.1 over all nine schedule/cancel pairs: setTimeout
and setInterval with clearTimeout or clearInterval cancel, and setImmediate
with clearImmediate cancels; the other five combinations leave the callback
running. Node's own lib/timers.js shows why: clearTimeout requires
timer?._onTimeout, clearImmediate requires immediate?._onImmediate and returns
early otherwise, and clearInterval delegates to clearTimeout.

* chore: retrigger title and readiness checks after the title was corrected

* fix(javascript): say cross-family timer clearing is runtime-dependent

Review feedback from @morluto: the previous wording claimed clearing across the
timer handle families "returns without doing anything, so the timer keeps
running". That does not hold on every supported Node version. Measured on Node
24.22.1, all three cross-family pairs fire:

| scheduled with | cancelled with | Node 24.22.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setTimeout` | `clearImmediate` | fires |
| `setImmediate` | `clearTimeout` | fires |
| `setImmediate` | `clearInterval` | fires |

`clearImmediate` cancelling a `Timeout` on Node 22 is the case the old claim
missed. Within a family the clear always cancels, which is why the analysis
links only same-family pairs; across families the outcome depends on the
runtime, which is exactly why the analysis reports `unresolved` rather than
`complete` in either direction.

The behavior and the tests are unchanged. The `timerHandleFamily` doc comment,
the linked-origin comment, and the test comment now state the runtime
dependence and why it justifies an unresolved result.

fix(cli): stop restating schema defaults in help descriptions (#9278)

The help renderer appends "(default: X)" whenever the option field declares a
schema default, so descriptions that also spell the default out print it twice:

  --block-size <value>  Power-of-two block size from 256 to 65536 bytes
                        (default 4096) (default: 4096)

Remove the hand-written default from the eleven options that own a schema
default across inspect-byte-entropy, inspect-devicetree,
inspect-packet-capture, inspect-packet-fields, inspect-signal-decoders and
decode-signal-recording, matching the rule in cliDecimalField's contract that
the domain field owns bounds, defaults and help.

Options without a schema default keep their prose: --match_limit, --line_limit,
--limit and --packet_limit are nullable or optional, so the renderer emits no
annotation and the description is the only place the effective value appears.

Add a boundary test asserting each such option states its default exactly once,
so a restated default cannot come back unnoticed.

commits.subject: feat(skills): build a computer-app environment from a request (#9049)
commits.body:
feat(skills): build a computer-app environment from a request (#9049)

* feat(desktop): capture, draft, export and witness a task inside a build computer

- start_build_capture runs REA's capture inside the computer through a
  small controller over computer-exec, after a user-space apt-get update;
  mark_build_checkpoint returns once the capture confirms the checkpoint;
  stop_build_capture returns the draft between seed and end.
- export_build_environment exports with the requester's task inside the
  computer and fetches the bundle through data/get in bounded batches.
- check_build_task grades a computer's data/get with REA's evaluator and,
  through seed, after_edit, near_miss and after_reset stages, records a
  witness with the action log and the screen recording; act_on_build_computer
  gains reset.
- Capture progress lines carry window, checkpoint and refusal events; apps
  start in the home; a pack script builds the runtime archive; long tools
  send progress notifications.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): make build capture and witness steps retryable, and close the near-miss reset hole

- A capture whose start answer is lost is stopped at once and kept
  unreleased until the stop is confirmed; a lost checkpoint answer is
  recovered from the capture's own log, and draft and export use the
  checkpoints its Evidence records; stop can be repeated to resume
  reading its result.
- A witness can check its seed again after a failed read, and keeps its
  stages in a saving state until the record is written, so a failed save
  can be retried without reading the app again.
- after_edit and near_miss count only click, drag, scroll, type and key,
  so a reset no longer stands in for the near-miss edit.
- A .deb build keeps its package file for capture and passes its URL to
  export; bundle downloads write each checked file before fetching the
  next; an apt-get update failure reports its exit code and log tail;
  reset sends progress while it waits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep the Trash out of seeds, bundle folders unwritten and first frames drawn

From the blind Inkscape rebuild:
- Paths in ~/.local/share/Trash get a desktop_trash reason and the
  shared_desktop role, so a file trashed before seed is neither owned nor
  seeded; the export names it in a limitation.
- The keep helper runs with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, so starting a
  computer from a bundle folder no longer writes __pycache__ into it.
- start_build_computer waits, bounded, until the first frame is not one
  colour before returning it.
From review: a .deb that apt also offers exports from apt, since export
passes --package-url only when the capture says the package must come
from its file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): bound the first-frame wait's retries to the time left, with progress throughout

Each retry of the drawn-first-frame wait runs under an abort that fires at
the 10 s deadline, and the latest frame is returned when time runs out.
connect takes the first frame itself while its progress heartbeat still
runs, reporting "waiting for the desktop to draw". The wait moves to
DrawnScreenshot.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): serialize each build computer's calls, keep one recording id, and separate unreadable checks from failures

- One queue per computer: actions, capture steps and witness checks run one
  at a time, so two overlapping after_edit checks can no longer both be filed
  and let the witness hold without a near miss. Close cancels the running and
  queued calls; different computers still run concurrently.
- The witness keeps one recording request id per computer, so a seed retried
  after a lost reply recovers the recording it started.
- A check that could not read its file is undecided, not a failure, so a
  temporary read error can't satisfy seed, near_miss or after_reset; such a
  stage is refused and can be checked again.
- The export's file listing is written to a file and read back in bounded
  batches, so a large bundle no longer overruns exec's 1 MiB output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): treat failures on cut views as undecided, require a decided seed failure at export, and keep a close's cancellation

- A presence check that misses its line, row or pointed value in a view cut
  short is undecided rather than failed, since the data may sit in the part
  left out; a witness stage can no longer be proved by such a failure.
- Export counts only decided failures on the seed, and refuses a task whose
  every seed failure is undecided.
- A step whose turn was aborted by a close or the caller returns cancelled
  even when its work finished, so start_build_capture no longer reports
  success for a computer being removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep a step's saved result when a cancellation arrives during its commit

Reporting cancelled for any step whose turn was aborted after its work
replaced a completed export or witness save with a bare cancellation, losing
what was saved and leaving the witness unreadable. Steps now return what they
completed; only start_build_capture, which commits nothing, checks its turn
after the post-launch screenshot and reports cancelled. Asking again for a
saved witness's final check returns its record.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): refuse a saved witness's repeated check for another folder

Asking again for the check that ended a witness returned its saved record
whatever directory came with it, so a caller naming another folder got
success though nothing was saved there. A different folder is now refused,
as an unfinished seed's retry already is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(desktop): assert the facts of cut-view and undecided outcomes, not their sentences

The new cut-view, missing-value, undecided-refusal and witness tests froze
whole descriptions, so a harmless rewording broke them. They now check each
outcome's id, passed and undecided exactly and the facts its message must
carry (file, pointer, line, row, stage) separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(desktop): read XML with a plain DOCTYPE, and check an element's whole text

- Both readers accept a DOCTYPE with only a name and an optional PUBLIC
  or SYSTEM identifier, record it as the view's doctype, and never fetch
  the DTD or expand entities beyond XML's five; an internal subset, an
  external entity and a parameter entity stay refused alike.
- text_equals and text_contains compare the concatenated text of the
  element (or text node or attribute) a pointer reaches, as XPath
  string() does, with optional normalize_whitespace; both evaluators
  agree, and a text check on a truncated element is undecided.
- Whitespace-only text between elements is dropped only when the element
  holds no other text, so text split into runs keeps its spaces.
- The draft suggests text_equals for an element whose text changed.

So an AbiWord .abw reads as XML, and its paragraph's text is checked
whole however AbiWord splits it into <c> runs, as Writer's spans are.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): draft whole-text checks on the paragraph, read only text as text, and skip asctime stamps

- A changed value is read at both ends, so text that became a run still
  marks its paragraph, and the drafted text_equals moves up out of mixed
  content to the nearest ancestor named by an attribute, such as
  AbiWord's p by its xid.
- Text checks accept only a text node or an attribute value; element
  names and doctype fields fail, in both evaluators.
- isTimestamp also recognises asctime dates (Www Mmm dd hh:mm:ss yyyy).
- XML files are drafted with the keyed diff the archive entries use, so
  no suggestion reaches an element by position; the shared logic moves to
  appTaskDraftNamed.ts.
- Text-check tests assert facts, not whole sentences.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep checks on a changed attribute inside a paragraph whose text check replaces its runs'

A drafted whole-text check on a paragraph hid every change inside it, so a
link whose label and href both changed drafted only the paragraph's text and
the new destination went unchecked. The text check now covers text and runs
added or removed whole; a changed name or attribute of an element both
versions hold keeps its own check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): read an attribute called name or attributes as an attribute when the draft keeps its check

The owner of `.../attributes/name` was taken as `.../attributes`, so a
changed `name` attribute inside a paragraph with a text check was dropped
again. The owner is now read by segment, attributes first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): draft text checks from text in runs added whole, and name a text element by its own id before its container

Text typed into a run the diff lists whole was never read, so the draft kept
only a presence check on the run, which wrong text also passed. Such text now
marks the nearest element both ends hold, or, when none can take the check,
the added element's own text. The climb also names an element by an
identifier of its own (id, xml:id, xid) before a larger container, so a
headline under a long layer keeps a whole-text check that survives re-split
runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(desktop): expect the whole-text check where #8988's pairing test meets text checks

On this branch a changed element's text is drafted as `text_equals` on the
element, so the identity pairing test now expects that check, under the
same `[@role=body]` key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(skills): build a computer-app environment from a request

The product skill gains references/desktop-build.md, a procedure that
takes Claude from a request such as "an Inkscape environment where the
agent changes a poster's headline" to a witnessed bundle and a report,
through start_build_computer, act_on_build_computer, the build capture
tools, export_build_environment and check_build_task: questions asked

feat(desktop): open the seed's document at launch, and say when a seed was made for the task (#9054)

* feat(desktop): capture, draft, export and witness a task inside a build computer

- start_build_capture runs REA's capture inside the computer through a
  small controller over computer-exec, after a user-space apt-get update;
  mark_build_checkpoint returns once the capture confirms the checkpoint;
  stop_build_capture returns the draft between seed and end.
- export_build_environment exports with the requester's task inside the
  computer and fetches the bundle through data/get in bounded batches.
- check_build_task grades a computer's data/get with REA's evaluator and,
  through seed, after_edit, near_miss and after_reset stages, records a
  witness with the action log and the screen recording; act_on_build_computer
  gains reset.
- Capture progress lines carry window, checkpoint and refusal events; apps
  start in the home; a pack script builds the runtime archive; long tools
  send progress notifications.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): make build capture and witness steps retryable, and close the near-miss reset hole

- A capture whose start answer is lost is stopped at once and kept
  unreleased until the stop is confirmed; a lost checkpoint answer is
  recovered from the capture's own log, and draft and export use the
  checkpoints its Evidence records; stop can be repeated to resume
  reading its result.
- A witness can check its seed again after a failed read, and keeps its
  stages in a saving state until the record is written, so a failed save
  can be retried without reading the app again.
- after_edit and near_miss count only click, drag, scroll, type and key,
  so a reset no longer stands in for the near-miss edit.
- A .deb build keeps its package file for capture and passes its URL to
  export; bundle downloads write each checked file before fetching the
  next; an apt-get update failure reports its exit code and log tail;
  reset sends progress while it waits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): keep the Trash out of seeds, bundle folders unwritten and first frames drawn

From the blind Inkscape rebuild:
- Paths in ~/.local/share/Trash get a desktop_trash reason and the
  shared_desktop role, so a file trashed before seed is neither owned nor
  seeded; the export names it in a limitation.
- The keep helper runs with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, so starting a
  computer from a bundle folder no longer writes __pycache__ into it.
- start_build_computer waits, bounded, until the first frame is not one
  colour before returning it.
From review: a .deb that apt also offers exports from apt, since export
passes --package-url only when the capture says the package must come
from its file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): bound the first-frame wait's retries to the time left, with progress throughout

Each retry of the drawn-first-frame wait runs under an abort that fires at
the 10 s deadline, and the latest frame is returned when time runs out.
connect takes the first frame itself while its progress heartbeat still
runs, reporting "waiting for the desktop to draw". The wait moves to
DrawnScreenshot.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): serialize each build computer's calls, keep one recording id, and separate unreadable checks from failures

- One queue per computer: actions, capture steps and witness checks run one
  at a time, so two overlapping after_edit checks can no longer both be filed
  and let the witness hold without a near miss. Close cancels the running and
  queued calls; different computers still run concurrently.
- The witness keeps one recording request id per computer, so a seed retried
  after a lost reply recovers the recording it started.
- A check that could not read its file is undecided, not a failure, so a
  temporary read error can't satisfy seed, near_miss or after_reset; such a
  stage is refused and can be checked again.
- The export's file listing is written to a file and read back in bounded
  batches, so a large bundle no longer overruns exec's 1 MiB output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(desktop): treat failures on cut views as undecided, require a decided seed failure at export, and keep a close's cancellation

- A presence check that misses its line, row or pointed value in a view cut
  short is undecided rather than failed, since the data may sit in the part
  left out; a witness stage can no longer be proved by such a failure.
- Export counts only decided failures on the seed, and refuses a task whose
  every seed failure is undecided.
- A step whose turn was aborted by a close or the caller returns cancelled
  even when its work finished, so start_build_capture no longer reports
  success for a computer being removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reporting cancelled for any step whose turn was aborted after its work
replaced a completed export or witness save with a bare cancellation, losing

completed; only start_build_capture, which commits nothing, checks its turn
after the post-launch screenshot and reports cancelled. Asking again for a
saved witness's final check returns its record.

* feat(desktop): read XML with a plain DOCTYPE, and check an element's whole text

- Both readers accept a DOCTYPE with only a name and an optional PUBLIC
  or SYSTEM identifier, record it as the view's doctype, and never fetch

  external entity and a parameter entity stay refused alike.

- Whitespace-only text between elements is dropped only when the element

* fix(desktop): wait out long build commands, fail a reset that restores nothing, and tie the witness to its bundle

A review found five gaps.

  waiting for headers after 300 s. So a slow export, draft or start always

  by that deadline.

  seed stage now refuses a task whose steps or checks differ from the
  bundle's.

* fix(desktop): keep a completed reset, an unread seed, and a failed apt update

A cancel after data/reset no longer drops the restore from the action log,
so a near miss cannot treat the restored seed as an edit. An unreadable
seed check that later passes leaves after_reset undecided instead of
failing the witness. apt-get update is kept only when Error-Mode reports
success and a package list was fetched. The controller reply schema lives
with the controller, and capture progress lines are read by their domain
parser.

* fix(desktop): keep a whitespace-only run under the paragraph text check

A run whose only text is whitespace is still text the paragraph check
reads. It no longer gets its own presence check, which a later save of
the same words without that run would fail. Images and breaks, whose
text is empty, still keep their own checks.

* fix(desktop): keep an unread reset and a cut text check undecided

after_reset stays undecided when any check was not read, even if another
check still fails and the unread result's boolean matches the seed. A
text check for a child past a truncated view is undecided in both
evaluators. A reset whose reply is lost blocks a near miss until a later
input or a reset whose reply arrives.

* fix(desktop): retry a witness recording and a published record's cleanup

A recording that fails to end or download is not written into the witness
folder, and a manifest already received is fetched again without ending
the recording twice. A folder that is published while its handles fail to
close keeps that record and retries the same cleanup instead of writing
the folder again.

* fix(desktop): keep a published witness error and tag an app data refusal

A second failure to close a published witness returns the original error,
so its record and cleanup lease stay bound. A reset the app itself
refuses is an AppDataRefusal; only a reply that is not that refusal stays
unsettled. A missing child of a cut view is undecided with the same
description in both evaluators, and the shared cases cover it.

* fix(desktop): align a cut view's missing text with the Python check

A missing child of a truncated view is undecided for the same sentence in both evaluators, including the pointer the view does not contain.

* fix(desktop): keep one published witness cleanup across retries

A published record and its bound cleanup error stay together. A later close failure returns that error, and the unused path that built a fresh adapter error is gone.

* fix(desktop): keep a bundle task read inside the witness result

A cancelled, refused, or failed read of the bundle's task files returns the witness's Result, including a cleanup lease when a handle would not close.

fix(desktop): keep a failed library owner query unknown (#9240)

* fix(desktop): keep a failed library owner query unknown

dpkg-query -S exits 1 when some requested path has no owner and 2 when
it could not answer at all. LibraryPackageInventory.packageOwners only
rejected the missing and failed outcomes, so an exit of 2 with empty
stdout parsed as a successful empty owner map and every located library
was recorded in unpackaged_libraries. That turns a failed lookup into an
incorrect ownership fact and drops the reason, while the executable
owner lookup in DebianPackageInventory already treats exit codes above 1
as unknown.

Treat an exit code above 1 as a failed query for the batch, report it in
library_packages_reason, and leave the libraries it covered out of
unpackaged_libraries. Already established missing_libraries are kept.

commits.subject: fix(wasm): admit compatible 1.0.x WABT releases (#9223)
commits.body:
fix(wasm): admit compatible 1.0.x WABT releases (#9223)

* fix(wasm): admit compatible 1.0.x WABT releases

REA_WABT_BIN_DIRECTORY admission compared each --version banner to the
literal 1.0.42, so a Homebrew or rolling-distribution WABT that advanced
past that build was refused even though wasm-validate, wasm-objdump and
wasm2wat accept the same flags and emit the same output shape. Callers had
to keep a hand-extracted 1.0.42 tarball alongside the system package.

Admission now accepts the release range ^1.0.42 and records the observed
banner, matching how the Wakaru adapter already admits compatible builds.
The verified release stays the reference: a banner other than 1.0.42 is
retained as tool_profile.release and provider.version and the report states
that only 1.0.42 was verified. All three tools must report the same release,
since one directory is one installation. Managed downloads stay pinned.

Fixes #9197

* fix(wasm): bound WABT admission to releases the report schema accepts

WABT_ACCEPTED_RANGE was "^1.0.42", which also admits 1.1.0 and later 1.x
releases, while wasmArtifactSchema only accepts 1.0.x banners. A configured
tool reporting 1.1.0 therefore passed version admission, ran the inspection,
and then failed at report parsing. Use the explicit ">=1.0.42 <1.1.0"
range so admission and the schema agree, and test the boundary.

Also carry the compatible-release warning into both partial-Evidence
builders. Previously only successful reports stated that REA verified
1.0.42, so a validation rejection or later read failure under a
compatible release silently dropped the uncertainty that a success reports.
Share the text through wabtReleaseLimitation so both paths stay aligned.

* fix(wasm): stop claiming the 1.0.42 commit for a newer admitted release

A caller-supplied 1.0.43 or 1.0.44 was admitted with the observed banner in
tool_profile.release, but source_commit still carried the 1.0.42 revision,
which is a claim about a build that did not run. Emit null for any release
other than the verified 1.0.42; the observed release and each executable
digest still identify what actually ran.

Also spell the accepted range as it is defined (>=1.0.42 <1.1.0) in the guide
and the failure fixture instead of ^1.0.42, which in semver admits 1.1.0.

* fix(cli): advertise the source-location path and URL constraints

trace-web-source-location declared manifestPath, sourceMapPath and sourceMapUrl
as bare strings, so `--schema --json` advertised them with no minLength and no
absolute-path pattern. The service then refused a relative manifest or map with
a post-parse invalid_request naming manifest_path and source_map.path, while
trace-web-module-imports already advertises those constraints from its domain
fields.

Bind the three positionals to webSourceLocationInputSchema so the domain field
owns the bounds, format and help, matching the rule in cliDecimalField that the
domain field owns bounds, defaults, nullability and help. The CLI now refuses a
relative or NUL-bearing value at its own boundary with a field-level message
instead of surfacing a service-level failure.

Add a boundary test that compiles the advertised args schema and asserts the
shared path and non-empty URL constraints, next to the existing sibling case.

* test(cli): isolate the NUL rejection from the absolute-path check

The boundary case for trace-web-source-location used "manifest\0.json", which is
also a relative path. The absolute-path constraint alone rejects it, so the case
would still pass if schema conversion dropped the NUL pattern. Use an absolute
path with an embedded NUL instead, and add the same case for sourceMapPath.

Input issues report minimum and maximum as inclusive bounds, as JSON Schema does, but the projection ignored Zod's inclusive flag. A .positive() field such as inspect_analysis_view view.limit or observe_native_ui pid rejected 0 and reported minimum: 0, naming the rejected value as allowed; .lt() limits had the same problem for maximum. commits.subject: fix(javascript): keep unisolated program-var route values unknown (#6778)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): keep unisolated program-var route values unknown (#6778)

* fix(javascript): mark unisolated program-var route values unproven

`JavaScriptRouteScan.#resolve` now records the identifier whenever a value
proof depends on a program-scope `var` in a script without a proven isolated
runtime. That binding is a global-object property, so `globalThis.NAME` or an
alias can replace it after the source initializer.

The mark lives in the shared resolver, so every consumer degrades from one
fact instead of each one opting in:

- path segments and navigation destinations stop asserting the source value
  and report an unknown interpretation;
- an index flag stays unproven, as before;
- a route container keeps its source route set and reports an incomplete
  interpretation, so `var routes=[...]` no longer loses every route.

The source initializer is still followed, which is what lets a container
consumer keep its facts while disclosing the gap.

* fix(javascript): keep literal child routes behind an unisolated children array

Rejecting the whole children configuration marked its records as claimed
by the interpretation, so the automatic-root loop skipped them and the
literal child paths disappeared even though their absolute paths need no
parent proof. Keep the source records reachable and let the walker report
the unproven ancestry as an interpretation gap.

* test(javascript): bound the index-route CLI acceptance matrix

The flag matrix runs sixteen CLI invocations in one test and passed at 20.7 s
against a 30 s default timeout, so it timed out on a loaded runner. The same
matrix is already asserted per case in javascriptRouteScan.test.ts, where each
case is an in-process parse; this file keeps one resolved case and one
unresolved case to prove both branches of the public CLI view.

* fix(javascript): retain ownership of unproven route literals

Keep source ownership separate from runtime value proof so rejected program-var route segments cannot reappear through the generic constant pass. Cover path, route, typed and alias forms, retain navigation controls and independent literals, and verify inventory and public CLI projections.

Run the existing CLI index cases independently so repeated process startup does not consume one combined test deadline. Preserve both cases and all assertions.

* fix(javascript): keep unisolated navigation data out of route literals

An unisolated program-var slot holds data, not a route. Refusing its
runtime identity released the object back to the independent route scan,
which then reported a query payload as a nested route. Report the object
as consumed navigation data and stop following it as a path.

* fix(javascript): follow rejected navigation data without trusting it

Claiming the whole object for a rejected value also claimed its sibling
properties, so an independent route in the same object disappeared.
Keep the property selection: ownership follows the slot, and only the
route consumers refuse an unproven runtime identity.

commits.subject: fix(doctor): probe providers with the selected client's registration environment (#9108)
commits.body:
fix(doctor): probe providers with the selected client's registration environment (#9108)

* fix(doctor): probe providers with the selected client's registration environment

rea doctor read provider settings only from the terminal running it. A client
registration that carries GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR or REA_JADX_MCP_CONFIG under its
own env block therefore looked unconfigured: doctor answered not_configured
while the server that client starts inherited the settings and worked. This is
the recovery command the docs point agents at, so the false negative sent them
back to re-apply fixes that were already in place.

When the caller names exactly one client, read that registration's effective
environment and hand it to the provider checks. Terminal variables that
providers resolve outside server config (PATH, SYSTEMROOT) stay inherited, and
running doctor without --client still reports this terminal. A registration the
loader cannot read keeps its own registration check as the answer instead of
being re-reported as four missing providers.

Fixes #9102

* fix(doctor): keep setup's terminal settings and a failed close on the host

Greptile found two regressions in the selected-client environment read.

Provider probes now start from the terminal and overlay the selected
registration, instead of replacing the terminal with the registration
alone. `rea setup --client` passes its own client selection through the
same doctor call, so on a first run with GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR exported and no
registration yet, the replacements made setup report providerConfigured:
false and offer Hopper over the selected BYO provider. The registration
still wins for every value it records.

The registration read now runs inside the caller's resource scope and, when
the close of the configuration file fails, retains the returned owner there
so host.close() retries it. Dropping that owner left an unretired handle
with no way to report the unfinished cleanup.

* fix(doctor): leave a registration's expression settings unknown

Greptile found the previous fallback filling a name the selected client
records as a Cordis expression with the terminal's value. `dsh` keeps such
a value as `!!js ...`, which is not a literal; the parser reports the name
in `unresolvedSettings`, and merging the terminal into it then made probes
certify a setting the client owns and this process cannot read.

Unresolved names are now removed after the overlay, and an unreadable,
malformed, or unresolvable registration returns no environment at all, so
the caller keeps the terminal instead of a partly-known one. Provider checks
report those settings as unconfigured, which is the honest answer for a
chain that resolves outside REA.

dsh's missing registration still inherits the terminal, which is the case
`rea setup` depends on.

* fix(doctor): fold registration settings by platform identity

`selectedProviderSettings` overlaid a selected client's registration on the
terminal with an object spread. On Windows a registration can record
`ghidra_install_dir` while the terminal exports `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`; the spread
kept both spellings, and since provider checks read the canonical uppercase
names, doctor either certified the terminal's install or reported the setting as
unconfigured. An expression the registration marks unresolved was skipped under
one spelling while its terminal value survived under the other.

Merge the two layers through `mergeEnvironmentOverrides` and fold the result
with `snapshotEnvironment`, so the registration's value wins regardless of how
it spells the name and the provider sees the names it reads. Fold the unresolved
names the same way before deleting them, and export the helper so the two
platform identities can be covered directly.

* style(doctor): wrap the long import in the runtime test

oxfmt wants the three imported names on their own lines; the previous
commit left the single-line form, which fails `npm run format:check`.

* test(codebuddy): construct the registration command like its sibling clients

`npxRegistrationCommand` was removed in c77735fa ("fix(setup)!: bind managed
registrations to selected installation"). The CodeBuddy boundary test landed
after that refactor and still imported it, so `npm run typecheck` failed on
every branch that descends from merge fb841a95 — main included, where the
main push CI is still queued.

Use `currentClientRegistrationCommand()` the way the kimi, lmStudio and other
client configuration tests already do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): retain failed registration file cleanup

* fix(doctor): preserve unknown client provider readiness

* fix(doctor): scope Kuna readiness to its environment

* test(doctor): respect Kuna host support

* fix(doctor): read a registration's unresolved settings only where the probe needs them

Every setting an expression made unresolved blocked readiness, even one the provider never consults for the configuration the client supplied. With a literal JAVA_HOME and jar path, JADX resolves Java by absolute path and does not read PATH, yet a dsh registration with an expression-backed PATH skipped the probe and reported the provider unknown. Ghidra is the same when both GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR and JAVA_HOME are explicit.

Decide per provider which unresolved setting the probe actually reads, and skip only those. Kuna's readiness list also omitted HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME, which its cache root falls back to, so an unresolved cache input could let the probe check a fallback directory and report available without knowing the client's real cache.

* fix(doctor): stop probing a registration expression as a literal

Two findings from the review, both about handing a probe a value REA cannot interpret.

REA_KUNA_CACHE_DIR made settingAffectsProbe ignore every unresolved Kuna setting, so an expression-backed REA_KUNA_COMMAND or REA_KUNA_JOBS silently fell back to a default and the provider could report ready. Limit the exception to HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME, the two cache-location defaults.

HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME were also added to KUNA_DOCTOR_SETTINGS, which registrationEnvironment copies wholesale, so setup persisted ambient values a child already inherits. Split the readiness inputs from the settings setup writes.

Qwen expands $VAR and ${VAR} in a recorded env value from the environment it runs with. REA cannot predict that, but it was handing the literal to the probes, so a registration appending to PATH made JADX search for a literal ${PATH} entry. Treat such values as unresolved for that client so the affected provider reports unknown instead of probing the literal text.

* fix(registration): recognize a client's env expression at the shared reader

Doctor decided which Qwen settings were expressions after the shared registration reader had already parsed them as literals, so doctor and setup/status held two interpretations of the same file. AGENTS.md requires normalizing once at the owning boundary, so move the recognition into ClientRegistrationEnvironment and let every consumer read the facts it returns.

The reader now takes the client name, marks a variable-expanding client's $VAR and ${VAR} values as unresolved, and reports those names through unresolvedSettings. Doctor drops its own parser; setup and status pick up the same facts, which also keeps an expression-valued timeout out of the resolved budget instead of trusting the literal.

* fix(doctor): preserve unresolved typed settings

* style(cli): wrap the native data type path description

The `inspect-native-data-type` argument description line is 82 columns, over the repository's 80-column `.oxfmtrc.json` limit, so `npm run format:check` fails on main and on every branch merged from it. It came in with #9465 and the following commits to this file did not touch it. Reformat the one call the formatter objects to; no behaviour change.
