commits.subject: fix(javascript): reject child-process option literals Node refuses at the call site (#9594)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): reject child-process option literals Node refuses at the call site (#9594)

* fix(javascript): reject a spawn stdio string Node refuses at the call site

`node:child_process` validates a literal `stdio` string before it creates anything, so a
bad value throws from the call itself and no child process exists. The analysis reported the
raw string as `stdioMode` and kept the spawn.

Measured on Node 24.22.1:

| `stdio` | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `"pipe"`, `"overlapped"`, `"inherit"`, `"ignore"` | child starts |
| `"ipc"`, `"PIPE"`, `"pipe "`, `"pipeline"`, `"stream"`, `"stdio"` | THREW `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` |

The accepted set is exact and case-sensitive, so it is a closed list rather than a pattern.
`"ipc"` is the interesting one: it is valid as an array element but refused as the scalar
shorthand, which is the shape a caller reaches for when they mean the array form.

`fork` differs on one value because it appends `"ipc"` to a string and splits it, so `""`
becomes the lone element `"ipc"` and is refused:

| call | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `spawn(..., {stdio: ""})` | child starts |
| `fork(..., {stdio: ""})` | THREW `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` |

`exec` is left alone, because it spreads its options and validates none of them. A number,
boolean or object `stdio` is also refused by Node, but `stdioMode` already reports those as
`"dynamic"`; deciding them here would claim more than the reported mode explains, so only
the string case is decided.

18 cases, 9 failing before this commit. `src/domain/javascript`: 5106 to 5124 passing.
`tsc` 0; `build` 0; `npm run format:check` 0; `npm run lint` 0 errors.

* fix(javascript): reject a non-string cwd or argv0 Node refuses at the call site

The same call-site validation the `stdio` string gets applies to `cwd` and `argv0`:
Node checks them before the child exists, so a non-string literal throws
`ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` and the analysis still reported a spawn.

Measured on Node 24.22.1, identical on `spawn`, `fork`, `execFile` and `exec`:

| `cwd` / `argv0` | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `"/tmp"` / `"x"` | child starts |
| `null` | child starts |
| `5`, `0`, `true`, `{}`, `[]` | THREW `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` |

`env` is deliberately not in the set: Node accepts any `env` value, including `5` and
`"x"`, so a non-object `env` is not a call-site failure.

Only an exactly readable literal is decided; a binding, a call or a member read stays
undecided, because its value is not settled by this expression.

The test file is renamed from `spawn_stdio_literal` to `spawn_option_literals` because it
now covers all three members. 16 cases added; reverting this check fails 9 of them.
`src/domain/javascript`: 5124 to 5140 passing. `tsc` 0; `build` 0;
`npm run format:check` 0; `npm run lint` 0 errors.

* fix(javascript): read the stdio and path options by value, not by AST kind

Seven review findings, each measured on Node 24.22.1. All seven were real, and two of them
were removing real children.

**`execFile` does not forward `stdio`.** Async `execFile` never passes `options.stdio` to its
underlying `spawn`, so `execFile(process.execPath, ["-e", ""], {stdio: "bad"})` returns a
real child — `stdioMode` already forces it to `"default"`. The new filter rejected it anyway
and dropped the spawn plus its linked interactions. `execFile` is now exempt, like `exec`.

**A no-substitution template literal is the same string to Node.** `readExactJavaScriptLiteral`
already resolves it, but the filter tested `t.isStringLiteral`, so ``{stdio: `ipc`}`` kept a
spawn Node refuses while ``{cwd: `/tmp`}`` — a valid path — was rejected because the same
branch called `readExactJavaScriptLiteral` and treated any hit as a non-string. Both sides
now read the value and test its type:

| call | Node 24.22.1 |
| --- | --- |
| ``spawn(..., {stdio: `ipc`})`` | THREW `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` |
| ``spawn(..., {stdio: `pipe`})`` | child starts |
| ``spawn(..., {cwd: `/tmp`})`` | child starts |
| ``spawn(..., {argv0: `x`})`` | child starts |

**A shape the literal owner does not price still has a settled type.** `{cwd: 1n}`,
`{cwd: /x/}`, `{cwd: () => {}}`, `{cwd: class {}}` and `{cwd: new String("x")}` all throw
`ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`, and none matched the previous object/array/boolean arms.

**The `fork` explanation was wrong.** Node's `stdioStringToArray` rejects `stdio: ""` with an
explicit check before anything is appended; it does not split the string and it never builds
an IPC-only array. The rejection was right, the reason was not, so the comment now states the
real rule.

44 cases; reverting the `execFile` exemption fails 1, reverting the value-based read fails 1,
and reverting the extended non-string arms fails 6.
`src/domain/javascript`: 5158 to 5168 passing. `tsc` 0; `build` 0;
`npm run format:check` 0; `npm run lint` 0 errors.

* fix(javascript): keep a path-shaped cwd that Node accepts

`cwd` is a path, so Node takes a byte array or a file `URL` there, not only a string. The
blanket `NewExpression` arm rejected every constructor for both members, which dropped real
children.

Measured on Node 24.22.1, identical on `spawn`, `fork`, `execFile` and `exec`:

| `cwd` | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `new Uint8Array([47, 116, 109, 112])` | child starts |
| `new Buffer("/tmp")` | child starts |
| `new URL("file:///C:/tmp/")` | child starts |
| `new String("/tmp")`, `new Number(1)`, `new Foo("/tmp")` | THREW `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` |

`argv0` is different: it is an argument string only, so `new Uint8Array([120])` and
`new URL(...)` both throw there. `isPathConstructor` names the constructors that can produce
a path, and only `cwd` consults it.

`URL` stays undecided rather than accepted, because whether a file URL resolves is a
platform property: `new URL("file:///tmp/")` throws `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` on Windows
while a drive-qualified path does not. Syntax alone cannot settle that, so the answer is
left open instead of guessed.

8 cases added; reverting the arm fails 3 of them.
`src/domain/javascript`: 5168 to 5176 passing. `tsc` 0; `build` 0;
`npm run format:check` 0; `npm run lint` 0 errors.

commits.body:
fix(desktop): resolve desktop entry ids that name a nested entry (#9563)

* fix(desktop): resolve desktop entry ids that name a nested entry

The desktop file id of an entry below an applications folder replaces
the directory separators with dashes, so applications/vendor/foo.desktop
advertises vendor-foo.desktop. locateDesktopEntry only probed the flat
path, so such an entry was either not found or, when a lower-priority
XDG root installed a flat file with the same id, a different
application was launched under the requested id.

List each applications directory instead and form every entry's id from
the path that holds it, so a dash inside a directory name does not
change the answer. The walk is bounded and stops reporting absence once
it can no longer decide, so a truncated search refuses instead of
falling through to a lower-priority root.

* fix(desktop): search nested entry directories without skipping answers

Three defects in findNestedDesktopEntry, all of which could select a lower-priority application under the same desktop file id:

`readdir` failure was treated as an empty directory, so an applications root or nested directory that could not be listed silently yielded to a lower-priority root. Only ENOENT and ENOTDIR now mean the root is not installed; any other failure reports desktop_entry_search_incomplete.

A directory whose own name ends in `.desktop` was skipped before it was searched, so `vendor.desktop/app.desktop` (id `vendor.desktop-app.desktop`) was unreachable. The suffix now selects a candidate only for files; directories still descend.

The entry budget was applied after `readdir` had materialized every name, so a large directory allocated far more than the 4096 entries it may examine. The walk now enumerates with `opendir` and charges the budget per entry.

* fix(desktop): finish the reachable nested search before reporting a gap

An unreadable or over-budget subtree is not proof the entry is absent, but
returning truncated as soon as one was met stopped the walk before the
siblings that could still hold it. The entry then looked incomplete even
though this root could answer, so a lower-priority root was never consulted
and the search reported a gap instead of the entry.

* test(javascript): distinguish package scope in route fixtures

* test(apple): separate identity and refusal fixture groups

* fix(desktop): resolve only applicable desktop ID paths

* test(desktop): cover applicable probe failure before a matching spelling

commits.subject: feat(native): list ELF and Mach-O initializer and finalizer functions (#9574)
commits.body:
feat(native): list ELF and Mach-O initializer and finalizer functions (#9574)

* feat(native): list ELF and Mach-O initializer and finalizer functions

inspect_native_initializers and inspect-native-initializers list the
functions an ELF or Mach-O image runs before and after main: ELF
DT_INIT, DT_FINI, preinit, init and fini arrays and .ctors/.dtors, and
Mach-O __mod_init_func, __mod_term_func and __init_offsets, with slot
addresses, resolved targets, symbols where available and relocation
facts for relocatable objects. Nothing is executed. Slot, symbol,
relocation and note budgets are shared across tables, sentinels are
matched at the image width, and target-derived names are bounded and
marked untrusted.

* fix(native): keep ELF initializer slots unresolved when relocation coverage is partial

A skipped, unreadable or over-budget section relocation table now keeps
every slot it could reach unresolved instead of reading the stored word as
raw or dropping a .ctors slot as a sentinel. Dynamic writes that only
partly overlap a slot, or write it twice, leave it unresolved. Linked
images no longer reapply retained non-SHF_ALLOC link-time records.

The dynamic relocation walk now pauses at the shared reader's step
boundaries and observes cancellation there, resolved targets need only
their first byte mapped, and unreadable symbol names make the report
incomplete.

* fix(native): stop reporting unchecked Mach-O initializer words as resolved

Object files now apply their own section relocations: an UNSIGNED entry
against a defined symbol gives symbol_addend, one against an undefined
symbol gives unresolved_import, and any other entry leaves the slot
unresolved. Linked images without a fixup decoder, such as 32-bit ones,
keep pointer slots unresolved when an LC_DYLD_INFO bind stream or
LC_DYSYMTAB external relocations could replace the stored word.

LC_DYLD_INFO rebases now report dyld_info_rebase instead of
chained_fixup, and unreadable symbol names make the report incomplete.
Section headers keep their declared reloff and nreloc for this.

* docs(native): move initializer guide under docs/guides/native

The documentation guide assigns analyst workflows to docs/guides/<domain>/.
Move the guide there, place its navigation and directory entries in the
Native binaries group, and update links from the docs index, CLI guide,
spec and authored skill. The public /native-initializers route is
unchanged.

The guide and spec also describe per-slot relocation coverage, retained
link-time records, Mach-O object relocations, undecoded bind streams,
the dyld_info_rebase resolution and unreadable names.

* fix(native): keep IFUNC and partly relocated ELF initializer slots unresolved

An absolute relocation against an STT_GNU_IFUNC symbol no longer reports
the resolver address as the target. Section relocation records now use
their real write width, so a record that writes only part of a slot,
starts inside it or repeats it leaves the slot unresolved instead of
reading a raw zero or dropping a .ctors slot as a sentinel.

On 32-bit ARM the Thumb bit is cleared when locating a target's section
and file offset, while value_va keeps the stored callable value.

* fix(native): locate Thumb Mach-O initializer targets and reject arm64_32 with a 64-bit header

On CPU_TYPE_ARM the Thumb bit is cleared when locating and naming a
target, since nlist values do not carry it. An arm64_32 image that
declares a 64-bit header is rejected as malformed rather than read with
8-byte slots. The guide and spec describe IFUNC relocations, partly
relocated section slots, Thumb targets and this rejection.

* fix(native): index initializer address lookups and keep ambiguous mappings unknown

ELF and Mach-O initializer lookups now build the shared file mapping
index once per image, so each slot and target lookup is logarithmic in
the number of load segments rather than a scan of every mapping.

An address that load segments map ambiguously no longer falls back to a
section header offset. Its file offset is reported as unknown and the
report is incomplete; only genuinely unmapped spans use the section
fallback.

* fix(native): report Mach-O bind names over the name budget

A bound import name longer than the 1024-byte name budget was dropped
without a trace, although it is the only identity of an unresolved
initializer target. It now counts toward the over-long name limitation
and makes the report incomplete.

* test(native): count mapping lookups instead of timing the load index regression

The load-mapping regression asserted a wall-clock bound, which is
sensitive to machine load. It now spies on the shared mapping module and
requires the same number of mapping scans and index builds for 8 and 64
slots, so a per-slot scan of every load segment fails deterministically
on a small fixture.

* fix(native): yield while decoding legacy rebase runs

* fix(native): preserve initializer mapping and coverage

* fix(native): index legacy fixup spans

* fix(native): preserve relocation uncertainty and bound bind lookup work

* fix(native): validate ELF slot mappings and yield section relocation scans

commits.subject: fix(javascript): reject a tls protocol version Node refuses at the call site (#9557)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): reject a tls protocol version Node refuses at the call site (#9557)

* fix(javascript): reject a tls protocol version Node refuses at the call site

`tls.connect` resolves `minVersion`/`maxVersion` before it opens a socket, so a bad literal
throws from the call itself and no socket exists. The acquisition filter decided the port
only, so it reported a complete built-in resource for a call that throws.

Measured on Node 24.22.1:

| `minVersion` / `maxVersion` | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `"TLSv1"`, `"TLSv1.1"`, `"TLSv1.2"`, `"TLSv1.3"` | socket created |
| `null`, `undefined`, absent | socket created |
| `"TLSv1.0"`, `"tlsv1"`, `"tlsv1.2"`, `"TLSv1.4"`, `"nope"`, `""` | THREW `ERR_TLS_INVALID_PROTOCOL_VERSION` |
| `5`, `true`, `{}`, `[]` | THREW `ERR_TLS_INVALID_PROTOCOL_VERSION` |
| `1n` | THREW `TypeError` |

The accepted set is exact and case-sensitive, so it is a closed list rather than a pattern.
`net` ignores these members, so only `tls` is consulted. The member is read in write order,
which is why `{minVersion: "nope", minVersion: "TLSv1.2"}` keeps its acquisition; a spread,
a computed key or an accessor leaves the answer undecided rather than decided against.

22 cases, 11 failing before this commit. `src/domain/javascript`: 5040 to 5062 passing.
`tsc` 0; `build` 0; `npm run format:check` 0; `npm run lint` 0 errors; `knip` 0.

* fix(javascript): read every tls options slot and check both version members

Four review findings, each measured on Node 24.22.1. All four were real gaps in the first
version of this check.

**An accepted `minVersion` returned before `maxVersion` was read.** `tls.connect({port: 80,
minVersion: "TLSv1.2", maxVersion: "nope"})` throws, because both members are resolved
before the socket opens. The loop now continues past an accepted version and returns only
for a rejected one.

**Only argument zero was read.** `tls` also accepts `(port, options)`, `(port, host,
options)` and `(path, options)`, and all three throw on a bad version:
`tls.connect(443, {minVersion: "nope"})`, `tls.connect(443, "127.0.0.1", {minVersion:
"nope"})` and `tls.connect("/tmp/x.sock", {minVersion: "nope"})`. Every object literal in
the argument list is now read; a spread argument shifts those positions, so it leaves the
answer undecided instead of picking a wrong slot.

**A signed number was left unknown.** `minVersion: -1`, `+1` and `-0` all throw, but they
arrive as a `UnaryExpression` and matched none of the literal arms. `readExactJavaScriptLiteral`
already normalises `-1` and `+1`; `-0` is the one case it excludes, so a sign over a numeric
literal is decided explicitly here rather than treated as unknown.

13 cases added; reverting the slot and loop changes fails 4 of them.
`src/domain/javascript`: 5062 to 5075 passing. `tsc` 0; `build` 0;
`npm run format:check` 0; `npm run lint` 0 errors; `knip` 0.

* fix(javascript): merge the tls arguments and honour a supplied secure context

Four review findings, each measured on Node 24.22.1. All four were real: the previous
reader checked each object argument independently and ignored the context.

**Several object arguments merge in order, so the later one wins.** The reader rejected the
first object and stopped:

| call | Node 24.22.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `tls.connect({port: 443, minVersion: "nope"}, {minVersion: "TLSv1.2"})` | SOCKET |
| `tls.connect({port: 443, minVersion: "TLSv1.2"}, {minVersion: "nope"})` | THREW |
| `tls.connect({port: 443}, {minVersion: "nope"})` | THREW |

The members are now resolved across the whole argument list in write order, so a later
argument replaces an earlier one the way Node's merge does.

**A supplied `secureContext` bypasses version parsing entirely.** Node uses
`options.secureContext || tls.createSecureContext(options)`, so
`tls.connect({port: 80, secureContext: ctx, minVersion: "nope"})` connects while a `null`
context throws. An unreadable context leaves the answer undecided.

**An ordinary method member cannot install a version.** The reader skipped any object
containing a method, so `{checkServerIdentity() {}, minVersion: "nope"}` kept a socket
Node never creates. Only an accessor runs a body and leaves the member open; a plain method
is a value Node never reads as a version name. A `minVersion() {}` member is itself such a
value, so it rejects.

**Signed BigInt and function-shaped versions were left unknown.** `-1n`, `() => {}`,
`function () {}` and `class {}` are all truthy non-strings that Node refuses; none matched
an existing arm. They are now decided.

12 cases added; reverting the merge and context changes fails 2 of them and reverting the
method arm fails 6. `src/domain/javascript`: 5075 to 5087 passing. `tsc` 0; `build` 0;
`npm run format:check` 0; `npm run lint` 0 errors; `knip` 0.

* fix(javascript): read only the options slot tls.connect copies, and its accessors

Six review findings, each measured on Node 24.22.1. All six were real.

**A falsy `secureContext` does not bypass version parsing.** Node tests
`options.secureContext` for truth, so `{secureContext: false, minVersion: "nope"}`, and `0`
and `""` with it, all throw. The guard only recognised nullish syntax, so it dropped real
throws. `staticTruthiness` now decides the context: a known-falsy value keeps checking, a
known-truthy one ends the check, and an unreadable one stays undecided.

**Node copies at most one options object.** Measured:

| call | result |
| --- | --- |
| `(443, {minVersion: "TLSv1.2"}, {minVersion: "nope"})` | SOCKET — the third argument is ignored |
| `(443, {minVersion: "nope"}, {minVersion: "TLSv1.2"})` | THREW |
| `(443, "127.0.0.1", {minVersion: "nope"})` | THREW — the host fills slot 1 |
| `({port: 443, minVersion: "nope"}, {minVersion: "TLSv1.2"})` | SOCKET — the second object wins |

The reader treated every object argument as merged in order, which let an ignored object
decide. `tlsOptionsObjects` now models the two overloads: an object in slot 0 is merged with
slot 1, and a port or path in slot 0 makes the first object among slots 1 and 2 the only one
read.

**An exact computed key names the member.** `{["minVersion"]: "nope"}` throws, but the
reader marked every computed key unknown before the shared name resolver saw it. Only an
unresolvable key is unknown now, and the case that asserted the old behaviour uses a
binding key so it still covers the unknown path.

**An accessor can write the member first.** `{get side() { this.minVersion = "TLSv1.2"; },
minVersion: "nope"}` connects, because Node's own copy runs the getter before it reads
`minVersion`; and a `set minVersion` in an earlier argument absorbs the later write. Both
are bodies this reader does not run, so an accessor anywhere in the merged objects now
leaves every version member undecided. A plain method still rejects, since Node never reads
it as a version name.

**An unshadowed `NaN` or `Infinity` is a non-string version.** Both throw, and neither
matched an existing arm. They are decided the same way the adjacent port filter decides
them, through `isUnmodifiedGlobalReference`, so a shadowed binding stays unknown.

16 cases added; reverting the truthiness, accessor and computed-key changes fails 2 of them.
`src/domain/javascript`: 5075 to 5188 passing. `tsc` 0; `build` 0;
`npm run format:check` 0; `npm run lint` 0 errors.

* fix(javascript): use the nullable key owner and settle unary versions

Six review findings, each measured on Node 24.22.1. All six were real, and three of them
were removing real sockets.

**`semanticStaticPropertyName` encodes an unresolved key as `""`, never `undefined`.** The
guard tested `undefined`, so it never fired and an unresolved computed key was read as a
member literally named empty. `const k = "minVersion";
tls.connect({port: 443, minVersion: "nope", [k]: "TLSv1.2"})` connects on Node 24.22.1
because the later computed member wins, while the analysis filtered on the stale `"nope"`
and dropped the socket. `semanticStaticPropertyKey` is the nullable owner and is now used,
with `null` treated as unknown.

**A getter can replace a plain version method before Node copies it.** The method branch
ignored `accessorWritten`, so `{get side() { this.minVersion = "TLSv1.2"; }, minVersion()
{}}` still returned `"rejects"` although it connects. The same unknown result now applies to
methods when an accessor is present.

**A non-literal second argument is a merged options object, not an absent one.**
`const o = {minVersion: "TLSv1.2"}; tls.connect({port: 443, minVersion: "nope"}, o)`
connects. The slot reader mapped every non-object to `undefined`, so only the stale first
object was examined. A non-object in a copied slot now stays unknown.

**`-0` is falsy, so a signed-zero context does not bypass parsing.** The local truthiness
helper did not fold a unary `-`, so `{secureContext: -0, minVersion: "nope"}` was treated as
a possible bypass although it throws. The shared `staticJavaScriptTruthiness` owner already
handles signed zero and replaces the local helper, which is deleted.

**A unary operator over a settled operand is a settled non-string version.** `!0`, `!1`,
`~~0`, `!!0` and `typeof 1` all throw `ERR_TLS_INVALID_PROTOCOL_VERSION`; the previous arm
recognised only `+` and `-`, and the exact-literal and shape arms did not reach them.
`void <expr>` stays accepted, because it is `undefined`.

The slot reader also had to distinguish a host string in slot 1 from an options object, since
`tls.connect(443, "127.0.0.1", {minVersion: "nope"})` throws while
`tls.connect(443, {minVersion: "nope"})` is the two-slot form.

`src/domain/javascript`: 5188 to 5197 passing. Reverting the key owner fails 1 case and
reverting the unary arms fails 2. `tsc` 0; `build` 0; `npm run format:check` 0;
`npm run lint` 0 errors.

* test(javascript): distinguish package scope in route fixtures

* test(apple): separate identity and refusal fixture groups

* fix(javascript): share TLS option facts and preserve merge uncertainty

* fix(javascript): separate TLS assignment authority from copy facts

commits.subject: feat(desktop): install extra packages beside an archive app, and keep a package file's dependencies at export (#9112)
commits.body:
feat(desktop): install extra packages beside an archive app, and keep a package file's dependencies at export (#9112)

* fix(desktop): keep added-record checks off ids, dates, and joined timestamps

A position-named record's fields keep their paths, so an identifier, a stamped date, and text past the limit are not suggested checks. A whole-text check does not climb into an ancestor whose text joins a timestamp.

* fix(desktop): bound home fetches and keep unsettled edits readable

Split home-folder reads by the guest answer budget, keep a capacity error
from the capture output, and drop the superseded task-argument refusal.
Grade kept text per line, leave unretained dconf unread, and reserve
by-position notes for XML children. Map a linked database's sidecars
through the selected spelling and stop a detached capture only when its
start identity still owns the pid.

* fix(desktop): describe unretained dconf as unread

The key comparison treats a missing copy as unknown. The comment still
said that copy counted as an empty key list.

* test(desktop): keep a capture capacity error through endedCapture

An output past the guest answer ceiling stays the resource constraint,
with its heap recovery and non-retryable status, instead of a generic
capture-exit message.

* fix(desktop): keep nested save times and formatting runs out of checks

A field check drops save-time leaves before it joins the field, so a nested
timestamp is not part of the suggested text. A text check beside a save time
uses the paragraph when the diff names a formatting run.

* test(desktop): read paragraph pointers from checks that have them

* test(desktop): expect a large task to export intact

The 96 KiB refusal is gone. A prompt past that size reaches the computer
and comes back unchanged, instead of failing before export.

* fix(desktop): keep real edits that save-side heuristics were dropping

Repeated unnamed fields stay content checks. A formula that still has
text is not renumbered with its ExprID. One gained style attribute is
the edit; a repeated fill-in stays upkeep. Phone numbers and plain
clock times stay text, and a decimal is the element's whole text. An
older verifier matches on the task it states, not its evaluator source.

* fix(desktop): cover repeated records and keep timestamps out of checks

An added record whose words are already in the seed still gets the list's
text when that text fits. Readiness is a start reason, so a final check
names seed locks without matching the message. Field text split by a
timestamp stays separate, and a timestamp line is not offered as a guard.

* fix(desktop): compare a cell's joined decimal within tolerance

The whole-element check keeps numeric tolerance, so 437.80 and a long
float still match 437.8, including when a run splits the digits. A
different number or other text does not. Both evaluators read an
element's text for that comparison.

* fix(desktop): keep selected logs and stop treating unknown walks as complete

Match an app name as a whole token, treat an omitted unchecked_paths count as incomplete, seed Chromium user_prefs.json, and keep a caller-selected log even when that path is also a state directory. A log inside the app's own folder still marks that folder so settings beside it stay seeded, while a lock in the home does not. Sibling locks under a selected folder stay out unless that lock was the selected path.

* fix(desktop): grade a number from a complete XML element only

A tolerance check joins an element's text only in an XML file or an XML
archive entry, and leaves that check undecided when the view is cut, so a
dropped descendant cannot turn the kept runs into a passing number. A JSON
object with the same shape stays the value itself. Equivalent decimals and a
split run on a whole cell still match.

* fix(desktop): accept an older grader only when its index helper agrees

The witness still matches a bundle whose evaluator is this REA's, or the older
index expression alone when no path segment is a leading-zero number. A
truncated verifier, a changed grader, or that older helper beside a segment
such as 01 no longer counts as the same task.

* fix(desktop): keep a lone lock a document and drop one beside its file

A selected name such as notes.lck stays a document, so launch and the draft
still treat it as the caller's file. A lock beside a recorded sibling is left
out of the seed unless that lock path itself was selected.

* fix(desktop): require the added record and leave save times out of list checks

A record a selector names is checked itself, so its words have to be in that
record. When an unnamed record only repeats words the seed already has, a
list that holds a save time is checked by the text around that time. A later
save of the same records still passes, and a missing or rewritten record fails.

* fix(desktop): judge the older index helper by pointer segments only

A leading zero in a file name or a URL does not change how the older index
helper reads a pointer. The witness still rejects that helper when a pointer
segment is a number such as 01.

* fix(desktop): keep a document whose name ends in .lock

A lock beside a recorded file still stays out of the seed unless that lock
was selected. A document such as Cargo.lock in the home is the user's file,
so the seed keeps it. An application lock in the home, such as poedit.lock,
stays out.

* fix(desktop): do not suggest list text the seed already passes

A repeated record is shown by text the seed does not hold. The seed's own
text is not a check. A pointer inside a check value is not a pointer segment
for the older index helper.

* fix(desktop): do not let a left-out lock hide settings checks

A sibling lock the seed omits is not the document the draft follows. Settings
changes stay suggested. The unused sibling-lock name helper is removed.

* fix(desktop): keep a linked settings file in the folder the link points at

A selected ~/.config alias no longer moves MuseScore settings to that alias.
The seed keeps settings/MuseScore or Documents, which is the path the export
opens the note from.

* fix(desktop): split home fetches by answer size and keep a size refusal

A batch of tiny files stops before each path's envelope exceeds the host
answer budget. A capture output past that ceiling stays a resource error
instead of becoming a generic exit.

* fix(desktop): seed a selected link under the path the app uses

The selected spelling wins, so ~/.config/MuseScore is not rewritten to the
folder it points at and the note stays the one launched document. A database
wal and journal follow that database. A launch argument is respelled the same
way. Teardown signals a detached PID only when its start identity still matches.

* fix(desktop): keep a witness's actions and an incomplete checkpoint

A failed witness save retries the action log it first recorded. A deletion
left unconfirmed between the seed and the end is not reported as no change.
Windows packs npm through a shell, which can start npm.cmd.

* fix(desktop): read verifier pointers from the parsed checks

A brace inside a check value is not an object boundary. A leading-zero
pointer after that value still rejects the older index helper.

* fix(desktop): leave out a sibling lock under a selected folder

A file under a selected folder inherits selected_path. That does not make
the lock beside its map a chosen document, so a settings change stays drafted.

* fix(desktop): prefer the most specific home spelling and retarget launch files

A selected parent directory no longer hides a settings folder walked through
a link. A launch filename under that folder is replaced with the seeded
file's absolute path.

* fix(desktop): pack the build runtime through npm's JavaScript entry

npm pack and npm ci no longer spawn npm.cmd through a shell, so a temporary
directory whose path contains spaces stays one argument.

* fix(desktop): spell launch settings and keep a database log exact

A database log matches only that file, so a neighboring folder is not moved.
A launch option and the working directory use the same home spelling as the seed.

* fix(desktop): draft a lock the export selected exactly

The draft uses the same selected paths as the export. A lock chosen by
itself stays in the draft. A lock under a selected folder stays out.

* fix(desktop): move a state database's logs with the database

The write-ahead log and journal follow the spelling the database received,
including a walked state link. A neighboring folder stays put. A separate
--config argument uses that spelling too.

* fix(desktop): keep a selected file ahead of a database-log guess

A file selected as itself keeps that spelling even when its name ends in
-journal. Relative launch arguments are resolved in the captured working
directory before that directory moves.

* fix(desktop): keep outside-home database logs and option values

A selected database outside the home keeps its write-ahead log. Launch
options are rewritten only when they name a captured file or settings path.

* fix(desktop): follow a database mapping and own limitation text

A selected database keeps its log when a parent folder moves or the file
sits outside the home. Trash and seed-lock tests compare the owning notice
with the paths, and launch options that are not captured paths stay as written.

* fix(desktop): retarget a settings folder that holds captured files

A nested profile directory is a captured path when a seeded file is inside
it. An option value that only resolves under the home stays as written.

* fix(desktop): keep a program word and a directory's neighbor

The program after env stays the program even when a captured file sits in a
folder of that name. A selected directory is not a database, so a neighboring
file keeps the parent folder's spelling.

* fix(desktop): record whether a selected path is a directory

Capture stores the walked path's kind. A neighboring file of a selected
directory keeps the parent folder's spelling even when that directory never
changes and its children are not content roots.

* fix(desktop): mark containing paths without a pairwise scan

A recorded path marks its known ancestors as directories in one walk up
the path, instead of comparing every recorded path with every other.

* fix(desktop): keep a selected folder that is named like a database log

A folder the caller selected stays a selected root when its name ends in
-journal or -wal. A generated log beside a database file still does not.

* fix(desktop): refuse a build command that exceeds the argument vector

Splitting one argument still leaves the whole command under Linux's E2BIG
limit. A request past that budget is refused before the process starts.

* fix(desktop): remap a captured path in an env assignment

The program word stays the program. A NAME=value assignment keeps its name
and follows a captured path value when that path's spelling moves.

* fix(desktop): keep oversized text out of draft guards

A value or line longer than the draft's text bound is not copied into a
guard, so one large frame cannot fill the task by itself.

* fix(desktop): keep an empty env value empty

An empty assignment is not a path. Resolving it named the working directory
and rewrote the value when that directory's spelling moved.

* fix(desktop): check build runtime export capability

* fix(desktop): provide complete runtime repack command

* fix(desktop): retain runtime probe failures

* test(desktop): identify capture independently of schema preflight

feat(desktop): check text kept in attributes, name a record by a child's text, and count members (#9114)

* fix(desktop): keep a lone lock a document and drop one beside its file

A selected name such as notes.lck stays a document, so launch and the draft
still treat it as the caller's file. A lock beside a recorded sibling is left
out of the seed unless that lock path itself was selected.

* fix(desktop): require the added record and leave save times out of list checks

A record a selector names is checked itself, so its words have to be in that
record. When an unnamed record only repeats words the seed already has, a
list that holds a save time is checked by the text around that time. A later
save of the same records still passes, and a missing or rewritten record fails.

* fix(desktop): judge the older index helper by pointer segments only

A leading zero in a file name or a URL does not change how the older index
helper reads a pointer. The witness still rejects that helper when a pointer
segment is a number such as 01.

* fix(desktop): keep a document whose name ends in .lock

A lock beside a recorded file still stays out of the seed unless that lock
was selected. A document such as Cargo.lock in the home is the user's file,
so the seed keeps it. An application lock in the home, such as poedit.lock,
stays out.

* fix(desktop): do not suggest list text the seed already passes

A repeated record is shown by text the seed does not hold. The seed's own
text is not a check. A pointer inside a check value is not a pointer segment
for the older index helper.

* fix(desktop): do not let a left-out lock hide settings checks

A sibling lock the seed omits is not the document the draft follows. Settings
changes stay suggested. The unused sibling-lock name helper is removed.

* fix(desktop): keep a linked settings file in the folder the link points at

A selected ~/.config alias no longer moves MuseScore settings to that alias.
The seed keeps settings/MuseScore or Documents, which is the path the export
opens the note from.

* fix(desktop): split home fetches by answer size and keep a size refusal

A batch of tiny files stops before each path's envelope exceeds the host
answer budget. A capture output past that ceiling stays a resource error
instead of becoming a generic exit.

* fix(desktop): seed a selected link under the path the app uses

The selected spelling wins, so ~/.config/MuseScore is not rewritten to the
folder it points at and the note stays the one launched document. A database
wal and journal follow that database. A launch argument is respelled the same
way. Teardown signals a detached PID only when its start identity still matches.

* fix(desktop): keep a witness's actions and an incomplete checkpoint

A failed witness save retries the action log it first recorded. A deletion
left unconfirmed between the seed and the end is not reported as no change.
Windows packs npm through a shell, which can start npm.cmd.

* fix(desktop): read verifier pointers from the parsed checks

A brace inside a check value is not an object boundary. A leading-zero
pointer after that value still rejects the older index helper.

* fix(desktop): leave out a sibling lock under a selected folder

A file under a selected folder inherits selected_path. That does not make
the lock beside its map a chosen document, so a settings change stays drafted.

* fix(desktop): prefer the most specific home spelling and retarget launch files

A selected parent directory no longer hides a settings folder walked through
a link. A launch filename under that folder is replaced with the seeded
file's absolute path.

* fix(desktop): pack the build runtime through npm's JavaScript entry

npm pack and npm ci no longer spawn npm.cmd through a shell, so a temporary
directory whose path contains spaces stays one argument.

* fix(desktop): spell launch settings and keep a database log exact

A database log matches only that file, so a neighboring folder is not moved.
A launch option and the working directory use the same home spelling as the seed.

* fix(desktop): draft a lock the export selected exactly

The draft uses the same selected paths as the export. A lock chosen by
itself stays in the draft. A lock under a selected folder stays out.

* fix(desktop): move a state database's logs with the database

The write-ahead log and journal follow the spelling the database received,
including a walked state link. A neighboring folder stays put. A separate
--config argument uses that spelling too.

* fix(desktop): keep a selected file ahead of a database-log guess

A file selected as itself keeps that spelling even when its name ends in
-journal. Relative launch arguments are resolved in the captured working
directory before that directory moves.

* fix(desktop): keep outside-home database logs and option values

A selected database outside the home keeps its write-ahead log. Launch
options are rewritten only when they name a captured file or settings path.

* fix(desktop): follow a database mapping and own limitation text

A selected database keeps its log when a parent folder moves or the file
sits outside the home. Trash and seed-lock tests compare the owning notice
with the paths, and launch options that are not captured paths stay as written.

* fix(desktop): retarget a settings folder that holds captured files

A nested profile directory is a captured path when a seeded file is inside
it. An option value that only resolves under the home stays as written.

* fix(desktop): keep a program word and a directory's neighbor

The program after env stays the program even when a captured file sits in a
folder of that name. A selected directory is not a database, so a neighboring
file keeps the parent folder's spelling.

* fix(desktop): record whether a selected path is a directory

Capture stores the walked path's kind. A neighboring file of a selected
directory keeps the parent folder's spelling even when that directory never
changes and its children are not content roots.

* fix(desktop): mark containing paths without a pairwise scan

A recorded path marks its known ancestors as directories in one walk up
the path, instead of comparing every recorded path with every other.

* fix(desktop): keep a selected folder that is named like a database log

A folder the caller selected stays a selected root when its name ends in
-journal or -wal. A generated log beside a database file still does not.

* fix(desktop): refuse a build command that exceeds the argument vector

Splitting one argument still leaves the whole command under Linux's E2BIG
limit. A request past that budget is refused before the process starts.

* fix(desktop): remap a captured path in an env assignment

The program word stays the program. A NAME=value assignment keeps its name
and follows a captured path value when that path's spelling moves.

* fix(desktop): keep oversized text out of draft guards

A value or line longer than the draft's text bound is not copied into a
guard, so one large frame cannot fill the task by itself.

* docs(desktop): correct dconf and check-preview guidance

A dconf version kept without its bytes is unreadable, not an empty key
list. A values preview is copied into a check only when it is an uncut scalar.

* fix(desktop): keep an empty env value empty

An empty assignment is not a path. Resolving it named the working directory
and rewrote the value when that directory's spelling moved.

feat(desktop): name a record by a nested field or a child's attribute (#9185)

* fix(desktop): keep a selected folder that is named like a database log

A folder the caller selected stays a selected root when its name ends in
-journal or -wal. A generated log beside a database file still does not.

* fix(desktop): refuse a build command that exceeds the argument vector

Splitting one argument still leaves the whole command under Linux's E2BIG
limit. A request past that budget is refused before the process starts.

* fix(desktop): remap a captured path in an env assignment

The program word stays the program. A NAME=value assignment keeps its name
and follows a captured path value when that path's spelling moves.

* fix(desktop): keep oversized text out of draft guards

A value or line longer than the draft's text bound is not copied into a
guard, so one large frame cannot fill the task by itself.

* docs(desktop): correct dconf and check-preview guidance

A dconf version kept without its bytes is unreadable, not an empty key
list. A values preview is copied into a check only when it is an uncut scalar.

* fix(desktop): keep an empty env value empty

An empty assignment is not a path. Resolving it named the working directory
and rewrote the value when that directory's spelling moved.

* fix(desktop): keep a run's font on the run, not the frame's text

A formatting attribute such as Scribus FONT is not the document's words.
Joining it across runs made a frame-wide text check of ItalicBold that
failed when a run was split. The font stays a value check on its own run.

* fix(desktop): do not pair JSON records by a selector-shaped field

A field named @record_id matched the id suffix and became [@record_id=one],
which reads an XML attribute. Records paired while their pointers matched
nothing. Names that start with @ or > are not id fields.

* fix(desktop): count a save-numbered id once when pairing members

xml:id and draw:id values such as id123456 were both generated and
numbered, so the same selector was counted twice and refused. A text
edit of two elements keyed only by those ids now keeps its check.

The boundary match for a secret cut short hid the start of any ellipsis-ended
text, so "Please…" became a redaction. It now applies only where text ends
one of REA's value cuts, whose lengths the producers and the redactor share,

fix(ci): restore main workflows and captured-state replay (#9763)

* fix(cli): record the caller HAR path in environment-build evidence

environment-build inspected a HAR without the caller path that
inspect-web-network-capture records, so the published evidence.json
omitted caller_input_path and failed the byte-for-byte portable check.

Also update three stale portable expectations that already fail on main:
the no-reader verifier digest matches the #9185 selector parent, uncapped
IDA callee pages report complete discovery, and a CLI refusal of a
malformed artifact inspection includes the undelivered source closure.

* fix: restore portable docs, alias, offset, and Windows cleanup checks

The witness page linked task anchors that were never written, so any
docs-touching PR failed the route check. A selected state directory was
restored as a dangling symlink by a duplicated helper. An empty
safetensors file reports the extent as outside the file before offset
conversion. Windows cleanup refusal uses the runtime's in-progress message.

* fix(cli): keep the caller's HAR spelling in environment-build evidence

inspect-web-network-capture records the path the caller typed. The
one-shot build had already absolutized that path, so a relative capture
disagreed with the three-step bundle. The byte-for-byte check now runs
from the capture directory and requires caller_input_path grafana.har.

* fix(desktop): create alias targets only for directory selections

A missing settings file was created as a directory because the helper
treated any absent path as a directory. The capture's selected path kind
now travels with the alias, and only a directory alias creates its target.
An absent file alias stays a file the app can create.

* fix(desktop): keep legacy alias kind unknown

Captures written before selected_paths.kind leave the alias unknown.
Defaulting those to a directory makes an omitted settings file a
directory, so a later write through the alias fails with EISDIR.

* fix(desktop): keep alias kind a file, directory, or unknown

The export plan was widening a missing selected path kind to string.
Record file or directory only when the capture says so, and unknown otherwise.

* fix(desktop): narrow a missing alias kind to unknown

The selected path kind was widened to string, so the export plan could
not keep the file, directory, or unknown distinction.

* test(desktop): expect alias kind in the rendered app module

The export now records whether a selected alias is a directory. The
rendered STATE_ALIASES tuples include that kind.

* fix(ghidra): reject an oversized Windows TCP endpoint as invalid

The POSIX read maps a record past the compact endpoint bound to
"Ghidra TCP endpoint is invalid". The Windows lease reported that same
bound as a generic observation failure, so an expanded endpoint failed
the Windows lane with a different message.

* fix(desktop): create a legacy alias when a child proves it is a directory

A capture written before selected path kind can still nest one alias
inside another. That parent is a directory. A legacy leaf stays unknown
so a missing settings file is not created as a directory.

* fix(desktop): restore selected aliases when the app owns no files

An empty state directory does not become an owned path, so the class
was ownless and never called _ensure_state_aliases. The ownless class
now restores aliases whenever the export recorded some.

* fix(desktop): create the parent of a missing file alias

A file alias must stay a file. When its parent directory was not seeded,
the symlink was dangling and a write through it failed with ENOENT.

* ci: retrigger checks after an unrelated Windows timeout

The Windows lane timed out in webModuleCli, which this diff does not touch,
and the rerun API is unavailable.

* test(evidence): preserve complete CLI refusal diagnostics

fix(cli): refuse an unsupported Node.js release before linking (#9297)

* fix(cli): refuse an unsupported Node.js release before linking

The dispatcher imported the compiled runtime before checking the runtime
range, so a release outside `engines.node` failed while linking a module
that imports `createZstdDecompress`. Callers saw a module-linking stack
trace from every command, including `--version` and `doctor`, instead of
the refusal the installer and `engines` already promise.

Check `engines.node` from the package read the dispatcher already performs,
before the first compiled import. The helper has no imports of its own: the
dispatcher must admit the runtime before any dependency can be resolved.

Fixes #9296

* fix(cli): ship and align runtime admission

* fix(ci): cover packaged runtime admission helper

* test(cli): assert Node admission with structured range results

Export satisfiesNodeRange and cover caret, minimum, union, and
non-release versions. The dispatcher proves the compiled runtime never
loads by the absence of its marker file, and compares stderr to the
helper's own message.

commits.subject: fix(cli): publish partial Evidence to --evidence_output on failure (#7797)
commits.body:
fix(cli): publish partial Evidence to --evidence_output on failure (#7797)

* fix(cli): publish partial Evidence to --evidence_output on failure

publishCliAnalysisEvidence returned a failed result unchanged before any
--evidence_output handling. When a source reached its deadline, or another
failure carried partial Evidence, the requested file was not written and
--detail summary still printed the complete partial Evidence inline, which
reached more than 64 MB on a large build.

A failure whose details.partial_observation is authenticated Evidence now
publishes it through the same projection and new-file publication as a
successful result. The failure keeps its code, message and remediation.
With --detail summary, details.partial_observation holds the summary
view, and details.diagnostics.evidence_bundle reports the path and bytes.
A refused publication keeps the complete partial Evidence inline and adds
details.diagnostics.evidence_bundle_error with the refusal and a
limitation. Without --evidence_output, for cancellation, and for raw
provider observations the failure output is unchanged.

Fixes #7787

* fix(cli): keep committed partial Evidence receipts on refused publication

When publishing the partial Evidence of a failed analysis, a refusal can
follow a commit. Staging cleanup that stays incomplete after its retry
returns cleanup_incomplete with published_path and bytes, and a
cancellation after commit returns cancelled with
diagnostics.evidence_bundle. The failure path read only the second form,
so a committed file with incomplete cleanup was reported as not
published, without its receipt or the cleanup resources, and the full
partial Evidence went back inline.

Keep the original analysis failure and record the receipt from either
form in details.diagnostics.evidence_bundle. Incomplete publication
cleanup adds published, published_path, bytes, cleanup and resources to
details, the shape a successful run's cleanup_incomplete reports;
resources join any the analysis failure already reports, and its own
cleanup reason is kept. Once the file is committed, the delivered view
(the summary with --detail summary) replaces the inline partial Evidence.
Receipts omit a path that holds an excluded sensitive value, as on
success.

Tests drive the real staged publication through its commit point: cleanup
that stays incomplete, cleanup confirmed by retry, and SIGINT after
commit. A composition test checks receipt redaction on the failure path.

* fix(cli): report incomplete partial publication cleanup

commits.subject: fix(windows): leave a shortcut icon comparison unknown across code pages (#9691)
commits.body:
fix(windows): leave a shortcut icon comparison unknown across code pages (#9691)

* fix(windows): leave a shortcut icon comparison unknown across code pages

Windows stores the LinkInfo LocalBasePath only as ANSI when the system
code page can represent it, while StringData stays UTF-16. The parser
projects the ANSI bytes as Latin1, so on a code page 936 host a path such
as F:\百度网盘\BaiduNetdisk\BaiduNetdisk.exe never matched the same
Unicode IconLocation, and icon_location_differs_from_target reported true
for a shortcut whose icon is its own target.

Record whether each target path is an ANSI projection. Compare it with
the icon only when both use the same encoding or the ANSI text is ASCII.
A full target that cannot be compared makes the result null, like a
%VAR% target.

* fix(windows): keep each LinkInfo part's encoding when joining paths

A joined LinkInfo target was marked ANSI when any part was ANSI. An ASCII
ANSI share with a UTF-16 suffix such as \\server\share + 工具\app.exe
then could not be compared with a Unicode icon, although no byte needs a
code page. Record which encoding each part's non-ASCII text came from,
and compare two paths when their non-ASCII text shares one encoding.

commits.subject: fix(elf): report the link-time kernel banner, not the kbuild placeholder (#9690)
commits.body:
fix(elf): report the link-time kernel banner, not the kbuild placeholder (#9690)

Since Linux 6.1, kbuild compiles init/version.o with a temporary
UTS_VERSION. Its build number and timestamp stay empty unless
KBUILD_BUILD_VERSION or KBUILD_BUILD_TIMESTAMP is set. That weak
linux_banner stays in the image ahead of the banner from
init/version-timestamp.o, and the first-match scan reported it. The WSL
6.18 kernel showed '# SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC ' instead of
'#1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue Oct  6 19:13:07 UTC 2026'.

Treat a banner with a space right after '#' or at its end as the
placeholder. Keep scanning and report a later banner that repeats its
text up to '#' and is not a placeholder. Report the placeholder when no
such banner follows.

commits.subject: feat(artifacts): inventory NTFS $MFT record headers offline
commits.body:
feat(artifacts): inventory NTFS $MFT record headers offline

An acquired $MFT stream had no reader, so an analyst holding one could only
treat it as an opaque file. Recognize the FILE signature of the first record
and inventory every record's header: sequence number, flags, used and total
bytes, base record reference and update-sequence array.

Each record's update-sequence fixups are verified against its sector
trailers. A mismatch keeps the header facts, is reported on the record and is
counted in the metadata, so a record that was not cleanly written is visible
rather than silently accepted. A missing or short array is reported as
unverified, a wrong signature stops the scan at its offset, and a trailing
partial record is reported as a byte count. Attributes, filenames and the
$UsnJrnl:$J journal are not decoded, so no path or change history is claimed.

Part of #9867

(cherry picked from commit ccb45f5712ebd1c3f5653fe0c61f6aa33d22935b)

commits.subject: fix(targets): admit distinct host slices and one-sided digests (#10016)
commits.body:
fix(targets): admit distinct host slices and one-sided digests (#10016)

* fix(targets): select a preferred Mach-O host subtype

Host admission refused every extra slice of the host CPU type, so arm64
plus arm64e and arm64e ABI variants never became universal targets. Rank
known subtypes and keep the earliest capability variant. Identical
subtypes and ties between unlisted bases still fail closed.

* fix(artifacts): treat a one-sided declared digest as metadata

An all-zero Godot MD5 was visible only because limitation text differed.
After comparison stopped using that prose, a claim on one side and no
claim on the other lost its metadata dimension. Compare the structured
integrity claim instead.

* fix(browser): keep unavailable resource inventories unknown

Directional coverage treated a resource retained from an invalid protocol
tree as an addition against a complete peer. An unavailable collection is
not a truncated sample, so it cannot prove membership.

* fix(native): read the admitted Mach-O slice for metadata

Capability-variant admission chose the first slice, then dispatch
metadata and slice tools ranked the FAT file again and rejected that
pair. Pass the admitted offset, and refuse a winner set that repeats
a subtype.

commits.subject: fix(scripts): validate package-map ownership and preserve HTML fallback (#10097)
commits.body:
fix(scripts): validate package-map ownership and preserve HTML fallback (#10097)

* fix(website): keep the HTML validator when the Markdown route is absent

A caller that prefers Markdown gets the HTML probe with its conditional headers
deleted, so the Markdown route can be evaluated on its own. When the Markdown
sidecar is missing the worker answers with that probe, which never saw the
caller's `If-None-Match`, so a matching HTML ETag returned 200 instead of 304.

Ask the asset service again with the caller's own request before answering with
HTML. The decision moves into `htmlFallback` so the request handler keeps its
complexity below the repository bound.

Verified by executing `node --test website/worker.test.mjs`: without the change
the new case fails with 200 instead of 304, and all four cases pass with it.
`oxlint` reports no findings and `oxfmt --check` passes. The website worker test
is not part of a CI workflow, so this suite runs locally only.

* fix(scripts): resolve package-map imports in the module-boundary guard

The guard resolved only relative, absolute and `file:` specifiers, so every
`#`-prefixed package-map import returned no target and was skipped. A pure-layer
file importing `#javascript-analysis-worker` passed, while the same import
written relatively failed with a `pure-layer` diagnostic: the gate failed open
on the spelling the package map exists to encourage.

Resolve a package-map specifier to the source file that produces its built
output, then apply the same ownership rules. The package map is read once per
repository root.

Verified with the new `scripts/lib/module-boundaries.test.mjs` (2 pass; the
package-map case failed before the change) and by running the complete guard on
this checkout, which still reports 4138 files with no findings, so the new rule
adds no false positive. `oxfmt --check` passes; `oxlint` reports the same single
pre-existing `failedBoundary` complexity warning it reported before this change.
The script tests are not part of a CI workflow, so this suite runs locally only.

* fix(scripts): normalize package targets as file URLs

commits.subject: feat(audit): report what a shipped app exposes to static analysis (#8525)
commits.body:
feat(audit): report what a shipped app exposes to static analysis (#8525)

* feat(audit): report what a shipped app exposes to static analysis

Adds `audit_release_exposure` and `rea audit-release-exposure` to report
source maps, Electron fuse implications, extractable payloads, debug
information, build metadata, and credential markers. Checks carry stable
IDs, observations, statuses, and fixed remediation, while incomplete and
unassessed checks remain visible without implying a security verdict.
Credential findings include only rule IDs and locations. The CLI
supports `--fail_on` severity thresholds and exits 3 when an exposed
check meets the threshold.

* fix(audit): keep incomplete coverage unknown across text, fuses, Go flags and cancellation

Probe files with unrecognized names as text, keep undecided fuse slices
unknown, forward opaque container coverage, read paths from Go build flags,
and compare inventoried digests before accepting owner facts.

Keep typed cleanup failures and attach the partial report when a later owner
is cancelled. Pin the verifier's @electron/fuses version and move the tests
to the named contract family.

* fix(audit): match package members by source spelling and close remaining coverage gaps

Reopen package members by their source spelling and keep caller path
traversal in directory reads. Parse quoted and attached Go build flags, bind a
native image fuse read to its own digest, and keep reader resources and the
audit's partial report when cleanup or cancellation combine failures.

* fix(release-exposure): bind package members by ordinal and follow named map references

Package members were matched to container entries by sourcePath, which is
not unique in a PyInstaller executable, through a queue that only moved when
a member was reopened. Bind by container-relative path and duplicate ordinal,
the numbering inventory uses, so read order cannot change which bytes a
member gets.

A sourceMappingURL naming a file without a map extension was ignored. Local
targets are now examined as maps whatever their name, and a target already
scanned as plain text leaves coverage unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): match data: source map scheme case-insensitively

URL schemes are case-insensitive, so an inline declaration such as
//# sourceMappingURL=DATA:application/json;base64,... was routed to the
local-reference path, which ignores scheme URLs. Its embedded sources were
silently dropped and source_map_sources reported not_observed.

* fix(release-exposure): normalize declared map targets and count unreached ones

A sourceMappingURL that decodes to a decomposed name (cafe%CC%81.json)
never matched the inventoried member, whose logical path is NFC, so the
map was scanned as ordinary text and its sourcesContent went uncounted.
Map-target lookups now use an NFC key on both the record and lookup
side; the declared URL is left as written.

A declared map target that is never reached is now counted as a skipped
map, so the source-map checks read as unknown coverage instead of
not_observed.

* fix(release-exposure): recover indexed leaves after any map format failure

An indexed map whose one leaf has malformed mappings (such as AA) threw a
format failure that only recovered leaves for unsupported sections, so a
valid sibling leaf with sourcesContent was dropped and
javascript.source_map_sources read unknown instead of exposed. Leaves are
now recovered for any format failure, with the envelope parse guarded so
invalid JSON still falls through to the unparsed count.

A nested package that inventory recognized but did not expand was probed
as a plain binary and left the source-map checks at not_observed. It now
marks coverage unknown and records a limitation.

Reader tests assert the javascript.source_map_sources status for the NFC
map-name cases as well.

* fix(release-exposure): count an unexpanded nested package as a readable member

An unencrypted nested package that inventory recognized but did not
expand is still a member its parent package already read. Count it as
readable so packaging.extractable_payload reports exposed, while its
own contents keep coverage unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): bound the indexed leaf fallback by decoder limits

The fallback walk after a map format failure expanded every section and
built a full ancestor path per leaf, so a map refused for nesting depth
could still allocate far past the decoder budgets. Walk only to the
64-level section depth and the shared record budget, keeping leaf maps
without materializing section paths.

* fix(release-exposure): collect UNC roots from Go flag paths

A flag such as -I\\buildhost\sdk\include matched none of the path roots
in GO_FLAG_PATH, so a network path that was the only one in complete
build info left go.build_paths at not_observed. Accept \\host\share
roots alongside the slash-rooted, dot-relative and drive-letter forms.

* fix(release-exposure): keep Electron undecided without positive proof

The desktop owner names Electron only from an ASAR layout, so an asar: false
build has no candidate. A complete scan with no candidate was reported as
not_electron, which outranks unresolved and safe fuse outcomes and hid them
as not_applicable.

Leave the family unknown unless the fuse holder rules Electron out: an app
bundle with no Electron Framework, or a directory with complete coverage
whose native images were all read and hold no sentinel. A directory with no
native image is not proof, so its fuse checks now report unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): decode wide text members before scanning

A member's kind bypassed the NUL guard, so a UTF-16 plist was decoded as
UTF-8, matched nothing and still counted as scanned. A directory holding
only that member reported text.credential_markers as not_observed.

Decode by byte order mark at one boundary instead. UTF-16 is scanned in
either byte order, and inline maps read the same text. UTF-32 and NULs no
mark explains count as skipped, whatever the member's kind. A binary
plist keeps its raw scan. Unnamed members with a mark now reach the
scanner, and the plist decoder shares the same mark detection.

* fix(release-exposure): follow file: URL source map declarations

The scheme guard in noteLocalMapReference returned on every URL scheme, so
a declaration such as file:///release/debug.json was dropped with the remote
ones. A member without a .map name was then scanned as ordinary text and
javascript.source_map_sources reported not_observed.

Convert file: URLs with fileURLToPath and record them in mapTargets through
the same step as relative declarations. A target that is never reached, or
that was already scanned as text, counts as skipped, and so does a malformed
file: URL. A file: URL names one absolute location, so a .map target outside
the inventory stays unassessed rather than being trusted by its name. Remote
schemes stay ignored.

* fix(release-exposure): match backslash-relative Go flag paths

GO_FLAG_PATH accepted dot-relative roots only with a forward slash, so
`-I..\sdk\include` and `-I.\sdk` produced no path and go.build_paths came
back not_observed. Accept either separator after the dots.

The CLI acceptance test now expects unknown for electron.run_as_node on a
directory with no native images, matching the service.

* fix(release-exposure): keep fuses unknown on incomplete inventory

A directory inventory that stops at an acquisition limit never reports
the images it did not reach, so the native image sample has no omission
and safe fuses on an included helper settled to not_observed even though
scan coverage was unknown.

Treat unknown coverage like a truncated sample until the Electron
executable is accounted for. A selected native file is that executable,
so it keeps its decided fuse result.

* fix(release-exposure): decode binary plists before scanning

A binary plist stores each string as ASCII or UTF-16BE. Scanning the raw
bytes as UTF-8 missed any string the encoder kept in UTF-16, such as one
with a non-ASCII character, and still counted the member as fully
scanned, so text.credential_markers read not_observed.

Decode through the plist owner and scan its strings, dictionary keys and
data. A plist that cannot be decoded keeps its raw bytes in the scan and
counts as skipped, so coverage stays unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): keep UTF-8 members that hold a NUL

Any NUL in a member's first 512 bytes made the decoder give up, so a script
with a literal NUL in a string never reached the credential or inline-map
checks. An exposed marker in it read as unknown, and --fail_on high exited 0.

Validity alone cannot tell wide text from UTF-8, since ASCII in UTF-16 is
valid UTF-8. Treat a header that is an eighth or more NUL bytes as wide text
and anything not UTF-8 as undecoded, and scan the rest.

The docs now separate BOM-marked UTF-16, which is scanned, from wide text
with no byte order mark, which is not.

* fix(audit): scan every string a binary plist stores

The plist scan read only the decoded value, which drops objects the root no
longer references and entries a later duplicate key replaced. Those bytes
still ship, but the audit marked the scan complete, so a credential stored
there read as not observed and --fail_on high exited 0.

Read strings, keys and data from the object table instead. A stored object
that cannot be read leaves the member unassessed, and a total byte budget
bounds table entries that overlap to repeat the same text.

* fix(audit): keep packaged native images from ruling out Electron

The applicability check only looked at the "native images" omission. An
Electron executable inside a compressed .NET or PyInstaller member is recorded
under "packaged native images", so a directory whose on-disk hosts had no fuse
sentinel read as not Electron and all four fuse checks as not applicable.

Treat that omission as an unread image too.

* fix(audit): keep readable plist text when one object is unreadable

Throwing on one unreadable stored object discarded every string already
decoded, so a UTF-16BE credential beside a truncated unused object was lost:
the raw bytes that replaced it cannot match NUL-separated text.

Return the decoded text with complete false instead, and keep the raw bytes
in the scan beside it so ASCII in the unread object is still seen. The member
stays unassessed. Text past the budget ends the same way.

* fix(audit): read escaped inline maps and extensionless SEA entries

A data URL may percent-escape its base64 payload, so a map such as one padded
with %3D did not decode and the audit counted no embedded source map. Decode
the escapes before reading the base64.

A directory walk classed a SEA entry by its code path, so a main script whose
code path names no script was never scanned as JavaScript and its inline map
went unseen. Class it by the role the SEA metadata gives it.

* fix(audit): check plist text against the budget before decoding it

decodeBinaryPlistText decoded each stored object before comparing its size
with the remaining budget, and it keeps going after an object is rejected so
later text is still read. A plist under the input limit could repeat a large
range through overlapping table entries and force gigabytes of decoding that
the audit then discarded.

Separate finding a stored payload from decoding it, so a range past the
remaining budget is rejected without allocating its text. Earlier text and
the incomplete result stay as they were.

* fix(audit): count a packaged PE with an unread header as a native image

A package member whose PE signature lies beyond the 4 KiB probe recorded only
a PDB failure. The image was neither read nor listed under packaged native
images, so a directory whose on-disk hosts had no fuse sentinel read as not
Electron and all four fuse checks as not applicable.

Count it as a packaged native image, the omission that keeps the question
open, and keep probing it for text as before.

* fix(audit): keep cleanup-incomplete errors from composed readers

A desktop, fuse, Go or Rust failure became a string on that check, so an
error with unfinished cleanup lost its resources and live bindings while the
audit reported success, and the MCP handler does not close the service after
each request.

Treat unfinished cleanup like cancellation: stop the remaining owners and
return the error with the partial audit. When the owner attached its own
partial, keep the error and replace the partial, so cleanup stays attributed.

* fix(audit): keep safe fuses unknown past a packaged native image

The fuse check counted sampled-out images as possibly unread but not native
images inside a package. A complete directory scan with a safe-fuse image on
disk, no ASAR hint, and an unopened packaged image reported the four Electron
checks as not_observed, although the Electron executable could be that image.

The fuse check, the Go and Rust checks, and the Electron rule-out each decided
this for themselves and had drifted apart. Move the decision to one domain
predicate, nativeImagesMayBeUnread, and use it in all three. A hinted
executable that was read still settles the check.

* fix(audit): settle fuses only on an identified host, and read Bun and HTML maps

A retained helper set electron_executable_included because the rank marks
every .exe or extensionless sibling of resources/app.asar. With more than four
siblings, or an inventory that stopped early, safe fuses on a helper reported
not_observed while the host went unread. Rank stays a sampling hint. The check
now settles only on an executable named as the host, or when inventory was
complete and every executable that could be the host was sampled.

A Bun sourcemap region is named .bunmap, so its role was lost and a complete
audit reported no source maps. Carry the region role from the reader's metadata
into the member view, in the expanded and unexpanded paths, and treat it as a
JavaScript map so an unparsable region stays unresolved, not a debug companion.

An HTML member was scanned as text but its inline scripts were never checked
for source maps. The HTML owner now returns each body, the reader examines it
like a script file, and bodies past the owner's limit count as skipped.

* fix(audit): charge map reads to the count before opening the member

An oversized or unreadable .map returned before readSourceMap counted it, so
the allowance of 32 never ran out. An unexpanded .NET or PyInstaller package
could then decompress every listed map member, about 1 MiB each, up to the
4,096 entry cap.

The count bounds reads, so examineMap now reserves the slot before it opens the
member. A map past the count is skipped unopened, and a linker map past it is
still settled from its bounded prefix. An inline data: map is already in memory
and keeps its charge at the point it is parsed.

* fix(audit): examine scripts HTML loads whatever they are called

isJavaScriptMember knows a script by its suffix or an assigned kind, and the
reader dropped the script references the HTML owner parses. An extensionless
main loaded by <script src="main"> was scanned as ordinary text, so a complete
inventory reported javascript.source_map_sources not_observed with shipped
sources in its inline map.

The reader now resolves each JavaScript script reference against the page and
its base href, and a local target without a JavaScript name is examined as a
script when reached. A target read before its HTML file, never reached, or not
placeable on disk counts as a skipped map, so the check stays unknown.

* fix(audit): charge sibling map reads to the map count

Every generic .map beside a selected file got a full 1 MiB read and a
parse, with no cumulative bound, so the 4,096-entry listing allowed about
4 GiB of reading for one small selection.

Move the slot rule into chargeMapRead, which examineMap and sibling
classification now share. Past the count a sibling reads only the header:
a linker map is still identified, and one that may be a source map stays
a skipped companion.

* fix(audit): report cleanup failures raised by member reads

A close failure during an embedded-package probe, member read or inventory
reaches the shared read filter as an ordinary reader failure. The filter kept
only cancellation and integrity, so the member became a skipped read, inspect
succeeded, and the retained descriptor was reported nowhere. MCP does not close
the service after each request, so no caller saw it.

Propagate any failure that carries cleanup, whatever its reason, so it reaches
releaseExposureFailure and the audit reports its retained resources.

* fix(audit): charge unsuccessful text reads to the byte allowance

An oversized, undecodable, or failed text read left textBytes unchanged, so
every member got the full per-member budget and the cumulative allowance did
not bound what a package decompressed. Count the bytes member reads produce
and charge them whatever the read yields. An oversized file on disk still
costs only its probe.

* fix(audit): bound the paths kept for HTML script targets

A base href is copied into every script target it resolves, so a page under
the text member allowance could retain hundreds of megabytes of paths. Charge
each new target's resolved path to a byte allowance and leave targets past it
unassessed.

* fix(audit): keep examining a page loaded as a script as HTML

A script element naming an .html member promoted that member to a
script, and the text pass then chose one reading. The page's own script
elements were never read, so an inline map in it was lost and a shipped
sourcesContent went unreported.

Run the script reading and the HTML reading independently, and list the
script target allowance among the cases that leave source map coverage
undecided.

* fix(audit): detect credential markers that end in a hyphen

The Google, GitLab, and Slack rules allow a hyphen in the token but ended
on a word boundary, so a token ending in a hyphen at the rule's minimum
length was missed and the audit reported the check as not observed.
Open-ended rules now take the whole token, and the fixed-length Google
rule checks the full token alphabet after its last character.

* fix(audit): confirm FAT identity for probed package members

The package probe treated a decoded FAT table as a universal Mach-O. A
JVM class past the 4 KiB probe shares the FAT magic, so its truncated
prefix decoded as a table, the member counted as an unread native image,
and Electron could not be ruled out of a complete scan.

Pass the member's declared size to the sniff and take identity from
classifyFatContainerEvidence. A member with no usable size, or with
slices past the probe, stays counted as possibly native.

* fix(audit): admit binary plists in package member probes

A package member's probe judged text by its own NUL test, which accepted
byte order marks but not the binary plist signature decodeMemberText also
reads. A PyInstaller executable shipping a binary Localizable.strings was
rejected without a scan or a skipped count, so a UTF-16BE private key
marker inside it could report not_observed.

Name the encodings that explain their own NULs in one predicate, and move
the plist fixture builders to module scope.

* fix(audit): locate Go findings only in images that retain build paths

The exposed decision required non-empty paths, but the locations took
every image whose build info read. An image with no paths was named as a
source of the leak beside the one that had them.

One predicate now decides both.

* fix(audit): keep completed findings when member cleanup fails

A descriptor close failure aborts the member scan, and the scan's state
was dropped with it, so the caller got a typed cleanup failure and no
report. Source maps already counted and credential hits already collected
were lost.
