The reader now hands the service what it assembled, with coverage unknown
and a limitation saying so, alongside the failure. The service runs that
scan through its existing stopped-audit path: no later owner runs, and the
report goes on the error as its partial observation.

* fix(audit): keep coverage unknown for nested ASARs in package hosts

A member of a PyInstaller or .NET host reaches the binary probe as a
plain file. An ASAR among them has a NUL-bearing header, so the probe
dropped it with no traversal and no omission, and source map checks could
read not_observed with complete coverage.

Ask the ASAR owner's signature probe, and record a match as a nested
package that was not expanded, as inventory-classified ones already are.

* fix(audit): let native format facts outrank member names

examineMember tried the name-based text and map routes first, so a PE an
owner identified inside an ASAR, named payload.json, was read as text.
Its CodeView path and the packaged-native omission were both lost, and
native.pdb_path read not_applicable.

Route an owner-established native format to the native probe first, and
count an encrypted one as a packaged native image for the same reason.

* fix(audit): report relative paths given to compiler path flags

go.build_paths only kept rooted paths, so retained build settings like
CGO_CFLAGS=-Iprivate-sdk read not_observed even though the setting names
a directory.

Take the relative argument of a C compiler path flag, attached or in the
next field. Scope this to compiler settings, because Go's own tools use
the same letters for non-paths such as -B gobuildid and -T 0x1000.

* test(javascript): expect retained text on SVG inline scripts

The SVG test from main predates this branch's inlineScripts text field,
so each side passed alone and only their merge failed.

* fix(audit): keep an unresolved Electron host's fuses unknown

fuseCheck decided from whatever outcomes the images reported, so a host
with no fuse answer read not_observed as soon as any other image in the
directory reported safe fuses.

Pass the images named as the host into the report and leave a check
unknown when one of them has no answer for it. Other images stay free to
have no fuses, because helpers in a real Electron install have none.

* fix(audit): bound the paths kept for local source map targets

noteMapTarget kept every declared target resolved against its member's
directory, so a short URL under a long directory could retain far more
than the script's own size, with no cumulative limit.

Add the allowance noteScriptTarget already has. A target past it stays
unassessed and counts as a skipped map, and is never read.

* fix(audit): borrow the audit's scope admission for inventory

inspect holds resources.run for the whole audit, and inventoryArtifact
entered the same scope again. With failed cleanup pending from another
audit, the inner run waits for a drain that waits for the outer run.

Add inventoryArtifactInScope, which takes the caller's admission.

* fix(audit): run the exposure verifier's commands under supervision

The verifier launched npm and the CLI with raw execFile and then removed
its temporary tree, so a timed-out child could outlive the tree it was
using.

Use the shared verifier commands and close them before removing the tree.
Their exit error carries stdout on its snapshot, so the audit's exit-code
branch reads it from there.

* fix(audit): read relative -L paths and split flag arguments

The relative-path reader handled C compiler settings only, so a directory
kept through Go's own linker flag, such as -ldflags='-L private-sdk -s -w',
reported go.build_paths as not_observed.

A quoted flag and argument also reached it as one field. The separating
space stayed on the argument, which reported rooted paths twice and kept a
leading space on relative ones.

Give -ldflags its own pattern that matches only -L, so -B gobuildid and
-T 0x1000 stay ignored, and consume the separator in the flag patterns.

* fix(audit): keep embedded leaves beside schema-invalid map fields

The reader recovers independent indexed leaves only after a
SourceMapFormatFailure, but inspectSourceMap let the schema's ZodError
through. A sibling with mappings "!", a section with a bad offset or a
root with a bad field skipped recovery, so a valid leaf with
sourcesContent reported javascript.source_map_sources as unknown.

Normalize schema rejection in SourceMapFormat, which owns these parses,
so every structural failure reaches consumers as a format failure. The
message is unchanged, and the codec and web fetcher already map both
cases to the same result.

* fix(audit): keep packaged executables' own packages unknown

examinePackagedBinary counted a native image inside a package and moved
on, while only on-disk images reached the embedded-package probes. An
ASAR carrying a PyInstaller, Bun, Node SEA or .NET executable with a
source map therefore scanned complete and reported
javascript.source_map_sources as not_observed.

Run the same classifier on packaged images. The probes read carrier
offsets from a file, so the member's bytes stay in a temporary file for
the probe alone. A detected package keeps member coverage unknown, as a
nested ASAR does, and an image past one file's total byte allowance
stays unprobed and unknown. A plain native member leaves coverage intact.

* fix(audit): read an app's sampled images for fuses

A .app target sent only the bundle candidate to the fuse reader, which
resolves to the outer Electron Framework. A sidecar with RunAsNode enabled
was never read, so the check reported not_observed in the app view while
the directory view reported exposed.

Send the bundle candidate first and then the sampled native images. An
image whose digest matches the bundle's read is skipped, so the framework
is not read twice. A sidecar's safe fuses cannot settle the outer framework,
so a bundle read with no answer for a fuse keeps that check unknown.

* fix(audit): read a Node shebang as script identity

The path classifier gives an extensionless executable a resource kind,
so a script such as bin/runner with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` header was
scanned as text without its inline maps being examined or counted. A
complete inventory then reported no shipped sources for it.

The probe holds the first bytes a member reader sees, so establish the
identity there. The script keeps the usual outcomes: a map that is read
counts, and one past an allowance or undecodable stays unknown.

* fix(audit): keep linker strings out of Go build paths

Reading `-X 'main.usage=-L level'` as a library directory made
go.build_paths report `level`, so a plain string could fail an audit
under --fail_on low.

Read the optional package selector once, before the setting's first
flag, and keep the argument of -X attached to it, so a string it sets
is never scanned as another option.

* fix(audit): keep a failed probe directory removal owned

A packaged image's probe copies the member's full bytes into a temporary
directory. When removing it failed, the error became an ordinary
unreadable probe: the audit could still succeed, nothing could retry the
removal, and the client heard nothing about the leftover bytes.

Hold the directory in the reader's resource scope, so close retries it,
and report the unfinished cleanup without replacing a primary failure.

* fix(audit): keep a declared .map from reading as a linker map

A script's sourceMappingURL=assets.map was dropped because the name
already looked like a map. A malformed assets.map then settled as a
linker map, so both source-map checks read not_observed and
native.debug_companions reported an exposure the release does not ship.

Keep a generic .map name as a declared target and read it as a
JavaScript map, in either scan order, so it stays unresolved.

* test(audit): rethrow typed errors from release exposure checks

A failed Result was rewrapped in a plain Error, which dropped its type,
cause and cleanup details from the test output.

* fix(audit): match companions by member identity, not spelling

An ASAR member's location is relative, and a declared map target is
absolute, so a malformed assets.map read before z.js stayed a linker
companion. The examined-map lookup, which is normalized, then returned
early, leaving both source-map checks not_observed.

Index companions by memberLocationKey and keep each reported spelling
under it. Spellings stay distinct because symlinks can make them differ.

* fix(audit): retract only guessed linker maps on a declaration

A script declaring sourceMappingURL=symbols.pdb after the scan reached
symbols.pdb removed the shipped PDB from the companion list, because a
late declaration retracted any companion. native.debug_companions could
then read not_observed.

Keep name-identified companions in their own set, and retract only maps
that were read as non-JSON and guessed to be linker maps.

* fix(audit): record an unfollowed map link as skipped

The directory and ASAR readers do not follow links, so a symlinked
app.js.map dropped out before any map counter moved. Its target was
scanned as plain text, and both source-map checks read not_observed.

Count a link that names a map as skipped wherever entries reach the
audit, and mark it examined so a declaration does not count it twice.

* fix(audit): read relative paths in Go compiler and assembler flags

A binary built with -gcflags=-I private-sdk keeps that setting, but
relative parsing covered only C compiler settings and -ldflags, so the
directory dropped out of go.build_paths.

Give -gcflags and -asmflags their own path options, taken from what
go tool compile and go tool asm document, and strip the package selector
as -ldflags does. The assembler's -D defines a symbol, so it is not one.

* docs(audit): state the packaged image read allowance

Packaged ELF, Mach-O and PE images are read in full and copied to a
temporary file, sharing one max_file_bytes allowance, but the docs and
coverage.allowances still said only a PE gets more than a header read.

Name the allowance and the copies in docs/release-exposure.md,
RELEASE_EXPOSURE_ALLOWANCES and the max_file_bytes description.

* docs(audit): say how go.build_paths treats rooted -X values

A rooted -X value cannot be told from a file path, so the audit reports
it. State that, and why, so the rule is a contract rather than a side
effect of how flags are scanned.

* fix(audit): keep a declared sibling map out of the linker guess

When the selected file declared a sibling map, the sibling classifier
never consulted the declaration. A malformed assets.map then read as a
linker map and raised native.debug_companions.

Leave a declared sibling to the unreached-target accounting, as members
already are, so it stays an unresolved source map.

* fix(audit): keep undecodable Go and Rust metadata unknown

Unsupported meant two things: a container this reader does not handle,
and metadata the image holds in a form the reader cannot decode, such as
a compressed .dep-v0 section. Both read as not_applicable, so an image
that carries metadata reported that the check did not apply.

Mark the second case on the format failure and carry it on
AnalysisUnsupportedTargetError, so the audit records a failed read and
stays unknown. The tools' own errors and messages do not change.

* fix(audit): keep coverage unknown for a PE header past the probe

A packaged member whose PE signature lies beyond the probe prefix stayed
unclassified, so the embedded-package probe never ran and coverage stayed
complete. A map inside such an image then read as not_observed.

Record the member as an unexamined package where it is already marked as
a possible native image.

* fix(audit): read the scripts of a standalone SVG

An SVG can carry a script with an inline source map, but only .html and
.htm members reached the script owner, so such a file left every map
counter at zero and javascript.source_map_sources read not_observed.

Treat .svg as a script-bearing page. htmlArtifactReferences already
reads SVG script elements, so this adds no parsing.

* fix(audit): keep every possible host when no name picks one out

With no named Electron host, every sibling ranks alike and
electron_host_paths stayed empty, so one image's safe fuses settled the
checks even when another possible host reported none.

Keep all sampled candidates as hosts in that case, so a candidate
without fuses leaves the checks unknown.

* fix(audit): read a text-named native member by its bytes

A PE member called payload.json took the text route, so it reached no
native probe, and its CodeView path and packaged-native uncertainty were
lost.

Decide from the bytes the text read already loaded, so real text costs
no extra read and the map and text allowances stay as they were.

* fix(audit): let a map or script read identify a native member

A package lists names without formats, so a PE called payload.js.map
took the map route and never reached a native probe. Its CodeView path
was lost, and with nothing counted as failed, native.pdb_path could read
not_applicable. A PE at a declared script or map target was lost the same
way, because declaration overrode the route.

Decide from the bytes the route already read, in the map route as in the
text route, and keep the listed kind for a promoted script target. Real
text and maps cost no extra read, so those allowances are unchanged.

* fix(audit): name a symlinked sibling debug companion

Selecting an executable skipped every symlink beside it before the name
check, so an app.pdb link left no companion path and no skip count, and
native.debug_companions read not_observed. Selecting the directory
reports the same link.

Check the name first. The map branch already needs a regular file, so no
link is followed.

* fix(audit): keep map coverage unknown for a linked script

A link named app.js to an extensionless payload was skipped as a link,
and its target was read as plain text with no map directives parsed. An
inline map there left no parsed or skipped count, so
javascript.source_map_sources read not_observed. Only links with a map
name were counted.

Count a link under any name that can declare a map, the set an unread
member already uses. It stays one omission when a page or a directive
also names it. The target is still not followed.

* fix(audit): keep a declared JavaScript map beside a selected file unknown

A local sourceMappingURL with a JavaScript map name such as app.js.map
was dropped on the assumption that it would be examined as a member.
When the selection is a file, sibling .js.map files are never read, so
the declared map left javascript.source_map_sources not_observed while
the same target spelled as a file: URL left it unknown. Record every
local target so an unreached one counts as skipped.

* fix(audit): read paths a C compiler forwards to the linker

CGO flags can hand linker options through -Wl,a,b or -Xlinker a. The
compiler flag parser saw -Wl,-L,private-sdk as one field and missed the
relative library directory, so go.build_paths reported not_observed.

Split forwarded options out before reading paths and read them with the
linker's own path options (-L, -T, --library-path, --script). This also
stops -Xlinker -Bsymbolic from being read as the compiler's -B prefix.

* fix(audit): read forwarded linker options by their linker meaning

The forwarded linker flag pattern read -Ttext=0x400000 as a script path
named text=0x400000, and it ignored -I, so -Xlinker -Ilib/ld-custom.so
lost the interpreter path the compiler flag pattern found before the
split.

Exclude the -T section and segment address options (bss, data, text,
text-segment, rodata-segment, ldata-segment) and read -I and
--dynamic-linker as paths.

* fix(audit): split Go flags as Go does and read external linker flags

Go splits a flag value with quoted.Split: a field that starts with a
quote runs to the matching quote, and any other quote is a literal
character. The reader stripped every quote, so CGO_CFLAGS
-I"/home/O'Neil/include" reported /home/ONeil/include, while cc was
given the directory "/home/O'Neil/include", quotes included.

-ldflags kept -extldflags values with the Go linker flags, where only
-L counts, so -extldflags=-Lprivate-sdk reported no path. The values
are now read as the C compiler driver reads them, including -Wl, and
-Xlinker forwarding.

A package member named payload.json or payload.js.map that holds an
ASAR took the text or map route, which checked only native signatures,
so the nested archive was scanned as text and coverage read complete.
The route's own read now recognizes the ASAR signature as well, and the
nested package leaves coverage unknown.

* fix(audit): keep a named script beside a selected HTML file unknown

A script element whose target had a JavaScript name such as app.js was
dropped on the assumption that it would be examined as a member. When
the selection is an HTML file, sibling scripts are never read, so a
sibling holding an inline map left javascript.source_map_sources
not_observed while the same target named app left it unknown. Record
every local script target so an unreached one counts as skipped.

* fix(audit): read a retained -pgo setting as one profile path

`-pgo file` names a single profile, and under -trimpath Go keeps only
its file name, so the flag readers dropped values such as
`private-training.pgo` and split paths with spaces or commas. Report
the value whole, skipping `auto` and `off`.

* fix(audit): read -extldflags paths as the external linker splits them

With -ldflags set to -extldflags '-L "/srv/private sdk"', the outer
flag reader could not match the path behind the inner quote, and the
external reader kept only relative paths, so go.build_paths read
not_observed. Read each -extldflags value once, as go tool link splits
it with quoted.Split, and collect rooted and relative paths from those
same arguments. The rest of the setting is read as before.

* fix(audit): read the Go linker's other path options

go.build_paths read only -L as a Go linker path option, so a retained
-ldflags='-tmpdir=private-obj -s -w' reported no path and --fail_on low
missed the directory.

Read every option `go tool link -h` documents as taking a directory,
path or file: -I, -L, -benchmarkprofile, -capturehostobjs, -cpuprofile,
-fipso, -importcfg, -memprofile, -o, -r and -tmpdir. -extld, -extar and
-libgcc name a program or `none`, so only their rooted values count.

* fix(audit): keep a quoted Go argument whole

goFields already reads -L "/tmp/private - sdk" as two arguments, but
each field was then split again before every whitespace-led dash, so
go.build_paths reported /tmp/private instead of the retained directory.

Split again only a field that begins with a flag, after any package
selector, as a quoted "-L dir -s -w" does. Any other field is one
argument and is kept whole, in -ldflags, -extldflags and CGO flags.

* fix(audit): keep coverage unknown for an unread packaged image

When a listed package member is a native image but its first read
fails, examinePackagedBinary returned before probePackagedImage could
mark its possible embedded package unexamined. Coverage stayed complete
and javascript.source_map_sources could report not_observed for a
payload nobody read.

Mark member coverage unknown wherever a native member goes unread,
including an encrypted one, as an image the probe could not read
already does, and say so in the limitations.

* fix(audit): read rooted Go tool path arguments whole

`-L "/tmp/private,sdk"` and `-L=/tmp/a=b` name one directory, so a `,` or
`=` in a documented path flag's argument is literal. `-trimpath` keeps its
prefix=replacement structure.

* fix(audit): count an unread packaged member once

* fix(audit): keep trimpath rewrites and directory fields apart from selectors

* fix(audit): keep a .map unsettled once a declaration was discarded

* fix(audit): skip env option arguments when reading a Node shebang

* fix(audit): keep companion coverage unresolved for a generic .map link

* fix(audit): count a dropped linker-map guess as a skipped companion

* fix(audit): read env settings after -- in a Node shebang

* fix(audit): route a selected native image named .map by its format

A directly selected or listed native image has no package format, so
examineMember skipped its native-first branch and sent a file such as
release.map through map routing. Its bytes then became a linker-map
guess and marked native.debug_companions exposed. Native format now
outranks the name for every member, packaged or not.

* fix(audit): read forwarded -rpath and -rpath-link as linker paths

A cgo build with CGO_LDFLAGS=-Wl,-rpath,private-runtime kept the
relative directory, but the forwarded linker parser only knew -L, -T,
-I, --library-path, --dynamic-linker and --script, so go.build_paths
reported not_observed. Add -rpath and -rpath-link to the same parser,
in the attached, = and next-field forms. Loader-expanded values such as
$ORIGIN/../lib and @loader_path/Frameworks name no build-host directory
and stay unreported.

* fix(audit): read each entry of a forwarded linker search list

-rpath and -rpath-link take a colon-separated search list. The loader
token filter tested the whole list, so -Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN:/opt/private-runtime
dropped /opt/private-runtime along with $ORIGIN, and the rooted-path pass
cannot see an entry that follows a colon. Split each search list into its
entries and drop only the loader-expanded ones.

* fix(audit): expand loader tokens only in a linker search list

The runtime loader expands $ORIGIN and @loader_path only in a -rpath or
-rpath-link search list. The token filter also ran on the argument of -T,
-L and -I, so -Wl,-T,$ORIGIN.ld dropped a literal linker script path and
a complete read could report go.build_paths as not observed. Search list
entries keep the filter; every other linker path argument is kept as is.

* fix(audit): count a .map link beside a selected file as a skipped companion

The sibling scan skipped any .map entry that was not a regular file, so a
symlink such as symbols.map -> payload beside a selected executable left
debug companion coverage at not observed. The reader never follows links,
so the linker map such a link may name is unread, not absent. Count a
generic .map sibling link as a skipped companion without following it,
as noteUnfollowedMapLink already does inside a selected directory.

* fix(audit): split a linker search list only for an ELF image

Only the ELF linker reads a -rpath or -rpath-link argument as a
colon-separated list. The Mach-O linker stores each -rpath argument as one
directory, so -Wl,-rpath,@loader_path/lib:extra is a single loader-relative
entry, yet it was split and extra was reported as a build path. Carry the
native image format into the Go flag reader and split search lists only for
ELF; other formats read the whole argument as one entry.

* fix(audit): expand only the image loader's runtime tokens

A runtime search path token is expanded only by the loader of the image's
format. The ELF loader expands $ORIGIN, $LIB and $PLATFORM; dyld expands
@executable_path, @loader_path and @rpath. Each is literal text to the
other loader, so -Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN:/opt/private-runtime on a Mach-O image
names a literal directory, yet it was dropped and go.build_paths reported
not_observed. Pick the token set from the native image format; the PE
loader reads no search list, so it expands none.

* fix(audit): keep a declared .map link beside a selected script a source map

The sibling scan counted any .map symlink as a skipped debug companion
before checking whether the selected script declared it as its source
map. classifySiblingMap already excludes a declared target that is a
regular file, so a declared symbols.map link added a false unknown to
debug_companions. Apply the declared-target check before either file-type
branch; noteUnreachedTargets still counts the unread map as skipped.

* fix(audit): byte-check members whose kind is only an inventory path role

Inventory gives a packaged member a role from its name, such as resource
for payload.json or source-map for payload.map. The packaged-format guard
treated any kind other than "file" as owner-stated, so a nested ASAR an
ASAR lists under one of those names skipped signature recognition and
cleared coverage. Track whether the package owner stated the kind (Bun
sourcemap region, SEA main script) and only skip the byte check then.

* fix(audit): read Go's linker -r setting as a runtime search list

go tool link -r sets the ELF dynamic linker search path, dir1:dir2:...,
which the linker writes to RUNPATH. It was read as one whole path, so a
release built with -ldflags='-r=$ORIGIN/../lib' reported the
loader-relative entry as a build path and go.build_paths as exposed.
Read -r entry by entry with the same image-loader-aware split and token
filter a forwarded -rpath uses: ELF splits at ':' and drops $ORIGIN
entries; Mach-O keeps the argument as one directory.

* fix(audit): keep a selected package executable's native carrier format

A directly selected PyInstaller executable named release.map recorded the
package format as its member format, even though its ELF or PE carrier was
already recognized. examineMember then missed the native-first branch and
treated the executable as a linker map, reporting a debug companion.
Forward the native carrier format for the selected file, as listed members
already do.

* fix(audit): keep coverage unknown for an unread unclassified member

A packaged member with no format of its own, such as a PyInstaller
payload.bin, recorded only a skipped text member when its read failed
before the header. Member coverage then stayed complete, though the
member could be a native image or carry a nested package. Leave
coverage unknown and say which member could not be read, as an unread
native member already does.

* fix(audit): keep ASAR header admission distinct from max_file_bytes

A directory holding an ASAR whose header exceeds the header admission
was reported as a file-size refusal with max_file_bytes advice, which
cannot fix it. Report the header admission as its own bound instead.

* fix(audit): thread the shared ASAR header admission into release exposure

createReleaseExposureService built ReleaseExposureReader with no admission,
so its inventory and every reopened ASAR reader stayed on the 16 MiB
default and ignored REA_ASAR_MAX_HEADER_BYTES and asar.max_header_bytes.

Resolve the admission in the composition with runtimeAsarHeaderAdmission,
as the Electron and V8 observation providers do, and pass it to both
inventoryArtifactInScope calls, the reopened container readers, and the
nested ASAR signature probe. The refusal now names the setting that can
raise it instead of claiming there is no runtime override.

* fix(audit): keep a nested ASAR probe stopped at the admission undecided

The release exposure reader treated an ASAR signature probe that stopped
at the header admission as "not an ASAR". A packaged member such as
payload.json holding an ASAR whose JSON starts past asar.max_header_bytes
was then read as plain text, its inner maps went unread, and
javascript.source_map_sources could stay not_observed.

A probe that reaches the admission limit, or runs out of a prefix read
after its extents parse, now marks package coverage unknown and records
a limitation, while the member is still examined as text.

* fix(cli): parse audit-release-exposure --max-file-bytes as a decimal token

Main now requires every numeric CLI option to admit decimal tokens and
reject 0x10 and 1e3 (tests/boundary/cli/cliDecimalArguments.test.ts).
Wrap the release exposure maxFileBytes option in cliDecimalField like the
other maxFileBytes options, so the domain field keeps its bounds and default.

* docs(specs): add the release exposure audit specification

Add spec.md, plan.md and tasks.md under docs/specs/artifacts/release-exposure/
as docs/development/documentation.md requires for a new feature, and list
them in docs/specs/README.md. The existing guide at docs/release-exposure.md
keeps describing current behavior and its route is unchanged.

* fix(audit): bind unpacked ASAR member reads to their inventoried digests

A selected ASAR is captured and checked against its inventoried digest, which
binds packed members. An unpacked member is read from its .unpacked companion
on disk instead, and readContainerMember and readEntryBytes never compared
those bytes with the member digest inventory recorded, so a companion
replaced between inventory and the scan was accepted.

readContainerMember now passes the member's inventoried digest for unpacked
entries, and readStreamBounded hashes the full stream, draining past the read
allowance when needed, and fails with "ASAR member changed before
interpretation", which surfaces as an artifact_changed error like the
container check. A regression test replaces a companion after inventory. The
guide, spec, plan and tasks describe the binding.

* fix(audit): let stated JavaScript roles outrank a .map name

isDeclaredMap() routed any member whose name ended in .map to map
handling before the owner's stated role or a page's script declaration
was considered. A Node SEA main script at boot.map, which the SEA reader
marks as javascript, and a .map script an HTML file loads both became
linker-map guesses, so their inline maps were never read and
native.debug_companions was reported exposed.

An owner-stated source-map role or a declared map target still makes a
member a map. Otherwise a stated javascript kind or a script target now
wins, and only then does the .map suffix, or the inventory path role that
repeats it, decide. Regression tests cover both cases, and the guide
notes that a SEA main script is read as a script whatever it is called.

* fix(audit): keep coverage unknown when a packaged text member fails to read

A compressed member named as text, such as payload.json in an unexpanded
PyInstaller host, can fail inflation before any header is returned. The
.bin case already leaves member coverage unknown because an unread header
may hide a nested image or package, but examineTextMember() only counted
the member as skipped text, so otherwise complete coverage stayed
complete and package-dependent checks could settle.

An unread packaged member whose kind its package did not state now goes
through noteUnreadBinary(), which counts it as skipped text, marks
coverage unknown, and records the limitation. A regression test corrupts
the zlib stream of payload.json in a CArchive host and checks the intact
member keeps coverage complete. The guide describes the rule.

* fix(audit): keep the unpacked ASAR digest check inside the read allowance

ea87cf8 made readStreamBounded hash an unpacked ASAR companion to its end
so it could compare against the inventoried digest, which drained the
stream past the read allowance. A 1 GiB unpacked module was read in full
for a 4 KiB header probe and again for a package probe, and a companion
that grew after inventory had no byte limit on that path.

readStreamBounded now stops at the allowance as every other member read
does, and compares the digest only when the member ended within the
allowance. A companion past the allowance stays over_allowance without a
digest verification. A test counts the bytes each scan read pulls from an
8 MiB companion. The guide and spec state the bound.

* fix(audit): read a script target whose bytes are a source map as a map

1d3f89f let a stated javascript kind or an HTML script target outrank a
.map name, so an HTML `<script src="main.map">` that points at a valid
source map with sourcesContent was read only as a script. Its sources
were never counted and javascript.source_map_sources could miss an
exposed finding.

A script role says how a member is loaded, not what its bytes hold. A
.map member or loaded script whose text parses as a source map, a JSON
object with version and mappings, sources, or sections, is now read as
a source map. Anything else is still read as a script, so a SEA main
script named boot.map and a .map script carrying an inline map keep
reaching examineInlineMaps. A regression test covers the map case, and
the guide states the rule.

* fix(audit): retract a linker-map guess when a page loads the map as a script

noteScriptTarget() returned early for a target already read, counting its
source-map coverage as skipped but leaving any linker-map guess the first
read recorded. When a directory or ASAR listed a non-JSON app.map before
the index.html that loads it with <script src="app.map">, app.map stayed in
native.debug_companions and the result depended on enumeration order.
noteMapTarget() already retracted such a guess for a late map declaration.

A late script declaration now retracts the guess too, and still counts the
script as skipped because it was never examined as JavaScript. A test
covers the directory and ASAR order, and the guide states the outcome.

* fix(audit): respect script and native identity for sibling linker maps

classifySiblingMap() guessed a linker map for any sibling .map whose bytes
could not begin a JSON object. A sibling boot.map that a selected index.html
loads with <script src="boot.map">, or an ELF image named release.map beside
a selected executable, was therefore reported in native.debug_companions.

scanSiblings() now skips a sibling that is a script target as well as a map
target, leaving noteUnreachedTargets() to count it, and classifySiblingMap()
records no guess when sniffNativeFormat() recognizes the header. Tests cover
both cases and the guide states the outcome.

* fix(audit): read a script-loaded map from the text that recognized it

scriptHoldsMap() recognizes a .map or script target as a source map from
decodeMemberText(), which honors a UTF-16 byte order mark, but
readScriptAsMap() then passed the raw bytes to readSourceMap(), which reads
UTF-8. A BOM-marked UTF-16 main.map loaded by <script src="main.map"> failed
the second parse and its prefix became a linker-map guess.

readScriptAsMap() now hands the decoded text to readSourceMapText(), which
readSourceMap() also uses for byte input, so both stages read the same text.
A test covers a UTF-16 map with embedded sources.

* fix(release-exposure): honor byte order marks in binary plist data

A binary plist data object holding BOM-marked UTF-16 text was decoded as
UTF-8, so credential markers in it went unmatched while coverage still
read complete. Decode such payloads with the encoding their mark declares,
and leave coverage incomplete for UTF-32, which no reader scans.

* fix(audit): keep an unprobed package member past the text allowance unknown

Once the cumulative text allowance was spent, examineTextMember() counted a
packaged member named like text, such as payload.json in a .NET or
PyInstaller bundle, as skipped text without reading its header. Coverage
stayed complete even though the member could be a native image or a nested
ASAR, while the same bytes named payload.bin kept coverage unknown.

An unexpanded package member whose kind the owner did not state now leaves
coverage unknown with a limitation when the allowance skips it, the same
uncertainty an unread .bin member carries. No extra read is made, so the
allowance still bounds what is opened. A test covers an ASAR with an
embedded source map named payload.json after sixteen full text members.

* fix(release-exposure): require a read host for every Electron layout

A directory with several resources/app.asar layouts counted one named
host as fuse coverage for all of them. Track host coverage per layout so
safe fuses stay unknown when a whole layout's possible hosts were
dropped from the native image sample.

* fix(release-exposure): keep a .map script past the target allowance unassessed

When HTML script references spent the resolved-path allowance, a later
.map script target was dropped without its script role, so its JavaScript
bytes settled as a linker-map guess and debug_companions reported an
exposure. A refused script target now sets mapTargetsDiscarded, the same
flag a refused map target sets, so a later .map stays unassessed instead
of becoming companion evidence.

* fix(release-exposure): read a Node shebang as script in any text member

A selected or listed text file such as runner.txt that starts with a Node
shebang went straight to the text reader, which never gave it a JavaScript
role, so its inline map went unread and source_map_sources read
not_observed. The text reader now takes the role from the bytes it read,
so every route into it sees the shebang, and the probed-text path no longer
sets the role itself.

* fix(release-exposure): exclude Go search lists by position, not by value

compilerPaths dropped every literal path whose text equalled a forwarded
-rpath or -rpath-link list, so CGO_LDFLAGS=-Wl,-L,$ORIGIN -Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN
lost the literal -L directory and go.build_paths read not_observed. The
literal flags are now read with each search list option and its argument
removed by position, and the search lists are still read entry by entry.

* fix(release-exposure): keep a probed Node launcher's role past the allowance

The probe recognized a Node shebang but handed the text reader the member
without its JavaScript role. Once earlier text spent the shared allowance,
the text reader returned before reading the header again, so an
extensionless launcher added no skipped map and both source-map checks read
not_observed instead of unknown. The probe now passes the role it found.

* fix(release-exposure): decode a map in the encoding its byte order mark names

The map reader, its prefix check and the sibling classifier decoded map
bytes as UTF-8, so a generic symbols.map holding BOM-marked UTF-16 source
map JSON failed to parse and its prefix read as a linker map: a spurious
debug companion and source_map_sources not_observed. Map bytes are now
decoded by their byte order mark at that boundary, and a UTF-32 map, which
this reader does not decode, stays unresolved.

* fix(release-exposure): keep a lone dash inside a quoted Go path argument

splitGoField split a quoted field before every whitespace-led dash, so the
retained -ldflags '-s "-L=/tmp/private - sdk" -w' read the dash inside the
directory as a new flag and goPaths reported /tmp/private. A quoted field
now splits only before a dash that begins a flag, so a dash followed by a
space stays part of the path.

* fix(release-exposure): choose possible Electron hosts within each layout

The named-or-possible host choice ran across every kept image, so a named
a/a.exe removed the unnamed b/launcher.exe of a second ASAR layout from
electron_host_paths, and its unresolved fuses no longer held
electron.run_as_node at unknown. Each layout now chooses its own named or
possible hosts, and the sets are combined.

* fix(release-exposure): read a relative compiler --sysroot as a build path

The compiler path flag list had no --sysroot, and the rooted-path fallback
cannot see a relative operand, so CGO_LDFLAGS=--sysroot=private-sdk left
go.build_paths at not_observed. --sysroot is now a compiler path flag,
attached with = or given as the next field.

* fix(release-exposure): recognize Windows Electron layouts by the owner's path

The desktop owner gives each file a native local_path, such as
C:\ship\App\resources\app.asar on Windows, and desktopPathConventions only
splits on /, so every ASAR basis was skipped: host ranking and
electron_host_paths stayed empty and a named host with no sentinel let a
safe helper read electron.run_as_node as not_observed. Each basis now
carries whether the owner's slash-separated path is an ASAR layout, and the
layout folders read a Windows absolute path with Windows separators on any
host.

* fix(release-exposure): read a Bun module by its JavaScript loader

An extensionless Bun contents member such as $bunfs/root/release carries
loader_name js, but ownerStatedKind kept only the sourcemap region, so the
member was never read as a script and its inline map went unseen. Give a
Bun contents region the javascript role for the js, jsx, ts and tsx
loaders, as SEA main scripts get it.

* fix(release-exposure): read a Node shebang .map as a script

An undeclared `.map` was routed as a source or linker map before its
first bytes were checked, so a Node script named `runner.map` recorded a
linker-map companion and never had its inline map read. When the map
read of an undeclared `.map` starts with a Node shebang, its map slot is
returned and the text reader examines it as JavaScript, so its inline
map is parsed and no companion is reported.

* Detect full-length GitHub refresh tokens

Narrow github.token to gh[opus]_ with 36 characters and give ghr_ its
own 76-character github.refresh_token rule, with a test.

* fix(release-exposure): bind a negative package probe to the inventoried image

An on-disk native image whose embedded-package probe finds nothing clears member coverage, so it now hashes the probed descriptor and compares it with the inventoried digest before accepting absent. A replacement after inventory fails as a changed member instead of reporting complete coverage.

* fix(release-exposure): let an app bundle read settle only its own layout

An app target, an app-bundle fuse read or a sampled selected executable used to mark the Electron executable as included for every ASAR layout, so safe outer fuses reported not_observed even when a nested Electron app's host was never read. Those reads now settle only their own layout; every other discovered layout still needs its own host read, so an omitted nested host keeps fuse checks unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): honor a Node shebang before guessing a sibling linker map

A sibling .map beside the selected file that starts with a Node shebang is a script, as it already is for a member .map, so classifySiblingMap no longer records it as a linker-map debug companion.

* fix(release-exposure): name a bundle's own layout by the owner's path

The settled layout set joined the caller's bundle spelling with Contents, so a selected /tmp/App.app missed the owner's resolved /private/tmp/App.app/Contents layout and safe fuse checks fell to unknown. Each archive basis now carries the owner's relative layout folder, and the bundle's own layout is the one whose relative folder is Contents, looked up by the owner's resolved folder.

* fix(release-exposure): read file-valued linker options as build paths

LINKER_PATH_FLAG listed --script but not the other linker options that read a file, so -extldflags=-Wl,--version-script=private-versions.map left go.build_paths not_observed. --version-script, --dynamic-list and --retain-symbols-file now read their operand as a path, attached or in the next field.

* fix(release-exposure): count a macOS bundle's framework and MacOS hosts in its layout

A .app layout resolves to its Contents folder, but its hosts are Contents/MacOS/* and the Electron framework binary under Contents/Frameworks, so per-layout host ranking and fuse coverage dropped them and one bundle's safe fuses could settle another bundle. Those images now belong to the bundle's layout, with the framework binary ranked as its host.

* fix(release-exposure): keep a bundle's launcher out of its fuse hosts

A macOS bundle's Electron Framework binary carries its fuses. When it
is among a layout's named hosts, it is now the layout's only fuse host;
the MacOS launcher beside it is still sampled but no longer leaves safe
fuse checks undecided when it has no sentinel.

* fix(release-exposure): keep an undecided PE package member out of linker maps

An unexpanded package member named .map whose PE signature lies past the
retained prefix fell through to noteUnreadMap, which read its MZ prefix as
a linker map and reported native.debug_companions exposed with complete
coverage. The map route now records the same undecided-PE uncertainty the
binary route does, so the member stays unexamined and coverage unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): scan the text of an undecided PE map member

A packaged .map member whose MZ header is undecided returned before its
fully read bytes reached the credential scanner, so a PEM key in it read
as unknown instead of exposed. Scan bytes read in full before returning,
while still keeping PE coverage undecided.

* fix(release-exposure): keep an oversized text member's undecided PE header

A packaged text member past the per-member allowance keeps only its prefix,
so an MZ header whose PE signature lies further in returned null and the
text route dropped the native and package uncertainty. Note the undecided
header as the map and binary routes do.

* fix(release-exposure): join Electron layouts by caller path and keep partial discovery unknown

The desktop owner resolves its root, so a target selected through a
symlinked parent got canonical local_paths that never matched the
audit's caller-spelled images, and the named host dropped out of
electron_host_paths. Rebase owner paths under the canonical root onto
the selected path.

When discovery stopped after it found one Electron layout, the basis
list was treated as exhaustive. Report the layouts as incomplete so safe
fuses on the listed host stay unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): keep Electron hosts under a trailing-slash selection

Join the rebased archive path with appendCallerPath so a selected
`/work/app/` yields `/work/app/resources/app.asar`, whose layout folder
matches the inventoried executables' parent.

* fix(release-exposure): keep maps unassessed for unread text past the allowance

A text-named member such as `runner.txt` can start with a Node shebang.
Once the text allowance is spent its header is not read either, so count
every unread member that could hold a script as a skipped map instead of
trusting the filename-derived role.

* fix(release-exposure): keep an unread packaged map member undecided

When a packaged map member yields no header (a failed read or no map
slot), its name is no evidence of its format. Route it through
noteUnreadBinary, as the text route does, so a member that may be a
native image or package keeps coverage unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): keep an undecided sibling PE header out of linker-map guesses

A sibling .map past the map allowance keeps only its probe, so an MZ
header whose PE signature lies further in is undecided. Share the
undecided-PE test with packaged members and count such a sibling as a
skipped companion instead of guessing a linker map.

* fix(release-exposure): keep possible fuse hosts when no ASAR layout names one

Without an ASAR basis no image is ranked, so no image counted as a fuse
host and one image's safe fuses could settle a sentinel-less sibling.
While the desktop family is undecided and no layout names a host, treat
every sampled image as a possible host.

* fix(release-exposure): keep images outside a found ASAR layout as possible fuse hosts

An asar: false build beside a discovered ASAR layout gets no basis, so
its executables were never fuse hosts and the layout's safe fuses could
settle a sentinel-less image in the other build. When no name picks out
a host outside the found layouts, treat every sampled image there as a
possible host, as the no-layout case already does while the family is
undecided.

* fix(release-exposure): keep a dropped host outside a found ASAR layout unread

An asar: false build beside a found ASAR layout names no host, so an
executable outside every layout that the native-image sample dropped may
be that build's unread fuse host. Coverage no longer counts as proven
when such an image was inventoried but not sampled.

* fix(release-exposure): read Go build-path response files named in compiler and linker flags

A CGO setting such as `-Wl,@/tmp/private-link.rsp` or
`-Xlinker @/tmp/private-link.rsp` names a response file the linker reads
options from, and a bare `@FILE` is read by the compiler driver. Report
the file's path, relative or rooted like other path arguments, without
opening it. An option's own value, such as `-install_name
@rpath/libx.dylib`, and dyld runtime tokens are not response files.

* fix(release-exposure): keep a dropped host outside an ASAR layout unread whatever its name

The guard for a sampled-out host beside a found ASAR layout ruled images
out by filename, so an asar: false host named like `b/My.App` was missed
and safe fuses from the sampled layout settled the installation. Every
inventoried native image outside the found layouts that the sample
dropped now keeps the fuse checks unknown.

* fix(release-exposure): keep maps unassessed for an unreadable extensionless launcher

An unclassified file whose initial header probe fails, such as an
extensionless `runner` that became unreadable after inventory, may carry
a Node shebang and a map directive. The probe failure now leaves its
maps unassessed, as an unread `runner.js` or packaged member does,
instead of counting the file as holding no script.

* fix(release-exposure): read a response file named like a dyld token

`-Wl,@rpath/private-link.rsp` names a linker response file, not a dyld
runtime path, so dropping every `@rpath` or `@loader_path` argument hid
it. A dyld token is now skipped only as the value of an option that takes
one, such as `-install_name` or `-dylib_file`.

* fix(release-exposure): keep the partial member scan on ordinary cancellation

A scan cancelled after some members were examined reported its partial
scan only when cleanup also failed, so a clean cancellation dropped the
recovered source-map and credential observations. A cancelled scan now
hands its assembled facts to the interrupted-scan visitor with unknown
coverage and a cancellation limitation, and the caller still receives
the cancellation error carrying that partial audit.

* docs(release-exposure): describe the partial report kept when the member scan is cancelled

Since the member scan keeps what it examined on ordinary cancellation,
the status guide no longer says that cancelling the scan returns no
partial report. It now describes the partial observation and limits the
no-report case to cancellation before the scan can be assembled.

* fix(release-exposure): keep maps unassessed when a text header is cut short

A text-named member read with one or two bytes of the text allowance
left returns only `#` or `#!`, which cannot establish a Node shebang, so
`runner.txt` kept its non-script role and its unexamined inline map was
treated as absent. A partial or missing header that could still start a
shebang line now leaves the member's maps unassessed, as an unread
member's do once the allowance is spent.

* fix(release-exposure): keep dotted executables as possible hosts in ASAR layouts

Inside an ASAR layout, a sibling whose name had a dot and no `.exe`
suffix, such as `my.app`, was neither ranked for the native sample nor
counted as a possible Electron host. With shared libraries filling the
sample, that image could be dropped while the layout still counted its
host as read, so safe fuses on a helper reported `run_as_node` as not
observed. A dotted sibling that is not named like a shared library is
now sampled after plain siblings and counted as a possible host.

* fix(release-exposure): split env -S shebangs on unquoted blanks only

The env shebang reader split the whole line on spaces before handling -S,
so a launcher such as `#!/usr/bin/env -S NODE_OPTIONS='--conditions
development' node` named `development'` as its program and its maps were
never assessed. An -S operand now takes the rest of the line and is split
the way GNU env -S splits it: single and double quotes, backslash escapes,
\_ and \c, and a leading # comment. A string env itself rejects, such as an
unterminated quote, runs no program.

* fix(release-exposure): keep owner facts completed before cancellation

When a Go, Rust, fuse or desktop owner finished its Evidence and then saw
cancellation, completeProviderEvidence returned that Evidence as the
error's partial observation, but the audit only kept the error and
substituted a not-run fact, so a recovered Go build path or Rust package
list reported unknown. Each owner's Evidence-to-fact reading now lives in
one function used for both a successful read and a completed partial, so
the partial passes the same schema and inventory digest checks before its
fact is kept. Later owners still do not run.

* fix(release-exposure): keep env -S programs named by a variable unassessed

`env -S` expands `${NAME}` from the environment, so a launcher such as
`#!/usr/bin/env -S ${NODE_BIN}` may run Node, but the shebang reader kept
the placeholder as the program name and treated the file as plain text,
reporting its inline map as absent. The env splitter now marks fields that
expand a variable, and a program whose name holds one leaves the shebang
undecided: the member's maps count as unassessed, and a `.map` companion
with such a header is not taken as a linker map. Quoted or escaped `${`
stays literal, and a resolved basename such as `${DIR}/bin/deno` still
decides.

* fix(release-exposure): keep the ASAR header admission for selected files

A directly selected app.asar whose header exceeds asar.max_header_bytes
now returns the typed header admission refusal and its recovery, as the
directory scan already does, instead of a generic partial report.

* fix(release-exposure): keep a map member with a variable env -S program unassessed

An undeclared `runner.map` whose `env -S` program is `${NODE_BIN}` may
run Node, so `examineMapMember` now treats an undecided `nodeShebang`
result as an unassessed map and companion, as `classifySiblingMap`
already does, rather than falling through to a linker-map guess.

* fix(release-exposure): read a forwarded -Map linker map path

splitForwardedLinkerFlags hands -Wl,-Map=private-link.map to the linker
side, but LINKER_PATH_FLAG had no Map entry, so the relative map path was
dropped and go.build_paths read not_observed. Add Map to the file-valued
linker options so -Map=FILE and -Map FILE are both reported.

* fix(release-exposure): count unread text in undecided map branches

An oversized .map whose shebang names its program with an unresolved
variable, or a package member with an undecided PE header, returned
before counting its unscanned text, so credential markers could read
not_observed. Count any non-bytes read as skipped text in both branches.

* fix(audit): bound map reads and preserve linker paths

* fix(audit): retain unread package uncertainty

* fix(audit): retain ambiguous linker operands

* fix(audit): preserve compiler path separators

* fix(audit): retain distinct linker map occurrences

* fix(audit): apply map declarations to their exact source path

A declaration recorded only its NFC lookup key, so every member or
sibling sharing that key took the declared JavaScript-map route. On a
normalization-sensitive filesystem an unrelated linker map spelled in
another form lost its companion evidence when the declaring script was
scanned first.

Record the resolved spellings each declaration writes and treat only an
exact match as declared. Another spelling in the bucket is read as an
undeclared map; when no declared spelling is reached, its linker-map
guess stays unresolved coverage rather than companion evidence.

* fix(audit): keep partial inventory from settling fuse-host coverage

When a directory read found ASAR layouts but the inventory stopped
early, a separate asar: false build outside those layouts may never
have been listed. Only sampled-then-dropped images counted as a
possible missed host, so reading every found layout's host reported
safe fuses as not_observed for the whole selection.

In limitNativeSample, treat an incomplete inventory as a possible
missed host outside the found layouts unless the read root is itself
a found layout, where host identity already settles coverage.

* fix(audit): apply script targets to their exact source path

A page's script element was recorded only by its NFC lookup key, so on
a normalization-sensitive filesystem a distinct file spelled in another
normalization form inherited the JavaScript role. An unrelated linker
map such as café.map beside a loaded café.map was never classified
and debug companion coverage could settle as not observed.

Keep the resolved spellings each page wrote under the lookup key, as map
declarations already do, and give the script role only to a member or
sibling whose exact path a page loaded.

* fix(audit): keep partial inventory uncertain beside a root ASAR layout

When the read root was itself a found ASAR layout, an incomplete
inventory was trusted to have listed every possible fuse host. A second
asar: false build under a subdirectory names no layout and sits outside
the root layout, so an inventory that stopped after the root host could
miss its launcher and still report the root's safe fuses as
not_observed. The same launcher, once listed, already kept the result
unknown.

Drop the root-layout exemption in limitNativeSample so any incomplete
inventory beside a found layout keeps fuse-host coverage unknown. A
complete inventory that lists only the named host still settles.

* fix(audit): read the linker's --just-symbols file operand

A Go build that forwarded -Wl,--just-symbols=private.syms through
-extldflags or CGO_LDFLAGS kept the relative symbol file in its build
settings, but the forwarded linker matcher knew only the short -R
spelling. Complete metadata then reported go.build_paths as
not_observed while the equivalent -R build was exposed.

Add --just-symbols to the linker options that read a file. Only -R
turns into -rpath when given a directory, so the $ORIGIN ambiguity
check stays on the short spelling.

* fix(audit): anchor expanded package members to the selected path

An inventory-expanded package member reports its location relative to
the selected path, such as app.asar/boot.map, but its lookup identity
resolved that location against the process working directory. An
on-disk page loading app.asar/boot.map, or an absolute file: map
declaration into the archive, resolved under the selected root, so the
declaration never matched the member it named. A script target with an
inline map then settled as a linker map, and a declared map stayed
skipped.

Resolve every member lookup and declaration base against the selected
path, and keep the reported location as written. Linker-map retraction
compares the same anchored spelling.

* fix(audit): read GCC's -I- include barrier as an option

CGO_CFLAGS=-I- is GCC's include barrier, the same as --include-barrier,
not -I with the directory "-". The compiler path matcher read it as a
build path, so a Go binary retaining it reported go.build_paths exposed.
Skip that exact field before path matching.

* fix(audit): keep packaged-image uncertainty after reading the host

A native image stored inside a package is never opened by a fuse reader,
so reading the Electron host on disk does not settle its fuses. Count the
packaged omission toward a partial fuse sample on its own, so safe host
implications stay unknown instead of not_observed while a packaged image
is unread.

* fix(audit): require every named host in a layout to be sampled

An ASAR layout can name more than one host, such as `a/a.exe` beside
`a/electron.exe`. The sample counted the layout as read when any one
named host was kept, so dropping the other still reported the Electron
executable as included and let safe fuses from the sampled images settle
run_as_node as not_observed. Count a layout as read only when every host
it could have was sampled, reusing the named-host selection the fuse
reducer already applies.

* fix(audit): keep a layout-less bundle read from settling partial inventory

A bundle with no ASAR layout, such as an asar: false build, counted its
framework read as covering the Electron host even when inventory stopped
early or the sample dropped an image. A nested build's host could sit in
the part never listed, so the root framework settled RunAsNode as
not_observed. Apply the same incomplete-inventory guard the layout branch
uses to the bundle read.

* fix(audit): read the linker's --sysroot directory operand

A Go ELF build that forwarded -Wl,--sysroot=private-sdk through
-extldflags or CGO_LDFLAGS kept the relative sysroot in its build
settings, but the forwarded linker matcher did not know the option.
Complete metadata then reported go.build_paths as not_observed, while
the compiler-owned --sysroot was already recognized.

Add --sysroot to the linker options that take a path, so the -Wl comma
form, the -Wl = form and both -Xlinker forms are read.

* test(audit): group Deno boundary regressions

* fix(audit): preserve Go linker file operands

* fix(audit): track script completion per source occurrence

* refactor(audit): give Go path parsing one semantic owner

* refactor(audit): preserve map roles at the parsing boundary

* refactor(audit): consume toolchain operands once

commits.subject: fix(native): list ELF initializers of images with COPY relocations (#10084)
commits.body:
fix(native): list ELF initializers of images with COPY relocations (#10084)

* fix(native): list ELF initializers of images with COPY relocations

inspect-native-initializers reported every init_array and fini_array slot
of a non-PIE executable as unresolved, and ordinary PIE executables as
incomplete, when the image carried a COPY relocation such as the one for
stdout.

The shared dynamic relocation reader had no write extent for COPY or TLS
descriptor relocations, so one such record made pointer coverage unknown.
It now sizes a COPY from the image's own dynamic symbol and a TLS
descriptor as two words. COPY sizes are accepted up to the file byte count
in total, so repeated records cannot multiply consumer work.

The section relocation fallback also treated a record whose destination
has no file bytes, as COPY into .bss does, as an unread table. A linked
image's record now affects only the slots it overlaps in memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YT2WLf5G9AnLKF3bZtNLwf

* test(native): cover a COPY relocation against symbol index 0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YT2WLf5G9AnLKF3bZtNLwf

* fix(native): size section COPY records and keep write extents opt-in

Address two review findings on the COPY relocation change.

The shared dynamic relocation reader yields COPY and TLS descriptor
records as writes only to a consumer that asks for whole extents. The
initializer walk asks. IL2CPP and the Android JNI overlay do not, so
both see these kinds as not decoded, exactly as before this branch.
IL2CPP finds unknown bytes by looking one pointer back from a read, so
a wider write of unknown value was read as stored zeros.

The section fallback takes a COPY record's span from the symbol its
table links to instead of assuming one word. A table counts as not
fully read when that size is not established, or when a record of
unknown extent writes memory that has no file bytes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YT2WLf5G9AnLKF3bZtNLwf

* refactor(native): size section COPY records in one helper

Move the symbol lookup, the allowance and the unread-table note out of
the record loop, so the loop only asks for the extent a record is known
to write. Behavior is unchanged.

Cover the allowance across two section records, and keep the new test
code within the lint thresholds the base already meets.

commits.subject: fix(captures): keep escaped JSON strings flat in the capture parser (#10139)
commits.body:
fix(captures): keep escaped JSON strings flat in the capture parser (#10139)

parseCaptureJson retained the strings jsonc-parser 3.3.1 builds fragment by
fragment around each escape, which V8 keeps as ropes several times larger
than their text. Escape-heavy HAR captures therefore exhausted the 192 MiB
decoder heap from about 15 MB, well inside the 32 MiB input budget.

Each string token is now decoded with JSON.parse from its accepted source
span, which yields the same value as one flat string. jsonc-parser reports
malformed strings through onError before the value callback, so JSON.parse
only sees tokens it already accepted. HAR, qlog and Playwright trace
decoding share this parser.

Fixes #10132

* fix(hardening): recognize the __chk_fail FORTIFY handler import

glibc exports __chk_fail as the shared failure handler that most FORTIFY
checks funnel into, and its dynamic import is a positive sign that the
binary uses FORTIFY. The ELF FORTIFY matcher accepted __fortify_fail and
__*_chk names, so an image whose only relevant import was __chk_fail was
reported as fortify: unknown with no evidence location.

format:check fails on the current head because the new fixture call fits on one line at the file's previous width but exceeds oxfmt's 80-column limit with the longer fortifyName literal.
